Whoever sins unto death is rejected; whoever sins venially is polluted.

**A defiled woman, etc.** She who goes after lovers, namely demons, who desire to adulterate the beautiful soul made in the image of God.

**VERSE 17. — A man from his seed.** (Isichius.) These matters concern only the letter, etc., up to “strongly resists through insult.”

**VERSE 18. — If he is blind.** (Isichius.) He is ignorant of the light of contemplation, oppressed by the darkness of the present life; because he does not carefully perceive the light that is to come, he does not know where to direct the steps of his works.

**If he is lame.** (The same.) He sees where he ought to go but, through weakness of mind, cannot do what he desires.

**If he is small, large, or crooked in the nose.** (The same.) He has a small nose who is not capable of maintaining the measure of discernment; for by the nose we distinguish fragrances and foul odors. A large and crooked nose is an immoderate subtlety of discernment which, growing beyond what is proper or fitting, confuses the rectitude of action.

**VERSE 19. — If he has a broken foot.** (Isichius.) He cannot proceed along the way of God and is deprived of good works—not like the lame man, who at least held despite his weakness.

**VERSE 20. — If he is hunchbacked.** (The same.) He is weighed down by earthly concerns and does not look toward heavenly things, looking only at what is below.

**If he is bleary-eyed.** A bleary-eyed person is one whose intellect flashes toward knowledge of the truth, but whose carnal activity obscures it. In bleary eyes the pupils are healthy, but the eyelids become thick because of the discharge; through its frequent flow even the sharpness of the pupil is damaged.

**If he has a white spot.** (The same.) He has a white spot who is prevented from seeing the light of truth because he is blinded by arrogance concerning wisdom or justice. The black pupil sees, whereas the white one does not: when the sense of human thought understands itself to be foolish or sinful, it grasps knowledge of inner brightness; when it attributes to itself the radiance of justice or wisdom, it excludes itself from heavenly knowledge.

**If he has a continual scab.** (The same.) He is one whose fleshly wantonness continually dominates his mind. In a scab, the heat of the inward parts is drawn toward the skin; this signifies lust, because in the same way the temptation of the heart leaps forth into action.

**If he has an ulcerous eruption on his body.** (Gregory, *Pastoral Rule*, part 1, chapter 11.) He has an ulcerous eruption on his body, etc., up to “because through every vice it undermines the soul.” “The root of all evils is greed” (1 Tim. 6).

**Or if he is herniated.** Others have “burdened,” because he does not carry out the shameful act in practice but is still weighed down by continual thought in his mind. He flows toward wantonness with all his thoughts, as though carrying the weight of shame in his heart.

**VERSE 21. — Anyone who has a blemish.** Whoever is subject to any of these vices is prohibited from offering bread to the Lord, lest he be unable to wash away the sins of others while his own sins are still laying him waste.

(Augustine, question 35 on Leviticus.) Every doubt has been removed, etc., up to “on whom it was necessary for incense to be imposed.”

The priest ought to be spotless in mind and conduct. Just as Moses, according to the Septuagint, commanded him to be clean of twelve blemishes, so Paul warned him to preserve twelve qualities, saying: “Not proud, not quick-tempered, not given to wine,” etc. (1 Tim. 2). For he is God’s steward, who ought to surpass his subjects in virtues.

This also takes place in the Church: if someone has been blemished but has ceased through repentance, he is not prohibited from sharing with the holy; but he may not minister, approach the veil, or come to the altar. For the veil and the altar are the body of Christ. Hence Paul says: “We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle have no authority to eat” (Heb. 13). And elsewhere: “Having confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Christ, the new and living way which he inaugurated for us through the veil, that is, his flesh” (Heb. 10).

**And he shall not profane it, etc.** They may scandalize the people by acting disorderly, thinking that the ministry of God, justice, and judgment are superfluous.

[Col. 0360A] **VERSE 24. — Moses spoke, etc.** He commends Moses’ dignity. To others God speaks only a few things, but to him he speaks everything, because he is righteous and is an image of Christ. He also exhorts us to attend to those who are greater and more perfect, who continually enjoy the eternal vision.

## CHAPTER 22

**VERSE 2. — Which they offer, etc.** That is, which they have offered to the priests, to be offered through them to the Lord. Note the kind of sanctification that takes place through the vow and devotion of the one who offers. But whether human beings are said to sanctify themselves in the same way when they vow themselves to some undertaking must be observed.

**VERSE 3. — Every person who approaches, etc.** It is as though he were saying: Let him not merely abstain from the ministry and mystical office, but let him not even touch the things that have been offered; for the clean must approach the clean.

**VERSE 4. — Whoever is a leper, etc.** He does not abominate the visible leper, who suffers unwillingly, but the spiritual one. He explains this where he says: “Whoever touches an unclean thing over a dead person,” or, according to the Septuagint, “every uncleanness of the soul,” that is, sin.

**From whom, etc.** (Jerome, Letter to Fabiola.) If one of the priests has a seminal discharge, etc., up to “let him be bound by the custom of no other person.”

**VERSE 9. — They shall keep, etc.** For those who keep the Lord’s commandments, they are the cause of justification and salvation; but for those who transgress them, they are the cause of sin and death, especially in the reception of holy things. “Whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment upon himself,” etc. (1 Cor. 11).

**VERSE 10. — A tenant of a priest, etc.** (Isichius.) One who does not live purely and diligently in the Church, as though he were merely passing through it for the sake of glory or profit, is remembered as a hired man. “He is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own” (John 10).

**VERSE 12. — Married to anyone from the people.** (The same.) It is not enough to be nourished in the faith of Christ; we must remain and grow in it. Nor must we mingle with any foreigner—that is, with doctrine, law, or action alien to God. Nor, because we descend from faithful fathers, should we presume upon holy things; rather, we must ourselves remain faithful wherever we are.

**VERSE 14. — Whoever eats from the holy things, etc.** (Isichius.) The Holy of Holies, etc., up to “hence Solomon says: ‘When you sit to eat with a ruler, carefully attend to what is set before you’” (Prov. 23).

**He shall add a fifth, etc.** The Septuagint has: “Upon it.” Therefore the fifth is commanded to be added not from elsewhere but from it and with it, or upon it. This is the word proclaimed by Christ himself concerning the Lord’s mystery. He removes us from ignorance and prevents anyone from thinking that it is carnal or earthly. It is rightly called a fifth because the spirit and word that he gives arrange our five senses. It brings not only taste to the mystery but also hearing, sight, touch, and smell, so that we suspect nothing earthly in the things that are heavenly.

**And he shall give it to the priest for the sanctuary.** (Isichius.) The sanctification of the mystical sacrifice and the true transfer from sensible things to intelligible things must be given to the priest, because through his virtue and word the things that are seen have been sanctified, so that all may surpass the senses.

**VERSE 15. — Of the children of Israel.** He signifies the faithful people, who through this mystery see God. Whatever anyone consecrates to God for the Lord’s sacrifice is most holy, because Christ’s body is made from such offerings. For he himself is the firstfruits of our dough; therefore it rightly subsists from our firstfruits.

**VERSE 17. — The Lord spoke, etc.** (Isichius.) Not only priests, etc., up to “otherwise it will not be received.”

**VERSE 18. — A man from the house of Israel, etc.** Even literally, if you offer a bull, sheep, goat, or anything of this sort—giving firstfruits to the priests, feeding the poor, establishing divine buildings, or doing anything that pertains to God himself, which is why it is called a whole burnt offering—this offering must be undefiled. Yet he does not name the pollution, so that we may understand the spiritual pollution that comes from robbery, injustice, greed, and similar things.

**VERSE 21. — A person who offers, etc.** He commanded that the people’s offering be clean; he adds what sort of ministers ought to be and to offer.

**Of peace offerings, etc.** Things that are effective for salvation and peace. Even if someone cannot practice philosophy perfectly, like the one who has abandoned everything, who devotes himself to virginity and similar pursuits, nevertheless there are degrees: “Star differs from star in glory” (1 Cor. 15).

**VERSE 22. — If it is blind, etc.** One who is ignorant of God and of his ministry, and cannot explain it to others; hence he acts negligently toward himself, toward others, and toward the ministry. Hence: “See, they all lack knowledge; they are all mute dogs, unable to bark” (Isa. 56).

**If it is broken.** In foot or hand. One whose action or will is weak or distorted is not worthy of salvation or of the sacred altars.

**If it has a scar.** He indicates a slanderer; for such a person is morally most wicked, and a very harsh wound is not easily softened.

**If it has eruptions.** The Septuagint has: “a cut tongue.” This is one who, because of a filthy life, has lost the confidence to teach. Hence David: “To the sinner God said: Why do you recount my ordinances?” etc. (Ps. 49).

**A scab or an ulcerous eruption.** The fornicator is signified, one who stains his body. “Whoever commits fornication sins against his own body” (1 Cor. 6).

**You shall not offer these to the Lord.** The Septuagint has: “They shall not offer these to the Lord.” Such people must not be offered for service at the altar. He does not add “the sacrifice of peace offerings,” as above, so that we may understand this to be said concerning ministers of the altar, who ought to be a whole burnt offering and to lead a perfect and complete life.

**With the ears and tail cut off, etc.** The ear is cut off in one who is disobedient, who delights in shameful words and rejects good things.

**Voluntarily, etc.** Such a person either carries out commandments and is called a bull, or is simple and is called a sheep. Therefore we do not wholly oppose him or count him among the enemy; rather, we teach and exhort him.

[Col. 0362A] **Or bruised, etc.** One who yields to the temptations brought against him and loses the strength of his soul. We ought not to suffer these things or yield to the enemy who afflicts us. Hence: “Why do I go about sadly while the enemy afflicts me?” (Ps. 41).

**And after the parts have been removed.** One who by a single evil action, as though with a knife, cuts himself off from union with God, deprived of the offspring of virtue and of the signs of manliness. Another person is gradually crushed.

**VERSE 27. — A bull, a sheep, and a goat.** (Isichius.) Nature is the mother of all things, etc., up to “hence Solomon says: ‘Before death, praise no one’” (Sir. 11).

**VERSE 28. — They shall not be sacrificed.** (Isichius.) This signifies the legal Passover, because Moses handed these things down to the Jews to be sacrificed on the day of Passover, saying: “You shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God: sheep,” etc. (Deut. 16). Those who have received the true Passover cannot celebrate this Passover.

**On one day, etc.** (The same.) Because the old Passover had its appointed time, etc., up to: “On the following day they crucified Christ.”

## CHAPTER 23

**VERSE 1. — These are the feasts of the Lord.** (Isichius.) If you examine the present things carefully, etc., up to “he rests on the intelligible Sabbath.”

**VERSE 4. — These, therefore, are, etc.** They are not “for the Lord,” as all the others are, but properly “of the Lord,” by which, after conquering the enemy, he saved the human race and brought it back from captivity (Exod. 2).

**VERSE 5. — On the fourteenth day, etc.** (Isichius.) Let us question the Jews, etc., up to “on which Christ our Passover was sacrificed,” etc.

[Col. 0362C] **It is the Lord’s Passover.** Because the Lord suffered, he did not immediately bring the times to an end but left the remnants of the final and evening hour, so that their sound—namely, that of the apostles—might go out into all the earth (Ps. 18), and their words to the ends of the world. In the evening also, or in the middle of the evening, anticipating his cross, he celebrated his own Passover, because he handed the mystical, true Passover to the disciples. It was already night when Judas, having received the morsel, went out to betray him; on the following day he completed the Passover. Hence the legislator established this feast on the fifteenth day and proclaimed the solemnity of unleavened bread.

**VERSE 6. — For seven days, etc.** If we truly wish to celebrate Passover, for seven days—that is, always—we must be unleavened from every kind of wickedness, and especially from Jewish error. Hence the Apostle says: “Not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth” (1 Cor. 5).

### Verse 7

**“Every work,” etc.** “Whoever commits sin is a slave of sin” (John 8). We must not serve sin when we celebrate Passover, in which Christ freed us from sin.

**“Servile,” etc.** He does not permit servile tasks to be performed, as on the other days from which he prohibited us; hence he adds: “But you shall offer a sacrifice by fire to the Lord.”

### Verse 8

**“A sacrifice,” etc.** The Septuagint has *holocausts*, indicating that he commands abstention from all servile tasks. Moreover, he named not only the first day but also the seventh, so as to encompass the whole of human life [Col. 0363A], because this is its beginning and that its end, in which everything can be included.

### Verse 11

**“On the following day.”** He could have said “on the second day of Unleavened Bread”; but, so that he would not direct our attention to the following day—namely, the day after the first—he said “on the other day,” signifying the resurrection that followed the Passion, just as one day follows another.

### Verse 12

**“And on that same day.”** The day of the Resurrection, that is, of the elevation of the sheaf. When we celebrate the Resurrection, we must not forget the Lord’s sacrifice, from which the sheaf was offered.

### Verse 13

**“Two-tenths.”** Perfect humanity and perfect divinity must come together as one. This occurs “in oil,” that is, through the mercy that he showed toward us. For the sacrifice is found to be a pleasing odor to the Lord if we understand in him those things that are worthy of him [Col. 0363B].

**“And libations.”** Behold the intelligible offering of Melchizedek, which is accomplished in bread and wine (Genesis 14). Hence one quarter is offered, so that the evangelical teaching may be signified by the fourth part; by the libation, however, the Lord’s saying is signified: “This is my blood, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins” (Matthew 26).

### Verse 14

**“Bread.”** The offering of the present gifts, which is the mystery of Christ, reconciled us to God and prepared a new food.

**“Parched grain.”** The Septuagint has *χίδρα νέα* (*chidra nea*), that is, “you shall not eat new grain, roasted,” or “crushed and cleansed by hand.” Thus others interpret *chidra*, because Christ’s commandments seek action and correction (Matthew 11) [Col. 0363C].

### Verse 16

**“Fifty days, and so forth.”** This is the Lord’s Day, on which we celebrate the feast of Pentecost. The Jews celebrate it neither according to the letter nor according to the spirit, since they do not even count the days according to the Law.

**“You shall offer a new sacrifice.”** A new one, not an old one, not a worldly one. For the Spirit’s coming renewed the whole of human life, because it confirmed Christ’s institution and perfected in them the confirmation of life. Hence: “He will take from what is mine and declare it to you” (John 16). Therefore he did not come on another day, but on the day of the Resurrection and of the offering of the intelligible sheaf, to show that the new way of life was perfected through Christ’s Resurrection and the coming of the Holy Spirit [Col. 0363D].

### Verse 17

**“In your dwellings,” etc.** For there is a principal dwelling, of which it is said: “Blessed are those who dwell in your house, O Lord” (Psalm 82). And elsewhere: “One thing I asked of the Lord; this I shall seek: that I may dwell,” etc. (Psalm 26).

**“Loaves of firstfruits.”** The Lord was the first to perfect and teach the Gospel together with the Law. “You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘You shall not kill’; but I say to you: Everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment” (Matthew 5). For here he joined the Law to the Gospel. Hence Luke says: “All that Jesus began to do and to teach,” etc. (Acts 1).

**“From two-tenths,” etc.** That is, from the teaching that teaches perfect divinity and perfect humanity; nor can they be cooked otherwise than through such teaching [Col. 0364A].

### Verse 18

**“Seven lambs.”** For the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, which he calls lambs because the Holy Spirit is one with Christ, of whom it is written: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world.” Therefore no one can say “Lord Jesus” except in the Holy Spirit (John 1; 1 Corinthians 12).

**“And two rams.”** By these the enemy is winnowed. These are the higher commandments and virtues, which are followed by the others as by sheep; for example: “Go, sell everything you have, and give to the poor” (Matthew 19).

**“With libations,” etc.** These are knowledge and correction; hence: “But thanks be to God, who manifests the fragrance of his knowledge through us, because we are the good odor of Christ,” etc. (2 Corinthians 2) [Col. 0364B].

### Verse 19

**“And two lambs,” etc.** The commandments of peace and holiness; hence: “Pursue peace with all and holiness,” etc. (Hebrews 12). Because these things were spoken in apostolic language, he commands that they be offered with the loaves of firstfruits, which signify Christ’s teaching. Hence below: “And when the priest has lifted them up with the loaves of firstfruits” (John 10).

### Verse 20

**“They shall be for the use,” etc.** For the use of that priest, namely Christ, who is our priest and our Lord. The loaves of firstfruits and the lambs of the commandments belong to him. He himself was speaking in Paul; he himself offered everything that has been said. He was the first to announce peace to the disciples, and he preserved holiness, like the Holy of Holies [Col. 0364C].

### Verse 21

**“Most solemn.”** In this feast the calling of the nations was not merely foretold but fulfilled, when Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and the other nations heard the apostles speaking in various tongues of the mighty works of God (Acts 2).

### Verse 22

**“Afterward,” etc.** He seems to have said the same thing above, but there he said: “You shall not complete your harvest”; here, however, he says: “You shall not cut it down to the ground.” The change of wording itself indicates a distinction.

**“The harvest of the land,” etc.** The way of life, whose harvest comes after Christ’s Resurrection and the coming of the Holy Spirit. Yet the word of preaching does not hand on all the knowledge that we shall possess in the future. For there are things that cannot now be revealed to us (Matthew 8); hence he inserted this law among the festivals mentioned above [Col. 0364D].

**“For the poor and the strangers.”** The Septuagint has “for the poor and the proselyte,” that is, for Christ, who had nowhere to lay his head, who came to his own and his own did not receive him. Here he understands only those who remain. Hence: “O the depth of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments and unsearchable his ways!” (Romans 11).

### Verse 24

**“In the seventh month, on the first day of the month.”** The number seven signifies completion, whether particular or general. Hence God rested on the seventh day (Genesis 2), and by his rest signified ours. Thus: “Whoever has entered that rest has also rested from his works, just as God did from his own” (Hebrews 4). The beginning of the completion of the ages, however, is the Lord’s coming; hence: “Little children, it is the last hour” (1 John 2). He calls this time “the first day of the seventh month,” just as the beginning of completion is also rest for us, whom he has caused to cease from evil works and freed from a heavy yoke. Hence: “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened,” etc., and “learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls” (Matthew 11).

**“With the sounding of trumpets.”** For it proclaims the Savior’s Resurrection, which is a memorial of the general resurrection. According to the Apostle, that resurrection will occur “at the voice of the archangel and at the trumpet of God,” etc.

### Verse 25

**“You shall perform no servile work in it.”** It is as though he were saying: It is no task to perform servile works. You did so before, but, just as you presented your members to iniquity for iniquity, now present them to serve righteousness for sanctification (Romans 6). For this is the true whole burnt offering [Col. 0365B].

### Verse 27

**“On the tenth day,” etc.** (Hesychius.) From this we understand that propitiation and liberation from sins are acquired through humility and affliction of soul. We ought to undertake this from evening—that is, to begin with repentance, which Christ made the beginning of his preaching (Matthew 4). A good life perfected in virtues must be built upon repentance. Hence he added: “And you shall offer a whole burnt offering to the Lord.”

### Verse 28

**“The day of propitiation.”** (Hesychius.) It signifies two things: for at this time we shall receive propitiation, and therefore on that day we must abstain from every evil [Col. 0365C].

### Verse 31

**“Nothing, therefore.”** He signifies that we must always cease from evils and superfluities. Hence the Lord neither permits us to plead our case nor to consider what we shall eat, drink, or wear; rather, he proclaimed the true Sabbath, the Sabbath of Sabbaths.

### Verse 32

**“You shall afflict.”** This is a recapitulation of humility, which is the foundation and basis of the virtues. Hence the Lord says: “Whoever humbles himself like this child is greater in the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 18).

### Verse 34

**“On the fifteenth day.”** (Hesychius.) This number marks the beginning of the feast, etc., through “the building not made by hands is held in the heavens” (2 Corinthians 5).

### Verse 36

**“Also the day.”** (Idem.) Note that he speaks similarly of the first and the eighth day, because the day of the Resurrection is the second day and the beginning of the age to come. The first day, in Christ, is the beginning of the way of life and the origin of future things; the eighth follows the present age, which is signified by the number seven. Moreover, the saints possess rest and the future life in this life. Hence it was said to the apostles: “The kingdom of God is within you,” etc.

**“Assembly.”** The Septuagint has “departure,” because here there is departure, while there is habitation there. Hence: “I desire to depart and to be with Christ” (Philippians 1).

### Verse 37

**“These are the feasts of the Lord,” etc.** (Idem.) Paul agrees with the Lawgiver, etc., through “whether in dangers or voluntarily we make our promises.”

### Verse 39

**“From the fifteenth,” etc.** The fifteenth, composed of seven and eight, signifies evangelical preaching, which consists of the present life and the future life: it brings the former to completion and prepares the latter [Col. 0366A].

**“On the first day and on the eighth day.”** (Idem.) The one that is the eighth, etc., through “because rest is reserved in the future for the faithful who fulfill the Law.”

### Verse 40

**“On the first day, fruit.”** (Idem.) Christ is the fruit, etc., through “at its proper time.”

**“And branches of palms,” etc.** The shoots of the youthful growth of righteousness, because “the righteous will flourish like a palm tree.” But because nothing is rejected from the palm tree, nor from those who live righteously, he adds “branches of leafy trees.”

**“And branches of a leafy tree.”** All the fruits of the virtues, but especially mercy, which ought to be continual and lasting. Hence: “Your oil shall not fail from your head” (Ecclesiastes 9).

**“From the torrent,” etc.** From the present life, which flows like a torrent, boiling with temptations and tribulations. Hence: “He will drink from the torrent on the way; therefore he will lift up his head” (Psalm 109)—that is, hanging on the cross [Col. 0366B].

## Chapter 24

### Verse 2

**“Command the children of Israel.”** (Hesychius.) The lampstand is the evangelical life, etc., through “where the merciful hide their treasures.”

### Verse 3

**“Until morning.”** Of the future age. For then there will be no time for praying or giving alms. Hence: “Do not say to your friend, ‘Go and return, and tomorrow I will give you’; for you do not know what the coming day will bring” (Proverbs 3, 27).

### Verse 4

**“Upon the lampstand,” etc.** Christ, who is the true light and enlightens every person who comes into the world. “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth,” etc. (Isaiah 53). Upon him burns the lamp, that is, the Holy Spirit, who appeared over the disciples in tongues of fire. To him we ought to offer the purest oil, that is, a clean life, knowing that not everyone can kindle that fire, but only Christ and his children. Filled with the Spirit, he says: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me” (Isaiah 61). He also says: “I have come to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I desire except that it be kindled?” (Luke 12). Breathing upon this fire, as though kindling it, he says: “Receive the Holy Spirit,” etc. (John 20). This lamp, however, is kindled only through a clean life and conduct; otherwise, once kindled, it is quickly extinguished. Hence: “Do not extinguish the Spirit,” etc. (1 Thessalonians 5) [Col. 0366D].

### Verse 5

**“You shall also take.”** (Bede, *On the Tabernacle*, book 1, chapter 7, volume 2.) The twelve loaves on the table of the tabernacle, etc., through “so that through the labors and good works of temporal life we may hasten toward it.”

**“You shall bake twelve from it.”** (Origen, *Homily 13 on Exodus*.) The word of the Lord is bread, but it is manifold, etc., through “bread is placed upon a clean table, namely, upon a holy and pure mind” [Col. 0366D].

### Verse 10

**“But behold,” etc.** (Hesychius.) A woman among the Israelites, etc., through “who is blasphemed in Christ.”

**“But behold.”** (Origen, *Homily 14 on Leviticus*.) Two are quarreling: one is wholly an Israelite, etc., through “for sometimes the one who is cast outside is within, and the one who is outside appears to be retained within.”

### Verse 12

**“And they placed him,” etc.** Moses does not pronounce a sentence against the blasphemer on his own authority; rather, reserving the matter for God’s command, he sends him to prison. For the Law hates the one who blasphemes, against whom it frequently proclaims the Trinity, though not openly as the Gospel does. Therefore it reserved him for the judgment of the Gospel: “Whoever has not believed in the Son has already been judged” (John 3:18), and the like [Col. 0367A].

### Verse 15

**“The man who,” etc.** This is a manner of expression, as though it said: “That man or that man,” that is, any man. It is not said, as some think, “man man” in a praiseworthy sense, as “a true man.” Rather, “man man” means anyone whatsoever, even one resembling an animal. Yet the one meant is truly a man. That this interpretation is not correct, but that this is a scriptural idiom, is clearly shown here, since the one being condemned—not the one being praised—is described in this way [Col. 0367B].

**“A man,” etc.** (Augustine, *Questions on Leviticus*, question 87.) “If he curses his God, he shall bear his sin. But whoever names the name of the Lord shall be put to death,” as though cursing his God were one thing, etc., through “this kind of expression should be noted.”

**(Hesychius.)** The Septuagint has: “Man, man,” etc., through “just as the Israelite’s son named and blasphemed” (Joshua 7).

### Verse 17

**“Whoever strikes and kills a man.”** The Septuagint has: “Whoever strikes the soul of a man,” etc., that is, whoever draws him into iniquity. By “soul,” he understands the animal man, who does not perceive the things of God’s Spirit [Col. 0367C].

**(Augustine, question 88 on Leviticus.)** “Whoever strikes the soul of a man and it dies,” etc. He does not say, etc., through “for this is what it means for the soul of a man to be struck.”

### Verse 20

**“Fracture,” etc.** The Septuagint has: “Crushing for crushing,” that is, if by teaching, persuading, or causing scandal he has crushed some virtue of his neighbor.

**“Tooth for tooth.”** The virtue of speech. For teeth are understood as words. Hence: “The teeth of the sons of men are their weapons and arrows,” etc. (Psalm 59). And: “His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk” (Genesis 49). For the words of the Gospel are clearer and more evident than the milk of the Law.

### Verse 21

**“Whoever strikes,” etc.** According to the letter, these rules were necessary for the Jews, who could not understand: “If someone strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also” (Matthew 5). But since they were malicious, they wanted to inflict evil and not endure it. Therefore they had to be restrained from crime by fear of reciprocal punishment [Col. 0367D].

### Verse 23

**“And they led him out,” etc.** He shows by the event itself that the Law was confirmed, so that you would fear blaspheming and flee from sin, since not only the ruler but the whole multitude punishes it. For all together ought to punish blasphemers, who were not afraid to slander the author of all things and to separate everyone from him.

## Chapter 25

### Verses 1–2

**“And the Lord spoke,” etc.** “When they had entered,” etc. (Hesychius.) The land is the good way of life, of which it is said: “Your good Spirit will lead me into a level land,” etc. (Psalm 142) [Col. 0368A].

### Verse 3

**“For six years,” etc.** While we are in this life and in the visible creation, which is signified by the number six. For everything visible was created in six days. “But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath for the land of the Lord.” When the Sabbath comes after the present age, of which Paul says, “A sabbath rest remains for the people of God,” signified by the seventh day on which God rested from all his works, namely, the visible works (Hebrews 4), there will no longer be a time for working.

**“You shall sow your field,” etc.** Through the field and the vineyard—when he forbade the one to be sown and the other to be pruned—every kind of cultivated land is to be understood. For nothing is to be done in an olive grove or in land of any other kind [Col. 0368B].

### Verse 5

**“What grows of its own accord,” etc.** We shall eat in the future the fruit of those things that we do here. Hence: “You shall eat the labor of your hands; blessed are you, and it shall be well with you” (Psalm 127).

### Verse 6

**“But they shall be,” etc.** He does not forbid the owner from feeding on what grows spontaneously, but from storing it up for personal use.

### Verse 8

**“You shall also count.”** Let us ask the Jews: if the Lawgiver honored the seventh day, as they say, and commanded abstention from work, why did he command the fiftieth year to be celebrated? For seven weeks of years make forty-nine years. It would not therefore have been necessary to abstain in the fiftieth year, unless the Law signified a mystery that the weakness of the Jews could not grasp [Col. 0368C]. For God signifies a twofold completion of all visible things: one particular to each individual thing, and another common to all things, when there will no longer be a time for working. In the earlier passage he intimated the first; here he indicates the second.

**“Seven.”** The human age is divided into a week of days. Therefore, when this number has been multiplied by itself, the entire completed age of the world has run its course and time has reached its end. The fiftieth then follows, as though after the forty-ninth year, in which the resurrection will occur. Hence he adds: “And sounding the trumpet in the seventh month,” etc. Therefore the Apostle says: “At the trumpet of God they will descend from heaven, and the dead who are in Christ will rise incorruptible” (1 Thessalonians 4). The trumpet must precede the one who raises the dead; therefore he commanded the trumpet to sound in the forty-ninth year, in which the universal completion occurs [Col. 0368D].

### Verse 9

**“In the seventh month.”** Because Christ came, as it were, in the seventh month of the world’s age: the first month was in paradise; the second lasted until the Flood; the third until Abraham; the fourth until the descent into Egypt; the fifth until the transmigration; the sixth until Christ’s coming; the seventh is the coming itself.

### Verse 10

**“And you shall sanctify the year.”** As though it were to be awaited and contemplated in holiness. For we must pursue peace and holiness (Hebrews 12), without which no one will see God.

**“Each one.”** There is a certain hospitable family of patriarchs and prophets, headed by Abraham. There is another of chastity, headed by Joseph. There is another of gentleness, headed by Moses (Genesis 18, 39; Numbers 12) [Col. 0369A].

### Verse 14

**“When you sell,” etc.** Anyone may sell or buy. Hence Paul says: “We are yours, just as you are ours” (1 Corinthians 3). According to the letter, this morally instructs us to show compassion toward our neighbors in contracts, so that no one may exploit the needs of the poor in business, nor strive to acquire the possessions of others, but may lend to those in need and gradually recover what was lent from the produce of the fields.

**“According to the number.”** (Hesychius.) That is, according to each person’s virtue. For the years signify the age in which it becomes manifest what each person is capable of according to the body [Col. 0369B].

### Verse 16

**“The more numerous,”** (Idem.) That is, if he is able to work much, he will demand much fruit; if he cannot do much, he will repay little. For one will bear fruit thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold (Matthew 13).

### Verse 18

**“Do the commandments.”** So that no one, after hearing about the moderation of buying and selling, might become more sluggish, and so that this condescension itself might do harm, he carefully adds: “Do the commandments,” etc. For he does not wish anyone to be idle, but to bear fruit according to his virtue. Conscience also examines each person’s virtue.

**“And the judgments,” etc.** (Idem.) Not corrupting their intention or their performance. For example, if someone gives alms, he should not harm one person in order to benefit another. The commandment that ordered almsgiving intended it to be just [Col. 0369C].

**“But if you say,” etc.** (Idem.) Since he had commanded the land to lie fallow for two years, lest they be disturbed by anxiety about what they would eat or drink, he says: “I will give my blessing,” etc. (Matthew 6). It should be noted that while Christ says, “Do not worry about tomorrow,” the Law commands them not to worry about three years.

### Verse 21

**“I will give my blessing.”** (Idem.) Christ. Hence: “We have blessed you in the name of the Lord,” that is, in Christ, who is the name of the Father. He named and manifested the Father to us. He came in the sixth year, that is, in perfection, which is signified by the number six, and in order to restore the human being whom he had formed on the sixth day. What is called the sixth day there is called the sixth year here, because much time elapsed between our formation and our reformation [Col. 0369D].

### Verse 23

**“And the land,” etc.** (Augustine, *Questions on Leviticus*, question 90.) Some manuscripts have, etc., through “whoever possesses something ought to use it.”

### Verse 25

**“If he has become impoverished.”** (Hesychius.) What our substance is, etc., through “he teaches how he should restore it.”

**“He is able to redeem.”** (Hesychius.) According to that passage, etc., through “so that it may in some way be common.”

### Verse 28

**“Until the year.”** The year, because it contains all hours, days, months, and every cycle, signifies perfection. Completed and lasting sin is corrected only by perfect repentance, in which fasting, prayer, sackcloth, almsgiving, and tears are practiced. Through these full remission is acquired [Col. 0370A].

### Verse 29

**“Whoever sells a house.”** (Idem.) The seller is not specified, nor is he called a neighbor or kinsman. For it is not one person but the whole people; nor is it a matter of the kindred of the Jews, but of Sodom and Gomorrah.

**“Whoever sells a house,” etc.** In the preceding chapter he explained the spiritual way of life of each individual; here he intends to treat generally of the synagogue or the Church, because the Church of the nations receives freedom, whereas the synagogue serves forever, except for the Levites—that is, the apostles and those who adhere to them.

**(Origen, *Homily 15 on Leviticus*.)** “Whoever sells a house,” etc. It is written concerning Jacob, etc., through “they always receive repentance and are always redeemed” [Col. 0370B].

### Verse 31

**“By the law of fields.”** (Hesychius.) Because in the Gospel they are neighbors, not to the Law. Therefore they can always be redeemed, and from Christ’s coming until the second coming they are redeemed in parts.

**The Septuagint:** “They shall be reckoned as the field of the land,” concerning which it is said: “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field,” that is, in the Gospel, in which the mystery of Christ is the treasure.

### Verse 32

**“The houses of the Levites.”** (Origen, *Homily 15 on Leviticus*.) If it is the house of a priest or Levite, etc., through “namely, the satisfaction of desire.”

### Verse 34

**“The pasturelands.”** (Hesychius.) Other fields, that is, ways of life of the virtues and teachings. These are separated from their cities, which are established and saved through them [Col. 0370C], and they are not sold, because they are received freely and given freely.

### Verse 35

**“If he has become impoverished.”** (Idem.) Admire the wisdom and piety of the Lawgiver: for in humble matters he explains lofty things, while according to the letter he gives a rule of piety.

**“Who brought you out.”** As though he were saying: Just as I freed you from the dominion of the Egyptians and, after casting out the sinners, led you into the land of the Canaanites that had already been promised, so I do not wish you to remain under the dominion of sinners or to embrace the company of sinners. Rather, when they wish to repent, you are to support them both by living with them and by sharing your resources.

### Verse 39

**“Through poverty.”** The letter is full of piety, but the spiritual understanding is fuller [Col. 0370D].

### Verse 40

**“But as a hired servant.”** Both are subject, but this one is nevertheless free. Thus the person who has been converted through you is indeed subject, but by the dignity of divine grace he is a brother.

### Verse 43

**“You shall not afflict,” etc.** Because “in the judgment with which you judge, you will be judged,” and “with the measure with which you measure, it will be measured back to you” (Matthew 7).

### Verse 44

**“Male slave and female slave.”** (Hesychius.) He shows the difference between those whom we save for God from among unbelievers and those who are already believers and like us, but who, in the dignity of their calling and conduct, have been weakened for a time in virtue and whom we correct. The latter work among us until the jubilee; the former are perpetual slaves.

### Verse 45

**“Those who are from these.”** (Hesychius.) The heretics related to the Jews, who proclaim the same mysteries with us, as though they were in our land, but do not believe rightly and perfectly.

**“You shall have these.”** (Idem.) Those whom we convert from the nations, from the Jews, or from the heretics, we acquire as male and female slaves forever, because we spend the money of teaching on them and may hand them over to our sons—that is, to disciples—to be taught, just as Paul entrusted the Cretans to Titus and the Ephesians to Timothy for instruction [Col. 0371A].

### Verse 46

**“But brothers.”** As though those whom you converted from the ungodly and those whom you restored after their fall would not have the same status among you.

### Verse 47

**“If he has grown strong.”** (Idem.) That is, if a foreigner, Jew, or heretic who has recently joined your faith has become distinguished in virtues, so that he can rebuke and exhort [Col. 0371B].

**“If he has grown strong,” etc.** According to the letter, he shows how greatly he loves freedom. For this reason he does not permit an Israelite to serve foreigners, but commands that he be redeemed.

**“Whoever wishes.”** It is shameful for a person nourished in the faith from childhood to submit to the teaching of such men who have suddenly become teachers. Hence Jerome: “Yesterday in the marketplace, today at the altar; yesterday a companion of actors, today a consecrator of virgins.”

### Verse 49

**“An uncle,” etc.** (Idem.) Uncles’ sons are those who have begotten us in the faith; their brothers are similar preachers; the sons of their brothers are disciples of similar men.

**“A blood relative.”** (Idem.) One who is more distant than an uncle or cousin but closer than a relative by marriage. For whoever does not care for his own, especially those of his household, has denied the faith (1 Timothy 5) [Col. 0371C].

**“A relative by marriage.”** (Idem.) In the kinship of the faith of Christ’s incarnation, since we are from his flesh and bones.

**“But if.”** (Idem.) The Holy Spirit acts for the sake of our freedom and glory, and commands that every slave of sin be redeemed through virtues.

**“And he himself.”** (Idem.) He who became poor through sin, although previously rich in virtue and teaching, rightly frees himself when by exhorting and advising he recalls himself to virtue.

### Verse 50

**“Having calculated.”** (Idem.) That is, considering within himself by what virtue, etc., through “therefore the Lord said to him: ‘Today salvation has come to this house.’” [Col. 0371D]

### Verse 51

**“He shall repay.”** (Idem.) According to the things by which he sinned, he ought to repay the price. What gluttony has committed, fasting should correct; what talkativeness has done, silence should erase; and similarly, opposites are healed by opposites.

## Chapter 26

### Verse 1

**“You shall not make.”** He prohibits the worship of idols, both visible and invisible.

**“A carved image.”** (Hesychius.) Wishing to carve some memorial of yourselves in the buildings of houses and the possessions of fields.

**“Nor an engraved figure.”** (Idem.) A heap of gold, silver, or precious stones, by which the avaricious are deceived, just as the nations are deceived by idols.

### Verse 2

**“Keep.”** (Hesychius.) By abstaining from every evil and devoting yourselves to every good; for this is the true Sabbath [Col. 0372A].

### Verse 3

**“If you walk in my commandments.”** He first stated what ought to be done and what avoided. At the end he enumerates the rewards due to those who observe them and the punishments due to transgressors.

**“If you walk in my commandments.”** (Idem.) These things cannot stand according to the letter, etc., through “which are signified in this chapter.”

**(Origen, *Homily 16 on Leviticus*.)** If the Law is carnal, etc., through “John came in the spirit and power of Elijah.”

**“My commandments.”** Such as this one: “Whoever does not keep the Sabbath shall be stoned by the whole assembly,” and the like.

**“I will give you rains,” etc.** “I will give” is superfluous according to our customary manner of speaking, but it has been added according to the manner of the Scriptures.

**“At their seasons.”** (Origen.) At an opportune time: to one not drunk or occupied with other matters. Therefore the teacher should wisely determine to whom he should give rain, to whom a measure of wheat, and to whom he ought to give milk rather than food [Col. 0372B].

### Verse 4

**“The land shall produce.”** The Septuagint has: “The trees of the field shall give their fruit.” (Idem.) The movements of the soul, which are higher than the movements of the earth, that is, of our flesh; their fruits are love, righteousness, gentleness, and the like.

**“The trees shall produce fruit.”** (Origen.) A tree cannot, etc., through “of which it is said: ‘It is a tree of life to those who grasp it.’”

### Verse 5

**“Threshing shall overtake the harvest.”** (Origen.) The soul that germinates from the word of God, etc., through “so that it may remain to be distributed with fellow servants at the proper time” [Col. 0372C].

**“Shall overtake.”** For bread strengthens the human heart, and wine gladdens it (Psalm 103). The things said about self-restraint, observances, and keeping the commandments appear to be grain, from which bread is made and hearts are strengthened. Those things, however, that pertain to knowledge and gladden the mind through the investigation of hidden matters are compared with wine and the vintage. The heart rejoices when obscure things [hidden things] are explained.

**“The vintage.”** The fruit of the soul. For the vintage is a tree. To possess both together—that is, to bear fruit in body and soul—is a great blessing.

**(Hesychius.)** For as the soul gathers its virtues, it immediately desires others. Hence: “Forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead” (Philippians 3).

**“The vintage.”** (Origen.) As though we were saying, etc., through “so that from the Spirit we may reap eternal life” [Col. 0372D].

**“Your bread.”** Namely, the bread that descended from heaven and gives life to the world, not the bread that abounds more in evils than in goods.

**“Without fear.”** If the body is stable and the soul bears fruit, we shall be secure in our land, because the flesh will not desire against the spirit (Galatians 5).

### Verse 6

**“And the sword shall not.”** (Hesychius.) For there will be peace within your borders; now wars and quarrels arise from desires.

### Verse 7

**“Your enemies.”** (Idem.) They have been killed by fasting, prayer, and similar practices. Hence: “This kind cannot be driven out except by prayer and fasting” (Matthew 17).

**“They shall fall.”** The Septuagint has: “In your presence, by your death”—that is, when you have put to death your members that are upon the earth, namely, fornication, impurity, and the like (Colossians 3) [Col. 0373A].

### Verse 8

**“They shall pursue.”** (Origen.) Just as the number five indicates the wise and the foolish, etc., through “so that they may not deceive believers.”

**(Hesychius.)** The Septuagint, etc., through “he can pursue and conquer.”

**“And a hundred.”** Those who possess not only subtle knowledge but also a perfect life, who are spiritually multiplied tenfold; therefore they are called a hundred, namely, those who produce a hundredfold fruit.

### Verse 9

**“I will look upon you.”** His regard is salvation. “The Lord looked upon Peter, and he wept bitterly.” If the sun does not look upon the crop, it remains fruitless. God looks upon the crop of our heart and illuminates, increases, and multiplies us with the rays of his word, so that we may become great, just as Isaac became great, and Moses great, and John great [Col. 0373B].

**“To grow.”** In good works, so that small things become great. Hence: “Whatever you did for one of the least of mine,” etc. (Matthew 25).

**“You shall be multiplied.”** So that few things may become great or many things may result. Hence: “If there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this saying: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself’” (Romans 13).

### Verse 10

**“You shall eat.”** (Origen.) The old Law and the prophets, etc., through “and we have put on the new.”

### Verse 11

**“I will set.”** If we possess the things mentioned above, having cast off the old man, our heart has been renewed: “God has come to us and dwells in us” (Colossians 3).

**“He will not reject,” etc.** (Origen.) I dare to say that Christ is the soul of God, just as the Word of God is the wisdom of God and the power of God (1 Corinthians 1). It is therefore as though he were saying: “My Son will not reject you” [Col. 0373C].

**“Soul.”** (Augustine, *Questions on Leviticus*, question 93.) God calls his own soul, etc., through “who say that Jesus did not have a soul.”

### Verse 12

**“I will walk.”** (Hesychius.) Made man. Hence: “This is our God, and no other will be accounted beside him; after this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings” (Baruch 3).

### Verse 14

**“But if.”** (Hesychius.) He expressed the blessings of the obedient in the preceding chapter; but in the present chapter he shows what the evils of transgressors are. Some of these the Jews suffered according to the letter, but all of them according to the spirit [Col. 0373D].

### Verse 16

**“In want.”** (Idem.) Of the word of God. Hence: “This saying is hard; who can hear it?” (John 6). Because they transgressed the understanding of the Law in order to invalidate the evangelical covenant, he spoke obscurely to them so that they would not understand.

### Verse 17

**“You shall flee, with no one pursuing.”** (Idem.) For the Gentiles will not pursue them in order to drive them out, but will pursue them while hastening toward their salvation, according to the saying: “I pursue, if somehow I may apprehend” (Philippians 3).

**“But if.”** (Idem.) He frequently uses such distinctions, etc., through “signifies a full and complete vengeance.”

### Verse 18

**“I will add correction.”** The Septuagint has: “And I will add to chastise you sevenfold,” etc. Here also “I will add” is superfluous. “Sevenfold” is to be understood as standing for every number [Col. 0374A].

### Verse 19

**“And I will break the pride of your hardness.”** Because you say: “We are Abraham’s seed, and we have never served anyone” (John 8). Therefore you will serve the nations.

### Verse 23

**“The sword.”** The Spirit, which is the word of God, which through preachers convicts the Jews, lest they contradict the holding of the Old Testament together with the Gospel.

**“I will send into the cities.”** Prophets in whom the faithful find fortification and salvation; the enemies flee and are captured there, and there they die, unable to resist the prophets who openly proclaim Christ [Col. 0374B].

### Verse 26

**“So that ten,” etc.** (Hesychius.) They do not have the bread of teaching, etc., through “therefore those who are nourished by these loaves are not satisfied.”

### Verse 27

**“But if,” etc.** (Idem.) Moses is not the only lawgiver, etc., through “and they blasphemed the author of the Law.”

### Verse 29

**“The flesh of your sons.”** That is, the disciples whom you take as sons, whom you lead into the same teaching with forceful words that corrupt the soul.

### Verse 30

**“You shall fall among the ruins.”** For the people fall when the Pharisees fall spiritually—those whom the people admired as idols, being devoted to their traditions.

### Verse 31

**“Your cities.”** Literally, or the books of the prophets, in which they do not find the fruit of holiness [Col. 0374C].

### Verse 34

**“Then the Sabbaths of the land shall please,”** that is, rest—namely, when you are keeping Sabbath and have been removed from the Law, since you do not find your will in the Law and the prophets.

### Verse 36

“It will terrify them.” Just as the leaf conceals the fruit, so the letter conceals the spirit: remove the leaf and receive the fruit.

“The sound of a flying leaf.” Hyperbole: for they will fear even the slightest things.

“They shall fall when no one pursues them.” For we do not pursue them, but follow after them in order to recall them.

### Verse 37

“They shall fall.” When we dispute with them, they bring forward various testimonies in turn; but they will be thrown into confusion by alternate arguments, as each one confounds the other while seeming to come to his aid. [Col. 0374D]

### Verse 41

“Uncircumcised is their mind.” Because they are uncircumcised in heart, polluted by the foreskin of their vices; for it is not the circumcision that is in the flesh that matters (Rom. II).

“Then they will pray for their iniquities.” The Septuagint: “They will approve their sins,” that is, the punishments which they will suffer for their sins.

### Verse 42

“What I made with Jacob.” (Hesychius.) Observe that he has altered the order of time and gender, etc., up to “but they are joined together as things related and corresponding.”

“I will also remember the land.” (Hesychius.) That is, the Scripture which I will entrust after the Jews have been cast out, who violated it [Col. 0375A] or were violating it and interpreting it perversely.

### Verse 44

“Yet even when they were in the land of their enemies.” At the end of the chapter he fittingly speaks gently: those whom he had terrified with threats he consoles with promises.

“Not utterly.” “A partial hardening has come upon Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles should enter,” and so forth (1 Tim. II).

“Nor did I reject them in such a way.” Since I desire the salvation of all, therefore, after such great iniquities, I also save the remnant of the Jews.

### Verse 45

“These are.” (Hesychius.) “Until the appointed time,” etc., up to “not by abolishing, but by fulfilling.”

“On Mount Sinai.” Not on Zion. Hence: “The God of gods will be seen in Zion” (Ps. LXXXIII). And elsewhere: “From Zion, the appearance of his beauty: God will come manifestly” (Ps. XLIX). And in Malachi: “Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his temple” (Mal. III).

## Chapter XXVII

### Verse 2

“A man who.” (Hesychius.) These words are full of wisdom. Above he prescribed what ought or ought not to be done; now he explains either wholly or partly the dignity of those who act, the distinctions between the perfect life, the moderate life, and the beginning of the knowledge of God, and he also describes the differences of the various ages.

“His life.” (Hesychius.) Aquila and Theodotion: “wonderful.” Symmachus: “if he has separated himself.” The Septuagint: “the honor of his life.”

“From the twentieth year.” (Hesychius.) When he is mature, strong, etc., [Col. 0375C] up to “concerning which it is said: ‘Be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect’” (Matt. V).

“ Shekels.” (Hesychius.) Or didrachmas, the sixtyfold fruit, etc., up to “hence: ‘Let a widow be enrolled if she is not less than sixty years old’” (1 Tim. V).

### Verse 5

“From the fifth year.” (Hesychius.) He who is sensible and has begun to advance, but cannot yet be adorned by the discipline of fasting.

“Up to.” (Hesychius.) He who has begun to advance through the five senses; for he has progressed toward virtue and perfection. Those who are twenty years old are strong and vigorous.

“A male shall give twenty shekels.” (Hesychius.) Or didrachmas, that is, forty drachmas, or four hundred obols. The number forty signifies the fruit of fasting and prayers. Moses fasted for that many days (Exod. XXXIV), as did Elijah (3 Kings XIX) and Christ himself, after which he was tempted by the devil (Matt. IV).

### Verse 7

“A female, ten.” (Hesychius.) Or didrachmas, that is, twenty drachmas or two hundred obols: namely, the observance of the Ten Commandments, which are doubled according to letter and spirit. In them fasting is not commanded, because it is fitting for those who have advanced but are not yet perfect.

“From one.” He is one month old who has now been born in faith; to such it is said: “Like newborn infants, long for the rational milk without deceit,” and so forth (1 Pet. II).

“Five.” Or didrachmas, namely, so that the male may have doubled senses and receive what he hears sensibly in an intelligible manner. [Col. 0376A] Thus he is led toward perfection, which is why his valuation is one hundred obols; for the number one hundred signifies perfection.

“For a female.” (Hesychius.) “For a female, three didrachmas,” etc., up to “as though they were already participants in evangelical conduct.”

“Sixty.” He who has promised an excellence of conduct, such as virginity or renunciation of the world, but has grown weak.

“He shall give fifteen.” Or didrachmas, which are thirty drachmas. For the good soil produced three fruits (Matt. XIII): the hundredfold, that is, virginity or renunciation of the world; the sixtyfold, namely, continence; and the thirtyfold, that is, the conduct of a chaste marriage. [Col. 0376B]

### Verse 8

“If he is poor.” He who has sinned greatly; therefore Aquila translated it, “if he has exceeded.”

“He shall stand.” For if we offer any subordinate of ours for the service of God, we ought not to receive him into our own service, promising on his behalf either something better or something less good.

“As much as he who values him shall determine.” That is, he will impose as much as he sees the man able to bear as satisfaction. But if he is wealthy, let him distribute money; if he is healthy, let him fast, pray, and labor.

### Verse 9

“An animal.” Since he has explained the distinctions and degrees of the offerings that come from ourselves, he now explains when the offering of those who are subject to us as animals is holy.

“It shall be holy.” According to the law, spotless and clean; for example, if we offer to God a son, disciple, servant, or anyone subject to us. [Col. 0376C]

### Verse 10

“That.” So that the offering may be twofold, and the enemy may be put to shame, since he had suggested changing the offering.

### Verse 11

“An unclean animal.” (Hesychius.) Those which are not together, etc., up to “so that it may be offered to the Lord.”

It must be understood that to be sanctified is one thing, to be holy is another, to be offered to God is another, and to belong to God is another. Whatever is sanctified and offered begins to be holy, although it was not so before, and it gradually increases. Whatever is holy and belongs to God needs no increase, because it is perfect. It is therefore good to be sanctified by the teaching and assistance of others, but it is better to be such a person as can sanctify both himself and others, which belongs to few.

Thus he sanctifies a house to the Lord who wishes his household and his kin—both sensible and intelligible—to conduct themselves purely and holy, so that they may be the Church of God. But if he is not capable of doing this by himself, the priest ought to consider whether the household is good or evil. For it consists of different persons, and he ought to impose upon each what he is capable of bearing. [Col. 0376D]

### Verse 13

“The fifth part.” The mind, namely, which governs the five senses, without which the foolish virgins are not received into the wedding feast (Matt. XXV).

### Verse 14

“If a man makes a vow.” (Hesychius.) In what follows he says: “Everything that is consecrated to the Lord, whether man,” [Col. 0377A] “animal, or field, cannot be redeemed”; here, however, he commands that a house and a field be redeemed. Perhaps he determines this according to the different intentions of those making the offering, as though in the former case the offerer had no desire to retain any longer what he had completely consecrated.

### Verse 15

“But if he who vowed it,” etc. (Hesychius.) To redeem is to free a household through teaching and a rule of life, and to wash away whatever opposes holiness. He shall add to the priest’s admonition and edification understanding and frequent recollection.

### Verse 16

“But if he consecrates a field.” That is, divine Scripture, whose vine is Christ and whose farmer is the Father (John XIV). In it the treasure is hidden, namely, saving preaching; in it each person’s possession differs, that is, the measure of knowledge which each person has been able to acquire for himself. [Col. 0377B]

“If it is thirty measures,” etc. (Hesychius.) In the thirty measures of barley understand the Old Testament. In the fifty shekels or didrachmas, according to the Septuagint, understand spiritual and perfect teaching. But when this rule is to be applied, whether it should be given perfectly or diminished, understand from what follows: “If immediately from the year of the beginning of the jubilee,” etc.

### Verse 17

“If immediately from the year.” (Hesychius.) That is, if he enters upon the way of grace, etc., up to “the one offering it to the priest will possess it from him.”

### Verse 19

“He shall add a fifth part.” His own understanding to the priest’s teaching. For at first we are governed by the teaching and instruction of the priest, but afterward we ought to advance and add our own understanding.

### Verse 20

“But if,” etc. (Hesychius.) “He consecrates the field and redeems the field,” etc., up to “for its profit belongs to the one who continually governs it.” [Col. 0377C]

### Verse 22

“And not from the property.” Because it had belonged neither to the custody of his ancestors nor to the purchaser himself.

### Verse 23

“The priest shall calculate.” Properly the priest calculates the true redemption with the one who admonished his brother to repentance, determining how he ought to repent. For the one who corrected him knows his actions and conduct strictly; the priest, however, determines the complete redemption.

“According to the number of years.” That is, according to what Scripture teaches about repentance; for this is the valuation of the jubilee, or remission.

“And the one who vowed him to the Lord shall give him.” He does not say “they shall give,” but “he shall give.” Although the determination of the valuation is made by the common counsel of the priest and the one who admonished him to repentance, nevertheless the one who stirred him to repent will offer him. For the repentant person will obey this man, who is himself bound to the penitent so that he may bring to completion what he began. [Col. 0377D]

### Verse 24

“But in the jubilee he shall return to the former owner,” etc. Because a person is not completely cleansed immediately when repentance is offered or determined, but only after it has been carried out; therefore he rightly says, “But in the jubilee,” etc. When repentance has been completed and remission received, he will receive the field of his conduct.

### Verse 25

“Every valuation shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary.” So that every determination may be made with holy weights, that is, weights proceeding from sacred Scripture. For external weights, such as those of philosophers or heretics, by which they weigh human truths and perfections, are neither holy nor just. [Col. 0378A]

“The shekel is twenty.” That is, the Ten Commandments understood according to letter and spirit. Whoever rejects either the Law or the Gospel does not possess the didrachma, nor are his weights holy.

### Verse 26

“The firstborn that.” (Hesychius.) Our firstborn, considered as our animals, are those who obey us: sons, servants, and disciples. But their firstborn are those who obey in such a way that they provide an example and instruction to others. Concerning these it is said elsewhere: “Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord” (Luke II). For he opens the womb for the generation of sons who begins to obey according to God. Hence Paul says of Timothy: “He is my beloved son in the Lord; he will remind you of my ways,” and so forth (1 Cor. IV). [Col. 0378B]

“No one will be able to sanctify or vow it.” Not because such persons are unworthy of sanctification, but because they are already holy and do not need to be sanctified. Such is a son who honors his father and mother in such a way that he also becomes an example to others, offering honor, as it were, to God who commanded this (Exod. XX). A servant likewise, who serves even his earthly masters in simplicity of heart and not merely for appearances, renders service to God himself (Eph. VI).

### Verse 27

“But if it is unclean.” (Hesychius.) A sinner who neither meditates on the Law as he ought nor attempts to distinguish it. Therefore whoever is exceedingly obedient to a father, master, or teacher, but does not meditate on or distinguish the Law, is indeed a firstborn among the animals, but he is unclean.

“And he shall add a fifth part of its price.” Offering him teaching together with understanding and governing him wisely. For it is the mark of an unintelligent father, master, or teacher not to teach those subject to him who belong to him, and not to order their lives so that they may act according to the Law. Let him therefore add understanding to submission and teaching; for he alone is clean in the present case. Hence he says: “He shall add a fifth part of its price.” Obedience has a price; therefore he did not say, “The priest shall value him,” as above. [Col. 0378C]

### Verse 28

“Everything that is consecrated to the Lord, whether man.” (Hesychius.) “To declare anathema is one thing,” etc., up to “that is, the conduct of our allotted portion.”

“Whatever has once been consecrated.” (Hesychius.) No one can despoil an enemy of what has been acquired by the right of war, etc., up to “nor do they receive increase or progress.” [Col. 0378D]

### Verse 30

“Of the Lord.” (Hesychius.) That is, of the one who carries out the commandments of the Law, etc., up to “because he does not know what recompense he ought to expect.”

### Verse 31

“If anyone.” (Hesychius.) According to the letter, the Lawgiver inserted many obscure and insoluble things, etc., up to “and the fruits of trees according to their season.”

### Verse 32

“Under the shepherd’s staff.” (Hesychius.) The staff of the cross, etc., up to “and they are known by him alone who distinguishes the holy.” [Col. 0379A]

### Verse 33

“It shall not be chosen, nor,” etc. Because there is no one who can be rejected, and it is not for you to decide which should rather be chosen.

“If anyone changes,” etc. (Hesychius.) Paul and Barnabas at one time disagreed, etc., up to his writing to Timothy: “Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry” (2 Tim. IV).

“It shall be sanctified to the Lord,” etc. (Hesychius.) Since everyone’s course is divine, lofty, and close to heavenly conduct, you strive in vain to remove one, introduce another, and consecrate one to God as though he were better. [Col. 0380A]

### Verse 34

“These are the commandments which he commanded,” etc. (Hesychius.) When our disciples are perfect, they need none of our instruction. Therefore he says that the unclean firstborn must be redeemed, but the clean not at all; nor must those consecrated to the Lord be redeemed, nor those of whom he has just spoken. For they have been shown to be perfect, since they bear a divine and heavenly intention.

[Col. 0379]

# The Book of Numbers

In Hebrew, **VAIEDABBER** (), that is: **“AND HE SPOKE.”** (G)*

## Preface

[Col. 0379B]

This book is placed fourth in the Law, both in the order of the history and in its mystery. In the historical order, because Leviticus, which is third, deals with the furnishings of the tabernacle, the order of the Levites, and sacrifice; this book, however, deals with the dedication of the tabernacle, namely, what the Levites are to carry, and what furnishings of the tabernacle they are to carry. Its mystery is shown in this: the tabernacle is set down with a watch kept around it by three tribes on each of the four sides. By this are signified the twelve apostles, who taught the faith of the Holy Trinity throughout the fourfold world.

Among figures, moreover, nothing is firmer than the square, and the perfection of the fourfold work is also commended. The lights were made on the fourth day (Gen. I); the fourth age, under David, was exceedingly strong; [Col. 0379C] the fourth age of man is likewise the strongest; and only four were received who wrote the Gospels. Among the gifts of the Holy Spirit is fortitude; and among the penitential psalms, “Have mercy on me, O God,” is the fourth, dealing with humility, through which we are strong. Among the names of the Lord, “strong” is the fourth: “Wonderful,” “Counselor,” and “God” precede it; “Father of the age to come” and “Prince of peace” follow it (Isa. IX), along with similar names. In this book also the strength of those who are numbered is shown, since those who are suited to war by age and virtue are commanded to be numbered.

It is called the Book of Numbers because the Israelites are numbered in it, both for this reason and because the encampments from Rameses to the Jordan are enumerated. But since “all these things happened to them in a figure” (1 Cor. X), and the Law was a shadow of things to come, [Col. 0379D] the history must be read in such a way that the allegory is not lost. Only the Israelites were numbered, not the proselytes and foreigners who were among them; yet not all Israelites were numbered, since neither children nor women were included, but only men fit for war.

For those alienated from God through the uncleanness of the Gentiles—or through Jewish cruelty—or Christians possessing childish fickleness or feminine softness are not numbered among the children of God. They were not numbered in Egypt, but after they had crossed the Red Sea, after the pillar of fire, at the encampment beside Mount Sinai. For those who remain in the darkness of sins do not belong to God; rather, those cleansed by baptism and armed by the laying on of hands belong to him. [Col. 0380B]

The encampments are rightly counted as twelve, from the first, which was at Rameses, to the Jordan, so that this may signify that we ascend into heaven through as many stages of virtues as there are generations by which Christ descended from Abraham to Mary.

Moses’ purpose in this work is to designate, through Israel and through the twelve encampments, the Christian people, their progress, and their ascent from earth to heaven. Israel signifies the people of Christ; the progress through the encampments signifies progress in virtue.

The order of the book is as follows. First, the leaders of the people and the people themselves are numbered and placed around the tabernacle in a square. The Levites, excluded from the numbering, are assigned to the service of the tabernacle. Then the tabernacle is dedicated, the manner of the offerings is given, and the list of the encampments is counted. [Col. 0380C] Next, Balaam’s prophecy is introduced: King Balak brings him in to curse the people of God. At the end, six cities are established—three beyond and three on this side of the Jordan—as places of refuge for one who, unwillingly, has shed the blood of his neighbor.

The Levites, keeping watch between the tabernacle and the rest of the children of Israel, divided among the Amramites in the east, the Kohathites in the south, the Gershonites in the west, and the Merarites in the north, signify the leaders of the Church. They stand between the ministers of the tabernacle, for whom they provide in temporal matters, and the laity, whom they govern in spiritual matters.

The Amramites—that is, Moses, Aaron, and their sons—inspect and wrap the innermost things of the tabernacle. Bringing in the Kohathites, they give them the wrapped objects to carry on their own shoulders, so that they may not die when they see them. For the mysteries of the Church must not be disclosed [Col. 0380D] except to the highest-ranking men, that is, Moses and Aaron, because the weak are scandalized by them. Hence the Gospel book is carried open by the presbyter and deacon, but closed by others.

The Gershonites and Merarites, who are less honored than the Kohathites, carry their burdens not on their own shoulders but by oxen and wagons. For “whoever wishes to come after me, let him follow me,” as though through death (Luke IX). And the more someone wishes to follow, the greater the persecution.

“You shall bless the children of Israel and say,” etc. From this passage comes the blessing pronounced by the bishop. The two raised fingers joined together signify the Law and the priesthood, understood through Moses and Aaron. [Col. 0381A] The three verses that follow contain the threefold petition made in the bishop’s words: the grace of the Holy Spirit, true salvation, and eternal peace are requested. Then follows the distinction of persons, always in these words: “May he himself deign to grant this, who lives with the Father and the Holy Spirit,” and so forth.

At the dedication of the tabernacle, gifts were offered by the leaders for its use and for the support of the Levites; the same thing is done today when a church is dedicated. So also, according to the custom of the laity, many gifts are offered to a woman when she is betrothed to a man. The Lord also granted silver vessels to the children of Israel in Egypt on the day when he was to lead them out. After the Red Sea he did not lead them immediately by the direct route against their enemies, lest they become afraid and turn back, but by a circuitous route. Then he commanded that [Col. 0381B] [the text is materially uncertain: “ne temporis re. p. t.”]. All things were carefully provided for. For when people enter the Church, its beauty must first be shown to them so that they may desire it, not its misery, so that they may fear it.

(Origen, Homily 1 on Numbers.) Not everyone is worthy of the divine numbers, etc., up to “he called them the hairs of the head.”

(The same.) Let us also consider this, etc., up to “and then the people are brought to the number at God’s command.”

See, therefore, how much you must pass through, how much you must endure, through how many advances, temptations, and battles you must fight, and how much you must conquer, in order to belong to the divine number, to be numbered among the holy tribes, to be visited, and to be enrolled by the priests of God, Aaron and Moses, in the censuses of the numbered. First you must receive the Law of God, the Law of his Spirit; [Col. 0381C] sacrifices must be offered; purifications must be completed; and everything taught by the Spirit must be carried out.

(Origen, same work.) The arrangement of the tribes, the distinction of orders, and the association of families, etc., up to “and such orders will exist in the resurrection of the dead, which are represented in this book.”

The fact that the position of the camps and the order of their encampment are described through a certain connection of the tribes also signifies a particular state in the resurrection of the dead. Three are placed in the east, three in the west, three in the south, and the last three in the north, which is called the harsh wind (Ecclus. XLIII). It is likewise not without significance that the tribe of Judah, which is royal (Ecclus. XLIV), is placed in the east, since the Lord arose from it. Issachar is joined to it, as is Zebulun, [Col. 0381D] and this threefold number is arranged in four parts.

Although these groups have different qualities according to their positions, they are all contained within the number of the Trinity. The fact that throughout all four regions they are gathered into one number signifies the same Trinity always, since all who come from the four regions of the world and call upon the name of the Lord are reckoned under the one name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. They recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of God (Matt. VIII).

We have spoken generally in this way because we wished briefly to comprehend the mystical content of this book. Taking the opportunity, let each person pursue a similar image in what follows—or, if God reveals more to anyone, a higher one. For I truly judge myself unequal to explaining the mysteries of the Book of Numbers, and much more inferior still to those contained in the volume of Deuteronomy. [Col. 0382A]

(Rabanus, on Numbers.) The Fathers show that the Book of Numbers is wrapped in a manifold obscurity of mysteries. In it the number of the children of Israel is mystically described, and the camps of the individual tribes are arranged around the tabernacle of testimony in the form of the Church. In it there is the distribution of the Levites for service and the offering of the leaders according to the correspondence of the sacraments. Finally, the catalogue of all the encampments from Egypt to the Promised Land is counted, to show how, having departed from spiritual Egypt, we hasten through the Red Sea and the desert of the present age toward our promised homeland in the heavens. [Col. 0382B]

(The same.) At the end of Exodus it is written, etc., up to “because he gives the Law for the instruction of believers, that is, of spiritual Israelites.”

(Isidore, on Numbers, volume V.) The Book of Numbers is so called, etc., up to “from which the grace of the Holy Spirit flowed forth and overflowed in a full flood.”

(The same.) The first encampment is, etc., up to “holding staffs in their hands.”

(The same.) The second encampment, etc., up to “and to hasten toward the holy land of the living.”

(The same.) The third encampment, etc., up to “so that under the leadership of our leaders we may reach the Promised Land.”

(The same.) The fourth encampment, etc., up to “Miriam leading the singing with tambourines.”

(The same.) The fifth is, etc., up to “so that sweetness may again be restored.” [Col. 0382C]

(The same.) The sixth encampment is, etc., up to “leaders of the sheep, teachers of the nations.”

(The same.) The seventh encampment is, etc., up to “and past dangers may be set before the eyes.”

(The same.) The eighth, etc., up to “we deserve the enemy’s great hatred.”

(The same.) The ninth, etc., up to “we begin to knock at the sacraments.”

(The same.) The tenth, etc., up to “the bread of angels is eaten.”

(The same.) The eleventh, etc., up to “the remaining matters will be explained more suitably in their proper places.”

## Chapter I

[Col. 0382D]

### Verse 3

“Of all the men.” (Origen, Homily 1 on Numbers.) Another version of the Septuagint: “Everyone who goes forth in the strength of Israel,” etc. “Therefore, whoever goes forth,” etc., up to “is handed down through evangelical and apostolic faith.”

### Verse 4
