“Leaders of the tribes,” etc. (Augustine, Questions 1 on Numbers.) What does it mean that he commands leaders to be chosen, one from each tribe, etc., up to “so that they may be called χιλίαρχοι [chiliarchs, commanders of a thousand]”?

### Verse 5

“From the tribe of Reuben.” (Rabanus, on Numbers, volume II.) Morally, Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, etc., up to “one heart and one soul.”

(Rabanus, same work.) The leader of the tribe of Reuben generally signifies those, etc., up to “caring for the continent, virgins, and both sexes.”

[Col. 0383A]

### Verse 6

“From the tribe of Simeon.” (Rabanus.) Simeon generally signifies all who obey, etc., up to those who say: “To you I have lifted up my eyes, who dwell in the heavens” (Ps. CXXII).

### Verse 7

“From the tribe of Judah.” (The same.) In Judah may be signified all who rightly invoke the name of the Lord and who, neither in understanding nor in speech, dissent from the rule of faith. Naasson is rightly their leader: he not only instructs others by preaching, but also kills within himself the poisonous darts of vices by disciplining his body, according to the saying: “I chastise my body and bring it into subjection,” and so forth (1 Cor. IX).

Allegorically, Judah—from whom came the kings—which is interpreted as “confession” or “praise,” signifies here the people of the Church, whose head is the lion from the tribe of Judah, that is, Christ. [Col. 0383B] For the praise or confession of true faith, that is, right preaching, exists only in the Church.

Therefore Naasson, that is, “serpentine” or “divination,” son of Aminadab, that is, “spontaneous people,” is understood as the Savior born from the patriarchs, servants devoted to God, who by his death destroyed the devil. In the serpent, from which the first cause of death—that is, sin—proceeded, death is represented. Hence: “Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,” and so forth (John III).

### Verse 8

“From the tribe of Issachar.” (The same.) Issachar fittingly represents monks. Having rejected all the affairs of the world, they seek an eternal reward through a strict life, with pleasure mortified, by the gift of God—that is, under the protection of the Holy Spirit. Trampling the pomp of the world beneath their feet and embracing humility, they desire to please God alone. [Col. 0383C]

“Nathanael son of Suar.” Nathanael is the leader of those who devote themselves piously to receive a reward in heaven. His name means “my God” or “gift of God”; he is the son of Suar, that is, “of the little one of Christ,” namely, of the one who appeared little among human beings. He himself is both leader and reward.

### Verse 9

“From the tribe of Zebulun.” (The same.) Zebulun represents those who are patient, etc., up to “against heretics and schismatics.”

### Verse 10

“Joseph.” Joseph, the father of two tribes, signifies Christ, the Father of two peoples and the cornerstone. Ephraim, the younger, preferred to Manasseh the firstborn, signifies the Gentile people preferred to the Jewish people. Hence: “Truly I say to you, I have not found such faith in Israel” (Matt. VIII).

“Elishama.” Elishama signifies Christ, of whom it is said: “He became obedient to the Father unto death,” and so forth (Phil. II). He himself says: “What I have heard from him, these things I speak in the world” (John VIII). He is the son of Ammihud, that is, “of an illustrious people,” namely, of the stock of kings, patriarchs, and prophets.

(Rabanus.) Elishama, leader of the tribe of Ephraim, signifies those who attentively hear the word of God with a good and excellent heart and bear fruit in patience.

“Manasseh,” etc. “One who forgets,” namely, forgetting what lies behind and stretching himself toward what lies ahead, so that he may receive the crown of life which God will give to those who love him (Phil. III; James I). [Col. 0384A]

“Gamaliel.” Gamaliel, “God has repaid me,” son of Pedahzur, that is, “of strong redemption,” is leader in the tribe of Manasseh, whose name is interpreted as “forgotten” or “forgetful.” When Christ—whom the Father sent into the world to call the Jewish people—came into his kingdom, he found a forgetful nation. Israel had forgotten its Creator. Yet not all perished; when the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, all Israel will be saved (Rom. XI).

### Verse 11

“From the tribe of Benjamin.” Benjamin signifies Jerusalem, which lies within his tribe. Its people, according to Rachel’s prophecy, were **Ben-Oni**, that is, “son of sorrow,” because he afflicted his mother with great grief. He shed the blood of the prophets and, conspiring in Christ’s death, said: “His blood be upon us and upon our children” (Matt. XXVII).

[Col. 0384B]

Among believers, however, according to the father’s prophecy, he is “son of the right hand.” Benjamin may also signify the Gentile people, who were “son of sorrow” because they persecuted Christians. He may also be called “son of the right hand,” either because at the judgment he will be at God’s right hand, or because he performs the right hand’s work, that is, good works.

Abidan, “my father is judge,” son of Gideoni, whose name is interpreted as “temptation of iniquity” or “of humility,” is the leader of this people. For Christ—whom the Jew despised as humble and whom the devil wickedly tempted—is the head of believers and the judge who is to come of the living and the dead.

Morally, Benjamin, “son of the right hand,” signifies those who fight bravely against enemies, firmly suppressing the goads of temptation and not permitting anything feminine or soft to rule within them. [Col. 0384C]

### Verse 12

“From the tribe of Dan.” Dan means “judgment” or “judging.” These are those who do everything with discernment and appoint Abiezer—“brother who helps”—as their leader, because they do everything according to the rule of the Fathers, or attribute all their good things to God.

(Rabanus, in the work cited above.) Dan, etc., up to “they are urged toward fellowship in spiritual grace.”

### Verse 13

“From the tribe of Asher.” (The same.) Asher, etc., up to “for it will be repaid to them in the resurrection of the just.”

### Verse 14

“From the tribe of Gad.” (The same.) Allegorically, etc., up to: “A rooster with girded loins and a ram, and there is no king who can resist him” (Prov. XXX).

### Verse 15

“From the tribe of Naphtali.” Naphtali, etc., up to: “I will no longer call you servants, but friends,” and so forth (John XV). [Col. 0384D]

### Verse 16

“By their clans.” (Augustine, Questions 2 on Numbers.) It is rightly asked why, etc., up to “and the New Testament through the four Gospels.”

### Verse 18

“From the twentieth year.” (Isidore.) Those chosen for war are numbered from the twentieth year, because from this age the battles against the individual vices arise. Therefore they are chosen for combat, so that they may fight against lust and not be overcome by luxury.

### Verse 37

“Thirty-five thousand.” The good married, because to signify the thirtyfold reward the forefinger and thumb touch in a gentle kiss. Hence one is thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another one hundredfold.

### Verse 59

“Seven hundred.” Those advanced in spiritual gifts and destined to be placed at the right hand of God. For the number one hundred is the first number counted on the right, [Col. 0385A] with thumb and forefinger bent into a crown. Hence: “Now the right hand counts the years.”

(Rabanus, on Numbers, volume II.) In the tribe of Levi, etc., up to “as though they carried the Church on the shoulders of labor and patience.”

### Verse 51

“When it is time to set out,” etc. That is, they will arrange by word and example how each person, humbled, should proceed in the advancement of virtues.

“Whoever is an outsider,” etc. (Augustine, Questions 3.) “The foreigner who approaches shall die.” Here “foreigner” must also be understood of those children of Israel, etc., up to “so that they may be called allophyli, as though they were people of other tribes.”

[Col. 0385B]

Allegorically: Whoever approaches the sacred ministry unworthily does not escape the punishment of presumption. For no one ought to take the honor for himself unless he is called by God, as Aaron was (Heb. V). Hence Uzziah, who usurped the priesthood, was struck with leprosy.

### Verse 52

“Each one according to his companies,” etc. (Origen, Homily 2 on Numbers.) “Each one according to his standards,” etc., up to “if nothing disturbed, nothing disordered, and nothing dishonorable is found in us.”

## Chapter II

### Verse 1

“And the Lord spoke.” (Origen, Homily 2 on Numbers.) A man according to his order, etc., up to “and to do nothing according to order.”

(The same.) Each one of us, etc., up to “lest on his account the name of God be blasphemed.”

[Col. 0385C]

“According to their standards.” By these the particular character of each person is designated, etc., up to “how much more do the rest of humanity bear their own standards in the movements of their minds and in the virtues of the soul?”

### Verse 2

“Around the tabernacle,” etc. (Rabanus, on Numbers.) Around the tabernacle, etc., up to “by whose prayers and teaching the Church is fortified.”

### Verse 9

“All who are in the camp of Judah.” Judah presides over these tribes: the royal tribe, from which Christ was born, the king and savior of the human race.

### Verse 10

“The southern side shall have as its leader.” This signifies the ancient people of God, who, receiving the light of the Gospel or of the Law, burned with love for the Creator.

### Verse 17

“The tabernacle of testimony shall be lifted up,” etc. The erection or dismantling of the tabernacle signifies the condition of the Church. It is erected among believers and dismantled among those who deny; in some sacred orders it is exalted, while in others it is humbled by the judgment of the priests through excommunication.

“On the western side they shall be,” etc. (Rabanus, on Numbers, volume II.) Let us say something further that may assist the reader, etc., up to “so that they may safely fulfill the divine office.” [Col. 0385D]

### Verse 18

“Western.” This side receives both walls of the tabernacle into itself, joining and completing them, and signifies the completion of the Church at the end of the world. Then the elect will be proved in the fruit of good works, the wicked will be handed over to oblivion and death, and the righteous will be placed at the right hand of God. [Col. 0386A]

### Verse 25

“The children of Dan camped on the northern side.” This side signifies the multitude of the Gentiles, languishing in the cold of unbelief until Christ, but, after the Jews were rejected by God’s judgment, enlarged within the Church and awaiting eternal blessedness.

## Chapter III

### Verse 3

“Of the priests who were anointed,” etc. (Rabanus, on Numbers, volume II.) The four sons of Aaron, etc., up to “are consumed by the fire of divine vengeance.”

### Verse 6

“Bring forward the tribe.” (Augustine, Questions 4 on Numbers.) “Take the tribe of Levi,” etc., up to “among the other camps of the children of Israel.”

[Col. 0386B]

### Verse 10

“An outsider.” (The same.) “The foreigner who touches it shall die.” It must be asked how he said this, etc., up to “for he was speaking from this point.”

### Verse 12

“I have taken the Levites.” (Augustine, Questions 6.) What does it mean that the Levites, etc., up to “nor are the descendants of the Levites or their animals counted in place of them.”

(Origen, Homily 3 on Numbers.) “I have taken the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel in place of every firstborn.” The Levites are taken in place of the firstborn, etc., up to “so that it is a greater thing to be taken in place of the firstborn than to be born firstborn.”

**LXX:** “From the midst of the sons of Israel,” and so forth. Levi is third among the sons of Israel; from what, then, are the Levites taken “from the midst”? I find the Shunammite confidently answering the king of Israel: “I dwell in the midst of my people” [Col. 0386C] (2 Kings 4). And John says of Christ: “There stands among you one whom you do not know.” I therefore think that one who has never turned aside to the right or to the left may be said to stand in the midst—one who committed no sin, and in whose mouth no deceit was found (Isa. 53). And because he always stands, he is said to stand in the midst. But one who imitates him, like the Shunammite, is not said to stand, because he sometimes inclines either to the right or to the left. For no one is clean from defilement, not even if his life should last a single day (Job 15); nevertheless, he is said to dwell in the midst of the people. The Levites, therefore, are taken from the midst of the sons of Israel. For Levites are those who did not know their right hand from their left, but, following Moses—that is, the law of God—spared neither father nor mother. So you too, if, when temptation and the anger of sin come, you neither incline to the right nor to the left, do not transgress the law of God, but stand fixed and steadfast in the midst; neither bend your knee to sin nor follow the image of a beast’s head—that is, of foolishness. You will be taken from the midst of the sons of Israel and placed among the firstborn.

**“He opens.”** Not everyone who opened the womb is worthy of primacy; hence: “Sinners are estranged from the womb; they have gone astray from the belly; they have spoken falsehoods” (Ps. 57). For how could anyone have gone astray from the way of God as soon as he came out of his mother’s womb? Or how could a newly born child have spoken falsehood? It is therefore necessary to seek a belly and womb to which the words “Sinners are estranged from the womb,” and so forth, may properly apply. And that will be the womb which every firstborn opens when he is sanctified to the Lord. The Lord opened Leah’s womb, which had been closed, and she bore the patriarchs; likewise Rachel’s, so that she too might bear children, although her sight was keen and her appearance beautiful (Gen. 29–30). In many passages of Scripture you will find wombs being opened; if you consider each according to its context, you will discover how sinners go astray from the womb, while others, by opening the womb, are sanctified in the order of the firstborn.

**“From which.”** (ORIG.) Because the firstborn of Israel were not sanctified beforehand, and so forth, until: “and he might be placed in the order of the firstborn.”

**VERSE 15.—Count the sons of Levi.** (ID.) Let us examine more attentively, and so forth, until: “and by perpetual watches they perform the divine ministries.”

[Col. 0387B] **VERSE 17.—Levi according to their names.** Levi means “added” or “taken up.” This is the order of teachers, who, chosen from the world by the grace of God for divine service, are joined to the assemblies of angels. Hence: “I chose you from the world” (John 15). And elsewhere: “They are like the angels of God in heaven” (Matt. 22).

**Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.** The three sons of Levi signify preachers of the Holy Trinity, distinguished by confession and admirable in faith, hope, and charity. Nor does the interpretation of their names in any way contradict this exposition; rather, it agrees with it very well. For Gershon is interpreted as “sojourner,” Kohath as “patience,” or “molar teeth,” and Merari as “bitter,” or “bitterness.” The minister of God recognizes himself as a sojourner and stranger in the world, and he is patient. He grinds the word of God with the tooth of discernment, according to the capacities of his hearers; and, showing the world to be bitter to him, he recalls others from its pleasures. They are counted from one month onward, because they must consecrate the beginning of their life to God, lest, after being promoted following many crimes, they cause the name of God to be blasphemed. Hence: “It is necessary that a bishop be blameless,” and so forth (1 Tim. 3).

**VERSE 23.—These shall encamp behind the tabernacle.** The fitting order of the sons of Levi is shown here: those who are first in rank are to guard the eastern side. Moses and Aaron, with their sons, are to have charge of the sanctuary in the midst of the sons of Israel. The Kohathites, from whom Moses and Aaron descended, are to occupy the southern side under the care of Eleazar the priest, who is senior to the sons of Aaron. After them come the Gershonites on the western side under the care of Eliasaph. Last are the Merarites on the northern side, under the guardianship of Ithamar, the younger son of Aaron. Morally, this expresses that the ministers of the Church must carefully preserve their proper order and must not desire greater things than their own position requires.

**VERSE 24.—To the west, under the leader Eliasaph son of Lael.** Where day closes, the stars set. This signifies that the ministers of the tabernacle must flee desire, mortify carnal longings with God’s help, and await the final day and the end of their labor, so that, dead to the world and alive to God, they may say: “But far be it from me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Gal. 6).

[Col. 0388A] **VERSE 29.—To the south.** This signifies that, after receiving the light of knowledge, the preacher ought, with discretion, to offer the word of patience and consolation to his neighbors. Under Eleazar—that is, under God’s help—according to the saying: “Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.”

**VERSE 35.—On the side.** The last of the Merarites, under Ithamar—whose name is interpreted as “bitter,” or “where there is a palm”—received the northern side, where icy horror persists. By this the ministers of the Church are warned not to grow sluggish through security. Although they have already entered the Church through the door of faith, received the light of knowledge, and mortified the desires of the flesh, they have not yet reached perfect sweetness—that is, eternal blessedness. Something bitter remains; they must contend with him who directs his throne toward the north, whose hardness cannot be softened. Hence: “His heart will be hardened like a stone,” and so forth (Isa. 14; Job 21). But when he has been overcome, they should rejoice and exult, having won the palm.

**VERSE 38.—Toward the eastern side.** The eastern side signifies the rising of faith, where Moses—whose name is interpreted as “taken from the water”—and Aaron, “mountain of strength,” encamp with their sons. Those who preside in the Church, to whom the keys of the heavenly kingdom have been entrusted (Matt. 16), ought to understand the order of entry and preach it to others. For everyone must enter the light of faith through the gate of confession into the water of baptism, so that, taken from the water, he may become a son by adoption; and, bringing forth children of good [Col. 0388C] works through the strength of steadfastness, he must carefully guard the entrance of faith through which he entered the Church, lest he be cast out as idle and useless.

**VERSE 39.—Twenty-two thousand.** The Levites are appropriately designated by the number twenty-two. For the Hebrew letters are comprised in this number and, according to some, the books of the Old Testament as well. By this prescription the ministers of God are warned to live and teach according to the law of God and not to exceed it in any way.

**(ORIG., Homily 4 on Numbers.)** There are many differences among numbers, and so forth, until: “the mystery of human generation is also explained.”

**VERSE 47.—Five shekels.** Mystically, whoever wishes to consecrate to God the beginning of his way of life and his will must carefully guard the five bodily senses, [Col. 0388D] lest through wantonness he slide into error or impure desires. But according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty obols—that is, according to the teaching of the Decalogue, which consists in the two commandments of charity—he should refer all his works to the house of the high priest and his sons.

# CHAPTER IV

**VERSE 2.—Take the total.** (ORIG.) Since the sons of Levi are divided into three orders, and so forth, until: “and we indicate them by purer senses, freed from worldly things.”

**(ID.) Another text reads,** and so forth, until: “so that he may perform the works in the tabernacle of testimony.”

**VERSE 3.—In the tabernacle.** (ID.) The tabernacle of testimony, and so forth, until: “not by Israelites but by Levites.” [Col. 0389A] **And they shall wrap the ark in it.** Lest anyone see it uncovered and die. For the one who touches ineffable mysteries is exterminated unless he has been promoted to the rank of priesthood by merit and knowledge.

**(ORIG., Homily 4 on Numbers.)** Seven particular kinds are enumerated, and so forth, until: “but let others see these things covered—or rather veiled—and carry them on their shoulders.”

**VERSE 6.—And they shall cover.** The sons of Aaron, the priests, to whom it is permitted to see everything naked and exposed.

**VERSE 7.—The continual loaves.** (AUG., Question 7 on Numbers.) “And the loaves that will always be upon it.” Certainly not the same loaves always, but loaves like them, because the former were removed and fresh ones were placed daily, while the table was never left without loaves. Therefore he said, “which will always be upon it”: that is, because there would always be loaves, not because those same loaves would always remain.

**VERSE 11.—And likewise the altar.** Another text reads: “And over the golden altar they shall spread a violet-colored cloth, and they shall cover it with a covering of violet leather.” This wording might seem to be the kind of expression that the Latin translators, regarding it as absurd and incomplete, wished to render thus: “Over the golden altar they shall spread a violet-colored cloth,” as though it ought to have said, “and they shall cover the golden altar with a violet-colored cloth,” not “they shall cover the violet-colored cloth.” This seems to signify that the violet-colored cloth itself was to be covered with something else. But it seems to me that this is not so much a type of expression as an obscure meaning. For it may be understood as follows: they shall spread a violet-colored cloth over the golden altar, so that the command has also prescribed that the violet-colored cloth itself be covered with another thing. The cloth would already be upon the altar, and the whole could be expressed briefly by saying that the altar was to be covered with a violet-colored cloth and that the violet-colored cloth was to be covered with another covering. Finally, he added with what he wanted the violet-colored cloth to be covered, when he said: “and they shall cover it with a covering of violet leather.”

**VERSE 15.—Then the sons of Kohath shall enter.** (ORIG., Homily 4.) Although they are not priests, and so forth, until: “whose inheritance our Lord Jesus Christ will grant us.”

**VERSE 18.—Do not destroy.** (ORIG.) “Do not exterminate the tribe of Kohath,” and so forth. Understand first the arrangement of the tabernacle, and so forth, until: “but shoulders signify works.”

**VERSE 20.—Others nothing, and so forth.** (ORIG.) In ecclesiastical observances also, and so forth, until: “and reason should require it to be brought into action.”

**VERSE 23.—From thirty.** The number thirty, formed by multiplying ten three times, signifies the integrity of faith and the perfection of works, without which no one should approach the divine ministries. Joseph, at the age of thirty, assumed the administration of Egypt (Gen. 41), and David assumed the kingdom, which he completed at seventy years—that is, at the age worthy of perpetual rest (3 Kings 2). Ezekiel also obtained the gifts of prophecy (Ezek. 1). And because adversities must be endured patiently through faith and rewards hoped for sublimely, the height of the ark or temple and the length of the tabernacle are measured as thirty cubits.

**“Fifty,” and so forth.** (ORIG.) In this book also, concerning the spoils of enemies, and so forth, until: “and deliver them to the sons of Kohath to be carried on their shoulders and transported by hand.”

**“All who enter,” and so forth.** (ORIG., Homily 5 on Numbers.) It is said concerning the Levites, and so forth, until: “who is found perfect in every respect through senses multiplied and purified.”

**VERSE 35.—To the fiftieth year.** (ORIG.) The fiftieth year signifies remission and indulgence, and so forth, until: “if the completion of one decade is added, the result is five hundred.”

# CHAPTER V

**VERSE 2.—Every leper.** Lepers are heretics polluted by various stains of error, not possessing [Col. 0390B] a uniform color of doctrine or faith; nor do they conceal their ignorance, but display it. Yet there is no false doctrine that does not at some time mingle some truth with it. Truth mixed with falsehood in anyone’s disputation or narrative, appearing as though it were the color of a single body, signifies leprosy, like the colors of truth and falsehood varying the human body in different places.

**VERSE 6.—Man or woman.** (RAB. on Numbers.) By this chapter we are admonished that, if we commit any offense through negligence, we should wash it away through confession and repentance and restore the loss. If we have inflicted loss upon our neighbor, we should repent before him and restore the loss. But if he is no longer present, we should satisfy the Lord by confessing, repenting, and giving alms.

[Col. 0390C] **(AUG., and so forth, Question 9 on Numbers.)** Another text reads, and so forth, until: “which was taken away through the offense.”

**VERSE 7.—They shall restore it.** (AUG., Question 10 on Numbers.) It is asked how Exodus can read, and so forth, until: “by which a thief who had been apprehended or convicted ought to be punished.”

**VERSE 8.—Except the offering of a ram.** The offering of the ram signifies Christ’s passion, in which we place our greatest confidence, because without him we can do nothing. He is the priest who reconciles us to the Father through the offering of his flesh (Job 15); therefore we offer our gifts to him, through whose intercession we may deserve pardon.

**VERSE 9.—To the priest.** Namely, to Christ, of whom it is said: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Ps. 110). Reserving everything, that is, to his judgment, lest someone judge an uncertain matter prematurely. Hence: “Do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes,” and so forth.

**(RAB. on Numbers.)** Barley flour signifies knowledge of the old law, and so forth, until: “it is reserved either for condemnation or liberation.”

**VERSE 15.—He shall not pour.** It is not fitting to anoint the unrepentant with the oil of flattery or indiscriminate mercy, nor with the incense of excessive praise or disordered prayer; rather, according to the Lord’s command, vice must be pursued promptly and orderly with zeal for justice.

**VERSE 17.—Holy water.** (ID.) The priest mixes a little earth from the floor of the tabernacle with this water. [Col. 0391A] In accordance with Christ’s decree, a commemoration of the patriarchs, prophets, and apostles is found to have been introduced.

**VERSE 23.—The priest shall write in a book, and so forth.** The punishment of sinners is explained in Holy Scripture. Whoever imbibes it devoutly and faithfully, fearing and avoiding the punishments of sinners narrated in it, will find the water, though exceedingly bitter, to be for his salvation. But whoever despises it will have his belly swell, his thigh decay, and he will become a curse and an example, because he will be punished by God’s just judgment; his desires and actions will become a reproach to him.

**VERSE 24.—He shall give her to drink,** so that her sin may be revealed, either here for correction or in the future for condemnation. For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed (Matt. 10). Hence the Lord says: “The word that I have spoken to you will judge you on the last day” (John 12).

# CHAPTER VI

**VERSE 3.—From wine and everything that can intoxicate.** (RAB. on Numbers.) In the twelfth encampment, and so forth, until: “and take delight in the corruption of the old wickedness.”

**VERSE 5.—No razor shall pass over him.** (ID.) That is, he will retain neither deceit nor malice in his mind, lest the hair of his head—that is, the thought of his mind—be polluted. Rather, he must preserve innocence until the end of his life. Otherwise his vow will not be acceptable. “But whoever perseveres will be saved” (Matt. 10).

[Col. 0391C] **VERSE 6.—He shall not approach a dead person.** (ID.) That is, he will not imitate one dead in sins, nor enter into the life of his iniquity, lest he lose his labor. For it is not the one who begins but the one who completes who will be crowned (2 Tim. 2).

**VERSE 7.—Nor over his father.** (ID.) That is, no carnal affection should draw him back. Every person, every rank, and every blood relationship must be subordinated to the service of Christ.

**God’s consecration.** (ID.) That is, the grace of the Holy Spirit has been poured into his heart. Hence: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit, in whom you have all been sealed” (Eph. 4).

**VERSE 8.—All the days of his separation.** That is, let him persevere to the end without contamination by sin or transgression.

[Col. 0391D] **VERSE 9.—But if someone dies.** (ID.) That is, if he wishes to imitate one polluted by mortal sin and descends as far as consent, he must know that his purity has been polluted and that his head must be shaved—that is, his mind must be cleansed from evil thought and harmful pleasure.

**He shall shave it immediately.** (ID.) At the time of compunction, when he recognizes that he has sinned, he should immediately strive to amend himself and always fear a similar fall.

**VERSE 10.—Two turtledoves.** (ID.) Turtledoves signify chastity, and young pigeons simplicity. Whoever, therefore, wishes to reach the resurrection of the good should offer to the priest—that is, to Christ—chastity of mind and body and simplicity in the Catholic faith, [Col. 0392A] through which he enters the Church, so that through the assistance of so great a high priest he may be purified.

**VERSE 11.—And he shall intercede.** (ID.) Hence: “Our advocate with the Father” (1 John 2). Or because he will cause us to intercede, according to the saying: “The Spirit pleads for us with inexpressible groanings” (Rom. 8).

**VERSE 12.—As the former days.** He must presume nothing from his former way of life, but trust solely in the grace of God, by whose gift he receives pardon and eternal rest.

**The consecration has been polluted.** Hence: “When the righteous turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, all his righteousnesses will be handed over to oblivion” (Ezek. 18).

**This is the law of consecration.** After the legislator has instructed the Nazirite how he is to be cleansed if his consecration is polluted by a dead person, he adds how, after completing his vow, he is to present himself to the Lord and offer thanks through an oblation. Mystically, he indicates that the continent life, together with the offering of works and purity of heart, will be pleasing to the good Lord at the end.

**VERSE 14.—A yearling lamb.** He offers this who places all his hope in its sacrifice; concerning it is said: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world” (John 1). He offers it as a burnt offering when, for love of it, he mortifies his flesh and consecrates his entire life to the Lord, kindled by the fire of charity.

**(AUG., Question 12 on Numbers.)** Another text reads, and so forth, until: “and this sacrifice of salvation, which he had earlier called ‘for salvation.’”

**(RAB.)** He offers the lamb as a burnt offering who presents to God simplicity of heart with devotion of charity; the ewe, which displays an example of innocence; but the ram as a peace offering when he governs himself well in the way of God and subjects rebellious flesh to the rule of the soul.

**And the ewe.** He offers the ewe for sin who faithfully believes that Christ, innocent, was offered for the sin of the human race.

**And the ram.** This occurs when he trusts that Christ is the one who, through the dispensation of the flesh, reconciled heavenly and earthly things, abolishing every principality and power; whom God exalted and gave the name that is above every name, and so forth.

**VERSE 15.—And unleavened cakes:** the old law, dictated by the Holy Spirit and tempered for human benefit.

**Without leaven:** because spiritual grace in the law and in the Gospel is evident to those who understand correctly.

[Col. 0392D] **VERSE 16.—Which he shall offer.** Presenting before God the merit and labor of each person, his meditation and observance of the law, he leads him, by rewarding him, to the entrance of heavenly life, once the struggle of good works has been completed.

**VERSE 17.—But the ram:** showing him to be worthy of the reward of perpetual rest, as the ruler of himself or of others, and as an excellent leader who governed himself well and led himself along the path of God’s commandments, according to the teaching of Scripture and the grace of spiritual gifts.

**(GREG., Book 2 of the Morals, chapter 39.)** Why do Nazirites grow their hair? and so forth, until: “he completes it in the perfection of devotion.”

[Col. 0393A] **VERSE 19.—And the cooked shoulder of the ram, and the twisted cake.** The high priest causes his holy one to offer to God the strength of the work, cooked and tested in the fire of tribulation.

**And the cake:** that is, knowledge of the law, which he helps to complete in action through the gift of the Holy Spirit.

**VERSE 20.—He shall elevate:** he will present to the Father the good things that the consecrated person performs and cause him to be rewarded with an everlasting recompense.

**Of the priest:** because whatever the Nazirite has rightly desired and completed in action pertains to the priest’s glory. For he is the one who works in us both to will and to accomplish (Phil. 2).

**After these things:** that is, after right intention, a discerning promise, perfection of works, and the retribution [Col. 0393B] of reward.

**To drink:** to draw fully and freely from the spiritual gift. Hence: “You will give them drink from the torrent of your delight” (Ps. 36).

**VERSE 22.—And he spoke.** Moses signifies the law, Aaron the priesthood, and his sons the order of the Church. The Lord therefore teaches through the law how the order of priests should build up the people by preaching and strengthen them through frequent prayer and blessing.

**(RAB., in the passage cited above.)** Moses has a manifold significance, and so forth, until: “while he completes, raises, and anoints the tabernacle.”

**VERSE 24.—May he bless.** (ID.) It should be noted that in this blessing the name of the Lord is introduced three times, so that the Holy Trinity may be understood—from whom, through whom, and in whom all good things are to be sought and obtained, because [Col. 0393C] “from him and through him and in him are all things.”

**And may he guard.** (ID.) May he preserve by his grace the blessing you have received: “Unless the Lord guards the city, the guard keeps watch in vain” (Ps. 127).

**VERSE 25.—May he show.** The showing of God’s face is reconciliation and the manifestation of true salvation. Hence: “Show us your face, and we shall be saved” (Ps. 80).

**VERSE 26.—May he turn, and so forth.** The turning of the face signifies mercy, and the turning away signifies anger. Hence: “Look upon me and have mercy on me” (Ps. 119). And elsewhere: “Why do you turn your face away and forget our poverty?” (Ps. 44). We must therefore ask that he whose help we have turned away from ourselves by sinning may, through his goodness, deign to shine his face upon us, so that, rescuing us from our enemies, he may grant us perpetual peace.

**VERSE 27.—They shall invoke.** (ID.) It belongs to priests to invoke the name of the Lord; it belongs to the Lord to accomplish what is requested. Let no one, therefore, claim for himself what the Trinity alone grants to whomever it wills.

# CHAPTER VII

**VERSE 1.—And it came to pass, and so forth, the tabernacle.** (RAB. on Numbers, vol. 2.) The Church or the perfect, in whom the fragrances of virtues and prayers are burned; or the humanity of Christ, in which he offered the sacrifice of our redemption to the Father. For he himself is priest, victim, and altar, because, holding death in his power, he accepted it by his own will. Hence: “No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down, and I take it up again” (John 10).

**VERSE 2.—The princes and leaders of Israel, and so forth.** (RAB. on Numbers.) The patriarchs, prophets, and apostles, and so forth, until: “it will be done for them by my Father.”

**VERSE 3.—Six wagons.** (RAB.) The wagons that the sons of Israel offered to the Levites for transporting the tabernacle signify the temporal supports that devoted peoples provide for preachers, so that, free from care and hindrance, they may devote themselves to divine service. Thus those who proclaim the Gospel may live from the Gospel: “If we have sown spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap material things?” (1 Cor. 9).

The wagons, rightly adorned with faith and an affection for mercy so that they may be acceptable to God, are accompanied by twelve oxen. For those who labor in the service of the saints, under the yoke of apostolic teaching, do everything honorably and orderly. Or we understand the oxen as teachers who labor worthily in the field of the Lord. Concerning them it is said: “You shall not muzzle the ox while it treads out the grain” (Deut. 25; 1 Tim. 5). Those who preserve the apostolic norm by living and preaching are to be honored with double honor.

**One ox, and so forth.** (ID.) Because of the unity of faith, and so forth, until: “they ought to hasten to the tabernacle of God with the service that is due.”

**VERSE 9.—But to the sons of Kohath.** (RAB.) It was written above, and so forth, until: “not even those who seem to possess some practice and learning.”

**VERSE 10.—The leaders offered offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day when it was anointed.** Each person, according to his ability, ought to offer faith, [Col. 0394C] teaching, and good works for the advancement and honor of the Church.

**The altar was anointed; they offered their offering before it.** At the time of the Incarnation, when, after the resurrection and ascension, the disciples received the outpouring of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2).

**VERSE 11.—Let the leaders offer their gifts each day.** The preachers are leaders of the right path. Although they offer the same teaching of faith and the same examples of good works, they nevertheless distribute their offerings according to the diversity of place and time.

**VERSE 13.—A silver bowl.** These vessels have a narrow mouth and signify the narrowness of the letter of the law and the obscurity of the prophets.

The various vessels made for offering libations are the various distinctions of the word according to the varying capacities of hearers. For the wise are to be taught in one way, the foolish in another; the rich in one way, the poor in another; the healthy in one way, the weak in another; the uneducated Jewish people, beneath the shadow of the law, in one way; and the Christian, seeing the mysteries of the law explained in the truth of the Gospel and needing to be nourished into a perfect person, in another.

**VERSE 19.—A silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, and so forth.** Spiritual knowledge in the law and in the Gospel, written and proclaimed for the salvation of human beings through the ministry of spiritual grace, is signified here. Thus the sacrifice is rightly made, because nothing is so pleasing to God as meditation on the law together with the execution of the work.

**(RAB., on Numbers, vol. 2.)** The bowl, first made of glass, and so forth, until: “it was given more clearly in the New Testament.”

**VERSE 20.—A small mortar.** (RAB.) The heart of the elect, full of divine wisdom and containing the fragrances of virtues. Hence it is said: “The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul” (Acts 4).

**From ten shekels, and so forth.** (ID.) Because, with the fulfillment of the ten commandments, they emit the fragrance of teaching and prayer, so that they may deserve to receive the denarius of eternal life.

**VERSE 21.—An ox from the herd, and so forth.** (ID.) These signify various persons, and so forth, until: “we should strive always to reform our life toward better things.”

He offers an ox who expends useful labor for his neighbors in the Church of God; a ram, who directs himself and others along the way of righteousness; a yearling lamb, who is simple and innocent. All these are offered as burnt offerings solely out of love for God and desire for eternal life. He offers a goat for sin who does not cease to repent and pray for his sins. He offers two oxen as a sacrifice of peace offerings who fulfills the two commandments of charity through good works: love of God, by keeping his commandments, and care for his neighbor’s needs, on which the whole law and the prophets depend. He offers five rams, five goats, and five yearling lambs because he strongly leads the five bodily senses along the way of truth, restrains them from sins, and sets forth an example of simplicity.

**VERSE 85.—Two thousand, and so forth.** (RAB.) In the silver vessels, and so forth, until: “one does not reach that place.”

[Col. 0395C] **VERSE 86.—Twelve golden mortars.** (ID.) Each of them weighs ten shekels, and all together they amount to one hundred twenty shekels of gold. They signify the hearts of the elect, preserving knowledge of the law in all things according to apostolic teaching. For twelve times ten makes one hundred twenty, the number at which the primitive Church in Jerusalem received the Paraclete Spirit (Acts 2). Hence it follows:

**By weight, and so forth.** (ID.) The sanctuary is the Church. Following its rule of faith and understanding, we believe that everything written in the law and the prophets is beneficial to us. Whatever is thought, understood, or observed outside the unity of the Church produces the condemnation of the soul.

**VERSE 87.—Oxen, and so forth.** (ID.) The oxen, rams, and lambs included in the number twelve signify those who, whether in the office of teacher, in the leadership of some rank, or living simply, strive to do everything according to apostolic and prophetic teaching.

**Goats, and so forth.** (ID.) These are those who strive to complete their repentance according to the rule of apostolic faith.

**VERSE 88.—Oxen, and so forth.** (ID.) In these, spiritual knowledge together with the perfection of good works is signified, because the course of the day is completed in twenty-four hours. They signify that the light of knowledge and faith is necessary for every Christian.

**Sixty.** The number sixty, that is, six times ten, demonstrates the perfection of the commandments. For it is necessary that those who preside, those who are subject, and those who repent do everything according to the Church’s teaching, so that their offering may preserve the rite and order of peace offerings and that they may deserve God’s grace rather than offense.

**VERSE 89.—And when, and so forth.** (GREG., Book 33 of the Morals, chapter 21, vol. 2.) What is it that Moses, and so forth, until: “and how he graciously descends to what is lowest and powerfully returns to what is highest.”

**From the mercy seat.** Because, through the grace of divine reconciliation, after the guilt of transgression God opened for us the way of truth.

**Between the two cherubim.** Because God appeared to Moses through an angelic vision, not in his own substance. Hence: “The law was ordained through angels in the hand of a mediator” (Gal. 3). Or because through both Testaments he teaches us the faith of truth with harmonious voice; or because, through the Son, who appeared in the flesh between the two Testaments, the Father spoke to the human race.

# CHAPTER VIII

**VERSE 2.—Seven lamps.** The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, which always remained in Christ and were distributed among his members according to his will.

**(BEDA, on Numbers.)** The table and the lampstand, and so forth, until: “forbidding him to bear testimony.”

**VERSE 3.—Upon the lampstand.** Namely, Christ, the firstborn from the root of Jesse, upon whom rested the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude (Isa. 11).

**VERSE 4.—Of gold.** Because Christ alone was free from sin and illustrious in works of righteousness; his members imitate innocence and righteousness as far as they are able, and they will be perfected in the future.

**Hammered.** Because Christ was perfect God and man from conception and birth, endured the pains of suffering (2 Tim. 3), and thus reached the glory of the resurrection. All who wish to live devoutly in him, like metal expanded by hammering, reach the grace of immortality through the insults of suffering.

**The shaft.** Christ, namely, from whom the branches proceed, because from him the righteous receive whatever good they possess. Hence: “Without me you can do nothing” (John 15).

**VERSE 6.—Take the Levites from me.** Mystically, he instructs the ecclesiastical order in how it should rightly be advanced to the dignity of the priesthood.

**VERSE 7.—The hairs of their flesh.** (GREG., Book 5 of the Morals, chapter 23.) The hairs of the flesh are any superfluities of human flesh, and so forth, until: “when we penetrate the heights of contemplation.”

**They shall wash.** That is, they shall cleanse their works, so that their conduct may be pure before God and blameless before human beings.

**VERSE 8.—An ox.** The mediator of God and human beings, through whose sacrifice our sins have been erased. In the two oxen his incarnation is signified. Christ’s passion is one, but it obtained two things for us: purification from sins and sanctification, so that he might offer us to God, dead indeed in the flesh but made alive in the spirit. Hence Paul: “But you were washed; but you were sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus” (1 Cor. 6). These two oxen—one offered for sin and the other as a burnt offering—may also express two kinds of action. By one we wash away the evil things we have done through the lament of repentance; by the other, through the fruits of good works and virtues, we earn God’s grace and the reward of blessedness.

**The libation.** The sacrament of the passion, understood and treated through spiritual knowledge, is most beneficial to the faithful and most pleasing to God—provided that the Lord’s minister presents himself clean and worthy both inwardly and outwardly to receive such mysteries.

**VERSE 9.—And you shall bring them near.** The Levites are brought near before the tabernacle of the covenant when the elect are advanced to the service of the altar [Col. 0397B] according to apostolic teaching. One enters the true tabernacle (1 Tim. 3) if one has begun well according to the teaching and examples of the saints and has persevered to the end.

**VERSE 10.—The sons shall place.** Because they must offer the assent of their devotion to their election and persist in good works at their command.

**VERSE 11.—From the sons of Israel.** (BED.) The election is to be made under the testimony and knowledge of many, so that a worthy examination may be conducted and no one may be able to find fault. For they must have a good testimony even from those who are outside.

**VERSE 12.—The Levites also, and so forth.** Because the ministers of the Lord hasten, through their own labor, to consecrate the beginnings of good works to the Lord, so that they may effectively complete either the repentance that must be undertaken or the practices of virtue that must be exercised.

**VERSE 14.—You shall separate.** The minister of the Lord must not be content with popular discipline; he must be distinguished and conspicuous in conduct and teaching.

**VERSE 17.—Every firstborn in the land.** (RAB.) The firstborn of the Egyptians, and so forth, until: “and the true Levite may be suitably assigned to the divine mysteries.”

**VERSE 19.—That they may serve.** Let the ministers of the Lord see how necessary it is for them to guard the rights of their office. They must not yearn for earthly profits or pleasures, since their proper task is to serve the tabernacle and pray for the people, lest there be among them a destroying plague. Otherwise they hurl both themselves and the people into perdition, and it is said to them: “I will accept no offering from your hand” [Col. 0397D] (Mal. 1).

**VERSE 24.—From twenty-five.** (ISID., Questions on Numbers, vol. 5.) From the age of twenty-five the Levites are commanded, and so forth, until: “it is utterly extinguished in them, so that they may not remain.”

# CHAPTER IX

**VERSE 12.—Let the sons of Israel keep the Passover at its appointed time, on the fourteenth day of this month, and so forth.** (RAB.–BED.) When in the Old Testament, and so forth, until: “And: ‘Behold, I make all things new’” (Rev. 21).

**(BED.)** Then the third week, and so forth, until: “he illuminated its extremities by spiritual grace through himself.”

**(ID.)** The moon’s own turning also, and so forth, until [Col. 0398A]: “he commanded them to be witnesses of his dispensation to the ends of the earth” (Acts 1).

**(ID.)** It is fitting, moreover, that the moon, and so forth, until: “it is rightly adapted to the joy of Passover on the fifteenth day.”

[ID.] Having taken these indications of the Passover, or *phase*, from the Law, we heirs of the New Testament also attach the Lord’s Day, because it excels both by the condition of the primitive light and by the triumph of the Lord’s resurrection.

[ID.] Likewise, the seven days of the moon, up to the passage resembling: “What I say to one, I say to all” (Mark XIII).

[ID.] In the name also of the Passover, etc., up to the point that, through each stage of spiritual passage, we may extend ourselves in return toward its Giver.

[ID.] Or, in the moon’s waxing toward humanity, etc., [Col. 0398B] up to the point where it may suitably be understood.

**VERSE 6.**—“Behold, certain men were unclean because of a human soul,” etc. (AUGUSTINE, *Questions on Numbers*, question 15.) And when at the time of the Passover certain men were unclean because of a human soul, etc., up to the point that perhaps, if they had not celebrated the Passover, it would not have counted as guilt.

**VERSE 8.**—“Stand, that I may consult.” (GREGORY, *Moral Commentary*, book XXXIII, chapter 21, vol. II.) Moses frequently withdraws to the tabernacle concerning doubtful matters, leaving the crowds, etc., up to the point when, in the meditation of their mind, they are withdrawn from bodily senses.

**VERSE 10.**—“The man who is unclean because of a human soul,” etc. (ISIDORE.) It is commanded that those who lived farther away, or were unclean in soul, should celebrate the Passover in the second month, because the Gentiles, having fornicated with all the demons, were unclean and far from God. But, cleansed by a saving confession, they are commanded to pass over to the birth of Christ as though to the second month.

(RABANUS.) He is unclean in soul, etc., up to the point that, purified toward evening, he eats the lamb with unleavened bread and wild lettuce.

**VERSE 11.**—“With unleavened bread.” (RABANUS.) He eats unleavened bread who performs upright works without the corruption of vainglory, and carries out the commandments of mercy without any admixture of sin.

“With wild plants.” Because, when we receive Christ’s body, we ought to be pierced with compunction for our sins, so that the bitterness of repentance may wipe away love of a perverse life.

**VERSE 12.**—“The whole rite.” Whatever was commanded historically in the Law, the Church observes spiritually in the celebration of the Passover.

“They shall observe.” Because his words must be examined carefully, so that in the present life they may be penetrated through understanding and practice.

**VERSE 13.**—“He shall be cut off.” He instructs those who were under the Law by threatening them, lest they neglect to observe the appointed time of the Passover. He also admonishes us to celebrate the spiritual Passover in its proper time, concerning which Paul says: “Behold, now is the acceptable time,” etc. (II Corinthians VI). For whoever does not celebrate in worthy faith the redemption of the human race, accomplished through the sacrifice of the true Lamb, and does not turn his life toward better things, passing from vices to virtues during this time of mortality, will not belong at the end to the glory of the resurrection granted to Christ’s true worshipers, but will be cut off from the fellowship of the saints.

**VERSE 14.**—“If a sojourner and a newcomer are among you,” etc. (RABANUS.) He shows that there is no distinction of persons before God. Whoever, having converted to the Catholic faith and been washed in Christ’s baptism, enters the unity of the Church may share in the ecclesiastical mysteries.

**VERSE 15.**—“The cloud.” (ISIDORE.) Christ is the pillar: upright and firm, supporting our weakness, shining through the night and not shining by day, so that those who do not see may see and those who see may become blind. Christ’s sacrament is likewise manifest as by day—in the flesh, as in a cloud—but in judgment it will be as in the terror of night. For then there will be great tribulation [Col. 0399B] like fire; it will shine for the just and burn the unjust (Exodus XII).

Mystically, this signifies Christ’s incarnation: his mercy protects the tabernacle of the Church, his goodness orders its condition, and his prudence directs its passage along the way of this world.

(GREGORY, *Homily 21 on the Gospels*, vol. III.) In the fire there is terror, etc., up to the point that he infused the fire of his love into those who recognize the darkness of their sins.

**VERSE 23.**—“At the word of the Lord they pitched their tents.” This signifies the cloud, which was a sign of the divine will, like the voice of one speaking.

## CHAPTER X

[Col. 0399C]

**VERSE 2.**—“Make for yourself two silver trumpets,” etc. (ISIDORE, *On Numbers*.) By means of two trumpets the army is led, etc., up to the point that the minds of the hearers are aroused more ardently for the battles of temptation.

**VERSE 4.**—“If you sound only once.” (RABANUS, *On Numbers*.) To sound the trumpets once, etc., up to the point that all may say the same thing in the same understanding and knowledge.

**VERSE 5.**—“The first.” Because the light of faith first shone forth. Therefore, after the preachers of the Gospel had been ordered, they were first told: “Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, but go to the sheep that have perished of the house of Israel” (Matthew X); to them Christ himself preached the Gospel in person. But after the resurrection, appearing to the disciples, he said: “Go and teach all nations,” etc. (Matthew XVIII). Thus the tribe of Judah, together with the others dwelling with it toward the east, moved its camp first; afterward the others did so according to their order. For it was necessary that the primitive Church first be established in Judea, and afterward that the Gentiles from all the nations of the world be called to the faith.

**VERSE 7.**—“But when there is to be a gathering.” (RABANUS.) At the assembly of the people, etc., up to the point that we seek nothing except that what is closed may be opened.

**VERSE 8.**—“The sons, however.” The preachers preach the word of God and show the way of righteousness to their hearers, so that they may place the step of good works on the path of God’s commandments and flee the way of the wicked.

“They shall sound the trumpets.” That is, by rousing their subjects to repentance and to the compunction of tears, and by urging the hearts of their hearers to implore God’s mercy. [Col. 0400A]

**VERSE 10.**—“Whenever you have a feast.” (RABANUS.) Note that in adversity, etc., up to the passage elsewhere: “Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season,” etc. (I Timothy IV).

**VERSE 11.**—“In the second year.” (JEROME, *Letter to Fabiola*, vol. I.) At the twelfth encampment the children of Israel came to the desert of Sinai, etc., up to the point that inside they are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of uncleanness.

(GREGORY, *Pastoral Rule*, part III, admonition 18.) Often we could persuade the proud more effectively of useful things, etc., up to the point that he would bend himself through the words of the exhorter.

**VERSE 23.**—“And the ark of the covenant.” (RABANUS.) The ark of the Lord’s covenant, etc., up to the point that it shows the path of truth and righteousness to those who follow it. [Col. 0400B]

**VERSE 34.**—“The cloud also.” The divine protection by which the grace of the Holy Spirit has defended the elect from the beginning of the world and guards them for future rest.

**VERSE 35.**—“And when it was lifted up.” Following Moses’ example, the leaders of the people are urged always to commend the flock entrusted to them to the Lord, at the beginning and at the completion of their work, so that he may protect his own sheep and drive away their enemies.

## CHAPTER XI

**VERSE 1.**—“Meanwhile there arose a murmuring.” (RABANUS, *On Numbers*, vol. II.) The fire of the Lord, once kindled, devours the murmuring people, etc., up to the point that they will be burned by everlasting punishment both in soul [Col. 0400C] and in body.

**VERSE 5.**—“The melons and leeks.” (GREGORY, *Moral Commentary*, book XX, chapter 19.) The minds of the carnal, through love of the world, etc., up to the point where they groan carnally.

**VERSE 16.**—“Gather for me seventy.” (GREGORY, *Moral Commentary*, book XXIX, chapter 13.) Just as young men are often spoken of, etc., up to the point that it is clear that the old age of the mind, not of the body, is chosen.

**VERSE 17.**—“That I may come down.” (ISIDORE.) At the thirteenth encampment, etc., up to the point that it had once existed in Moses and the prophets.

“And I will take from your spirit and give it to them, so that they may support,” etc. (AUGUSTINE, *Questions on Numbers*, question 18.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that Moses would not therefore have less.

[Col. 0400D]

**VERSE 21.**—“Six hundred thousand foot soldiers of this people.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 19*.) It is asked whether Moses said this in distrust or as an inquiry, etc., up to the point when God’s sentence did not follow to punish but rather to teach.

**VERSE 24.**—“Moses therefore came and related the words of the Lord to the people, gathering.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 6 on Numbers*.) Another reading: “Moses went out,” he says, etc., and similar passages.

**VERSE 25.**—“Taking from the spirit.” (ID.) It must not be understood, etc., up to the point that its source suffered no loss through the derivation.

“When it had rested.” “And the spirit rested upon them, and they all prophesied,” etc. It is not written that the spirit rested [Col. 0401A] upon them, etc., up to the point that he set forth the praise of their life and their virtues.

(ORIGEN.) “And the spirit rested in them, and they prophesied,” etc. The spirit immediately works, etc., up to the point that it is not fitting for the presence of the Holy Spirit to be absent.

**VERSE 26.**—“But they had remained in the camp.” It was not through negligence of the Lord’s command, but through the devotion of humility, judging themselves unworthy to receive so great a gift. Therefore God, the judge of hearts, judged them worthy and displayed them as such.

**VERSE 29.**—“Why, he said, are you jealous?” (GREGORY, *Moral Commentary*, book XXIII, chapter 24.) The pious mind of pastors, etc., up to the point that he did not envy the good he possessed.

“The abundance of quail, which was little,” etc. (RABANUS, *On Numbers*.) The carnal people of the Jews, etc., up to: [Col. 0401B] “Our citizenship is in heaven” (II Corinthians X).

**VERSE 34.**—“The graves of desire.” (ISIDORE, *On Numbers*, vol. V.) The thirteenth encampment is at the graves of desire, etc., up to the point that inside they are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of uncleanness.

“They came,” etc. (JEROME, *Letter to Fabiola*.) The fourteenth encampment, etc., up to the words spoken through the prophet: “Will he who falls not rise again?” (Jeremiah VIII).

(ISIDORE.) The fourteenth encampment, etc., up to the point that he will restore her to forgiveness.

## CHAPTER XII

**VERSE 1.**—“And Miriam spoke,” etc. (ORIGEN, *Homily 7 on Numbers*.) Miriam is the Jewish people; Moses is the Law of the Lord [Col. 0401C], etc., up to the point when “there will be one flock and one shepherd” (John X).

(ID.) Because Aaron and Miriam slandered Moses, they were rebuked, etc., up to the point that leprosy follows those who disparage and speak evil.

(ID.) Everyone who also misunderstands Moses’ writings and receives the spiritual Law carnally slanders him, because he interprets the words of the Spirit in a carnal manner.

Mystically, not only the Jewish heretics who do not receive the Law and the Prophets slander Moses. They also attack him because he was a murderer, since he killed an Egyptian, and with blasphemous mouths they compose many other accusations against the other prophets. Therefore they are leprous in soul and are expelled from the Church of God. Or, they are heretics who slander their neighbors.

[Col. 0401D]

“The Ethiopian woman.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 20*.) Concerning Moses’ wife, etc., up to the point that the names of places and nations are often changed by the passage of time.

**VERSE 6.**—“If there is anyone.” (ORIGEN, cited above.) Hear how much benefit slanderers confer, etc., up to the point that God does not speak even to him in a riddle but openly.

**VERSE 8.**—“The Lord.” (ID.) Another reading: “And he sees the glory of the Lord.” Moses saw the glory of the Lord when the Lord was transfigured on the mountain, and Moses was present with Elijah and conversed with him (Luke IX). Therefore he rightly adds:

“Why, then?” (ID.) What is said to them, etc., up to the point that we should glorify him according to the greatness of our understanding.

[Col. 0402A]

**VERSE 10.**—“The cloud also withdrew.” (ID.) “And the cloud withdrew from the tabernacle,” etc. First the cloud withdrew, etc., up to the point that the leprosy of sin may appear in us.

“And when he had looked.” (ORIGEN, cited above.) Another reading: “And Aaron looked upon Miriam, and behold, Miriam was leprous.” He wishes to show by this, etc., up to the point that the Apostle recalls them to the ordinances of perfect birth: “My little children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you,” etc. (Galatians IV).

**VERSE.**—“And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: God, I beg you, heal her. The Lord answered him.” (ID.) Another reading: “And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying: Lord, I beg you, heal her,” etc. Who was more fitting to pray for the health of his people than Moses? Perhaps this was what he discussed with the Lord on the mountain of the Transfiguration (Matthew XVII), asking that, when the fullness of the Gentiles had entered, all Israel might be saved (Romans XI).

**VERSE 14.**—“If her father had spit in her face, should she not at least,” etc. Spitting in the face is a sign of repudiation. Hence the next of kin who repudiates a marriage is spit upon the face after being deprived of his sandal. Therefore Isaiah says: “All the nations are like a drop from a bucket and are counted as spittle” (Isaiah XL, according to the Septuagint). It is thus shown that this people too, like the other nations that are counted as spittle, has been rejected. For if you consider its former honor—the pontifical order, the insignia of the priests, the Levitical ministries, the majesty of the temple, and their earthly fellowship with heavenly things—what honor, what glory was that? (Romans V.) But now [Col. 0402C] they shudder in great disgrace, without a temple, without an altar, without a sacrifice, without a prophet, without a priesthood, and without heavenly visitation. Hence it is clear that the father, spitting, covered their faces with disgrace.

Therefore they are separated outside the camp for seven days, that is, through the week of this world. In the week of days, the substances of the whole visible creation appear to have been produced; then what did not exist was made. During the week of the whole world, certain mysteries—known then to God alone—are unfolded concerning what was produced. In this week, because Miriam has been separated, the camps of the children of Israel do not move, but remain enclosed in one place, and none of them advances until Miriam has been cleansed of her leprosy.

“For seven days, and the people did not move from that place.” [Col. 0402D] (ORIGEN.) Miriam is healed on the seventh day through the intervention of Aaron the high priest. But we who slander will remain leprous until the end of the world’s week, that is, until the resurrection, unless, while there is time for repentance, we are corrected by turning to Jesus and beseeching him through repentance.

## CHAPTER XIII

**VERSE 4.**—“Pharan.” (RABANUS, *On Numbers*.) It should be noted that Pharan is not the particular name of an encampment, etc., up to the point that these things are contained through the thirty-second encampment.

Pharan is interpreted as “visible mouth.” In this it may be understood that the Word became flesh, and that the invisible became visible. It may also signify that, after the end and completion of everything that had to be accomplished concerning that people had come, he then passed over and came to the one who previously had not believed that the Word had become flesh.

“Send men,” etc. (RABANUS.) Twelve scouts are sent to the holy land, etc., up to the point that its ashes are a sprinkling for atonement.

**VERSE 18.**—“Go up toward the southern region.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 21*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that there was a somewhat lower place there, from whose valley the cluster was taken.

**VERSE 24.**—“Which they carried,” etc. (ISIDORE, *On Numbers*, vol. V.) Two men bring a cluster from the promised land on a piece of wood, etc., up to the point that neither Christ can exist without the Law nor the Law without Christ.

**VERSE 24.**—“Also from the pomegranates and figs,” [Col. 0403B] etc. These signify the Law, because neither Christ can exist without the Law nor the Law without Christ.

**VERSE 26.**—“The scouts of the land after forty days,” etc. (ISIDORE, cited above.) The scouts who were sent to the fertile land terrified the people, etc., up to the point that the melons of vices and lusts are withered by corruption.

**VERSE 27.**—“Into the desert of Pharan, which is at Kadesh.” (RABANUS.) The desert of Pharan contains eighteen encampments, etc., up to the point that they are forbidden to cross the Jordan.

## CHAPTER XIV

**VERSE 7.**—“The land,” etc. (ORIGEN, *Homily 7 on Numbers*.) What is this land, holy indeed and good, but inhabited by the impious? etc., up to the point that they are driven away as we enter it, and fall as we ascend.

**VERSE 9.**—“Do not fear the people of this land, for we can consume them as bread.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 23 on Numbers*.) Caleb and Joshua son of Nun, speaking to the people, etc., up to the point that these people recognize the Lord as creator, arranger, and dispenser of the ages and of all things.

**VERSE 12.**—“Therefore I will strike them.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 8 on Numbers*.) This threat is not wrathful but prophetic, etc., up to the point that he therefore intercedes more earnestly for that people.

(ID.) “Therefore I will strike them.” This threat is made by the Lord, etc., up to the point that, after this people has been rejected, he may raise up another people.

**VERSE 31.**—“The little ones.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 8*.) “But their children who are here with me, whoever do not know good or evil,” etc. Our fathers were that earlier people, etc., up to the words: “If you remain in goodness,” etc.

**VERSE 34.**—“A year for a day.” (ID.) As though a year were assigned for each day, etc., up to the point that judgment has been given to no one except him to whom the Father has entrusted all judgment (John V).

(ID.) Someone may perhaps deny that this accords with God’s goodness, etc., up to the point that he no longer permits the soul to be wounded by sin.

(ID.) I will add something else, etc., up to the point that we may trust all the more that our advocate Jesus will obtain forgiveness for us from the Father.

**VERSE 40.**—“We are ready.” (RABANUS, *On Numbers*.) O extraordinary boldness of the human mind, etc., up to the point that thus we shall receive the joys of the heavenly homeland promised to us.

## CHAPTER XV

**VERSE 4.**—“A sacrifice,” etc. The faith of Christ’s incarnation, which is most fully commended in the Law, or observance of the Decalogue.

(RABANUS, *On Numbers*.) The Law commands that in private and public sacrifices, etc., up to the point that it is one-sixth of a *congius*.

(ID.) It is therefore commanded through each kind of animal, etc., up to the point that every folly and cunning is abominable to God.

**VERSE 6.**—“And rams.” (ID.) In the offering of a ram, two-tenths of fine flour are offered; of oil and wine, one-third of a *hin*. Because the ram signifies the order of rulers, it is rightly offered with two-tenths, since anyone entrusted with the office of ruler must hold to the Decalogue of the Law in understanding and practice. One-third of a *hin* of oil and wine is supplied when charity, mercy, and the grace of spiritual teaching are bestowed by him upon his subjects.

**VERSE 8.**—“When you make a burnt offering from cattle,” etc. (ID.) In the offering of an ox, three-tenths of fine flour and half a *hin* of oil or wine are used, etc., up to the point that they may hope, by God’s grace, to be perfected in themselves in heavenly blessedness.

“When you come into the land,” etc. (RABANUS.) When anyone enters the present Church through faith, etc., up to the point [Col. 0404C] from whom the supplement of perfection is hoped.

**VERSE 22.**—“But if through,” etc. (AUGUSTINE, *Question 24*.) What is commanded concerning how sins are expiated, etc., up to the point that these are distinguished from the sins of those who sin willingly.

**VERSE 24.**—“He shall offer a young bull.” (RABANUS.) The children of Israel offer a young bull from the herd as a burnt offering, etc., up to the point that he was heard because of his reverence.

**VERSE 28.**—“The priest.” Christ, who entered once for all into the holy places through his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption (Hebrews V).

**VERSE 30.**—“But the soul,” etc. (AUGUSTINE, *Question 25 on Numbers*.) Another reading: “Any soul that has sinned,” etc., up to the point that it would now take too long to discuss.

(ISIDORE, *On Numbers*, vol. V.) The impious criticize the fact that, by God’s command, the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath was slaughtered so atrociously by the whole people, [Col. 0404D] etc., up to the point that he is judged by spiritual persons.

**VERSE 38.**—“Fringes.” (ID., cited above.) The children of Israel are commanded to place them at the four corners, etc., up to the point that we should do everything for the glory of God.

## CHAPTER XVI

**VERSE 12.**—“Would you call Dathan?” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 26 on Numbers*.) What does it mean that Dathan and Abiram, summoned by Moses during the rebellion, etc., up to the point that they did not say, “We will not go up,” but “We are not going up,” according to a certain manner of speech?

**VERSE 26.**—“Withdraw from the tents.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 27*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that “the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father” (Matthew XIII).

[Col. 0405A]

(ISIDORE, *On Numbers*, vol. V.) Through Dathan, Abiram, and Korah, etc., up to the point that they will perish in the eternal fire prepared as punishment.

“And they descended.” (AUGUSTINE, *Question 29*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that they are kept in reserve to be punished as though in the prisons of hell.

**VERSE 37.**—“Command Eleazar.” (ID., *Question 30*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that through them an example was given to the others concerning what they should fear.

“Let him take the censers.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 9 on Numbers*.) Korah represents those who rise up against ecclesiastical faith and the teaching of truth, etc., up to the words: “For they have been sanctified and offered to the Lord.”

(ID.) It can also be understood in another way, etc., up to the point that the courage of their spirit would not have shone so magnificently if the cowardice of the others had not been exposed.

[Col. 0405B]

**VERSE 38.**—“Because,” etc. (AUGUSTINE, *Question 30 on Numbers*.) As for the placement around the altar, etc., up to the point that those who attend less carefully understand that it happened in the same order in which it is narrated.

**VERSE 39.**—“He took.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 9 on Numbers*.) Nothing is useless before God, etc., up to the point that they would perish together with the ashes of all the others.

**VERSE 40.**—“As the Lord suffered.” (ID.) An example is also given to posterity, lest anyone, through the presumption of a proud spirit, seize for himself the priestly office not given by God. Rather, let him yield to the one whom neither human ambition, corrupt favor, nor condemnable bribery has brought forward.

[Col. 0405C]

**VERSE 43.**—“Moses and Aaron.” (ID.) In Sodom, indeed, etc., up to the point that through them we can escape destruction.

“The cloud covered.” (ID.) For previously we do not read that the cloud had covered the tabernacle, etc., up to the dangers of the sea and rivers, etc. (II Corinthians XI).

**VERSE 41.**—“Withdraw.” (ID.) Moses and Aaron are therefore commanded, etc., up to the point that those who are sent into eternal fire are dead, while those who are sent into the kingdom are alive.

**VERSE 48.**—“And standing between.” (GREGORY.) Aaron, to appease God’s anger, took the censer and stood between the living and the dead, because it is the priest’s task to pour out prayer to God, both for the righteous, that they may not fall, and for sinners, that they may rise again. Hence: “Let my prayer enter like incense in your presence” (Psalm LXXXVII).

(ISIDORE.) Aaron, taking the censer, ran to meet the plague. Standing in the midst of the living and the dead, he excludes the deadly blow by his interposition, like a kind of wall. This priest is Christ, who, seeing death’s ruin in the world, came from the highest heaven to meet it, and came forward like a giant to run the course. He stood between the living and the dead, because he was born and died; and thus, taking the censer of his passion and presenting it as a sweet fragrance, he suspended the destruction of eternal fire and endured the hostile death.

“And the plague ceased.” (ORIGEN.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that an earthy and terrestrial understanding does not grasp the mysteries.

[Col. 0406A]

Our body is also called an earthen vessel, or the letter of the Law, in what the Apostle says: “We have this treasure in earthen vessels” (II Corinthians IV). For while we are placed in the body, the Lord bestows the treasure of grace through the Holy Spirit; and in the words of the Law, which are despised because they seem not to have been explained by any grammatical art, the treasure of God’s wisdom and knowledge is hidden.

## CHAPTER XVII

**VERSE 1.**—“From all the leaders.” Every leader has a staff, because without it he cannot govern the people. Hence Paul, because he was a leader of the people, said: “What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love?” (I Corinthians IV).

[Col. 0406B]

(ORIGEN.) It is necessary for all the leaders of the tribes to have staffs, etc., up to the point that he found an abundance of priestly fruits together with nuts.

**VERSE 5.**—“The staff will blossom.” (ORIGEN, cited above.) God promised one fruit on the staff and gave several, etc., up to the point that these things are contained in wisdom alone.

**VERSE 8.**—“He found that the staff had blossomed,” etc. (ORIGEN, cited above.) When Aaron’s priesthood, etc., up to the point that our bodies still differ from the glory of the resurrection until the end of the world.

(ID.) The dry staff blossoms, etc., up to the point that the body will blossom in the resurrection.

“The staff.” (GREGORY, *Moral Commentary*, book IV, chapter 29.) The flesh of Christ, cut off and mortified from the root of Jesse, etc., up to the crown of martyrs and the grace of the self-controlled.

[Col. 0406C]

“Swelling,” etc. (ORIGEN.) In this way, indeed, etc., up to the point that, according to Scripture, it extends to a thousand generations.

(ORIGEN, cited above.) We can also understand in this way those things, etc., up to the point that they are charity, joy, peace, and the other virtues (Galatians V).

## CHAPTER XVIII

(RABANUS, *On Numbers*, vol. II.)

**VERSE 1.**—“You and your sons,” etc. Another reading, etc., up to the point that he says it belongs to the priest.

(ORIGEN, *Homily 10 on Numbers*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that the remission of sins is signified.

(ID.) Jesus, our high priest, etc., up to the point that God knows we are not fit for martyrdom.

(ID.) It must be asked how some are called holy, etc., up to the point that he is holy who cures his sin through the high priest.

**VERSE 7.**—“But you and your sons.” (ID., *Homily 16*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that, if we cultivate them well, they will bear the fruit of life for us.

“But you and your sons.” Allegorically: the more perfect members of the Church, namely the holy teachers, whose office is to handle the divine sacraments with their hands, to examine the sacred vessels—that is, the mystical words of Scripture—and bring them to understanding (II Chronicles XXVI). Let the rest of the multitude meditate carefully on what they can grasp and what the teachers’ discernment commands.

“If anyone from outside,” etc. Not from the tribe of Levi. Uzziah [Col. 0407A], because he usurped the priesthood, was struck with leprosy, although he was from the tribe of Judah.

**VERSE 8.**—“The Lord spoke,” etc. (RABANUS, *On Numbers*, vol. II.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that, although it is always eaten, it always remains—indeed, it increases.

“Of the firstfruits.” Literal firstfruits are consumed; spiritual firstfruits are preserved. For the more abundantly you take in the word of God, the more it will abound.

“Everything that is sanctified by the children of Israel.” (ORIGEN, *Homily 11*.) Another reading, etc., up to the point that it is not sanctified and is not received among the firstfruits.

(ORIGEN.) According to the literal sense, he seems to exclude proselytes, etc., up to the point that they make fathers enter the Church.

(ID.) It is also commanded that every male appear three times a year, but not every female (Exodus XXIII).
