Others say that the Cherethites were appointed to punish the guilty, while the Pelethites were appointed to defend the innocent.

**Moreover.** The sons of David are the faithful of Christ, whom the holy Church bears for him. They are “a chosen race, a royal priesthood” (I Peter II).

**First at hand.** Because through good works they merit for themselves the kingdom of heaven; they are nearer to God in proportion as they are holier.

## CHAPTER XIX

### VERSE 1

**Ammon.** (RABANUS.) It is interpreted as ..., up to the point where it says: “His face is against those who do evil” (Psalm XXXIII).

## CHAPTER XX

### VERSE 1

**He gathered.** (RABANUS.) Joab began the war; David completed it. Christ wages war when the order of preachers opposes the powers of the world with faith, but the end of the combat and the triumph are attributed to Christ, who works in us both the willing and the accomplishing (Philippians II). He took for himself the crown that he had taken from the devil, namely the faithful who surround him like a crown. Hence: “You will bless the crown of the year with your goodness” (Deuteronomy VII).

### VERSE 2

**The crown, etc.** (JEROME.) Because he purified it by smelting, according to the Law. The Hebrews relate—since it was unlawful for a Jewish man to receive anything of gold or silver from idols, because the Law forbids idolatry—that Ittai the Hittite, who had come to David from among the Philistines, snatched the crown from the head of Milcom, so that it would be lawful for a Jew to take it from the hand of a man, whereas it was not lawful to take it from the head of an idol.

**The war.** (RABANUS.) It should be noted that in Paralipomenon three principal wars of David are read, etc., up to: “In God we shall do valiantly,” etc. (Psalm LIX).

### VERSE 5

**Another war.** (The same author.) In the Book of Kings it is written: “The third was at Gob against the Philistines, in which Adeodatus son of Saltus, the cloth-worker, a Bethlehemite, struck down Goliath of Gath,” etc. (II Kings XXI). Gob, etc., up to the point where the Hebrews, however, consider Arapha to be the mother of the giants, Orpah, Naomi’s daughter-in-law.

## CHAPTER XXI

### VERSE 5

**And it was found, etc.** (RABANUS.) In the Book of Kings it is written as follows: “There were found from Israel eighty thousand valiant men, and from Judah fifty thousand fighting men.” The Hebrews assert that this number was discovered by Joab, but that the writer did not wish to show more than what is written in Samuel and in the Book of Kings, where only those who survived the slaughter are included.

### VERSE 7

**And he struck.** He means the death that first came as the cause of sin. It spread among the people because the shepherd’s life often sins on account of the flock’s wrongdoing. David, lifted up by pride, sinned by numbering the people, and the people received the punishment, because the hearts of rulers are disposed according to the merits of their peoples. The just Judge punished the vice of the sinner through the punishment of the people, on whose account he had sinned. But because David, in his own will, was not free from the fault of pride, he received the vengeance due to his fault. Thus the punishment that struck the people bodily also cast down the ruler through grief of heart.

**I have sinned greatly, etc.** In the Book of Kings it is written as follows, etc., up to the point where David, bound to do this, offended God.

### VERSE 13

**And he said.** If he chose famine, he would seem to act against others, because, possessing much grain, he would not suffer want together with them. If he chose to be defeated by enemies for three months, he himself, having mighty men around him, would fear nothing while the army was subjected to death. Therefore he chose a suffering common to himself and to others, in which the fear would be equal for all.

### VERSE 14

**Seventy thousand men.** (RABANUS.) The heads and elders of the people were counted. The Hebrews further assert that as many thousands were killed from the whole people as the number written in Paralipomenon exceeds the number in Kings. They say that in Paralipomenon both those who remained and those who were killed were counted, whereas in Kings only the living were counted.

### VERSE 18

**And he built an altar to the Lord God on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.** (RABANUS.) It is fitting that when David wished to appease the Lord, he was ordered to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah or Ornan. For God is not appeased by a human being unless that person establishes for him, in the ark of the heart, through the light of right faith and true love, an altar of humility upon which to offer a sacrifice of praise.

## Verse 25

Therefore David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold, of the finest weight, for the site, and built there an altar to the Lord, etc. In the Book of Kings it is written thus, etc., up to the point where Solomon afterward built it and its courts.

# CHAPTER XXII

## Verse 2

**“That they might be gathered together.”** (RAB.) From the Church Christ chose the craftsmen of his house, who would hew and polish the rough morals of human beings, so that in the spiritual building they might be joined to one another through the various bonds of faith and charity. Hence: “For this reason I hewed them by the prophets, and slew them by the words of my mouth” (Hosea 6).

[Col. 0658A]

## Verse 3

**“Iron.”** He ordered the firmness of faith through sacred doctrines, so that those entering the Church might be pierced by the goads of fear and thus be mutually joined by the faith of love and fellowship. Hence: “Pierce my flesh with your fear” (Psalm 118). And elsewhere: “Jerusalem, which is built as a city whose fellowship is in itself,” etc. (ibid. 122).

**“Bronze.”** The resonant readings and spiritual songs which the holy Fathers prepared for the instruction of the Church and for Christ, the true peacemaker.

## Verse 4

**“Also timber.”** Men distinguished for their virtues, whom they instructed by way of example or inserted into their writings.

**“Sidonians and Tyrians.”** Because through preachers chosen from the Gentiles such men came to the knowledge of the Church.

[Col. 0658B]

## Verse 5

**“He is a child and delicate.”** In the time of the Old Testament, knowledge of Christ’s incarnation was obscure; there was also a small number of the faithful, who are members of Christ.

**“He prepared the expenses.”** Moses prepared the expenses of the Lord’s house when he said: “O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, except that you fear the Lord your God, that you walk in his ways,” etc., and in other similar passages.

## Verse 8

**“Much.”** This signifies that the Jews, because of their carnal observance of the law and their bloody works, could not prepare a spiritual building for the Lord; or because they had hands polluted with the blood of Christ and of the prophets. Hence: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you” [Col. 0658C] (Matthew 23).

## Verse 14

**“One hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver.”** (RAB.) The Fathers of the Old Testament inserted depth of meaning and elegance of expression into their writings.

**“Talents.”** The talent surpasses the other weights; it signifies both the greatness and the perfection of a matter.

## Verse 15

**“Craftsmen, stonecutters, and masons,” etc.** (RAB.) The preachers, who are called stonecutters, masons, craftsmen of wood, and by many other names, because the preachers’ teaching is shaped according to the capacity of their hearers. The wise, the foolish, the proud, and the humble must be taught in different ways.

## Verse 17

**“David also commanded all the leaders of Israel”** [Col. 0658D] **“to assist Solomon,” etc.** This signifies that the law and the prophets teach with firm authority that those who preside in the Church through holiness and virtue should assist the true Solomon in his building—namely, by teaching and by acting. Hence: “Worship the Lord in his holy court” (Psalm 18).

**“A sanctuary for the Lord God, so that the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the vessels consecrated to the Lord might be brought into the house that is being built,” etc.** “The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom” (Wisdom 7). In this house the ark rests—that is, faith in Christ’s incarnation.

# CHAPTER XXIII

## Verse 1

**“Therefore David,” etc.** After the completion [Col. 0659A] of the Old Testament, the incarnation of the Savior followed, whose kingdom will have no end. Hence: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son” (Galatians 4).

**“And they were counted.”** Those who perform the Lord’s ministry must preserve faith in the holy Trinity and the fulfillment of the commandments. Hence: “Thirty-eight thousand men were found.” For whoever serves God with sound faith and right conduct to the end will attain the grace of the resurrection and eternal blessedness, which are signified by the number eight.

**“Twenty-four.”** Because true ministers of light must persevere and not turn aside from the way of righteousness. For through twenty-four hours the whole circuit of the world is illumined and the shadow of darkness driven away. Hence the seventy-two disciples were sent to preach, because faith in the holy Trinity together with works of light is sufficient for righteousness: three times twenty and four times three make seventy-two, a number which embraces the diversity of languages and the sequence of the books of both Testaments.

**“Of the overseers.”** No one ought to seek the dignity of this order unless he is devoted to perfection and teaching. For the world was made in the number six, and the human being was created on the sixth day, on which he was also redeemed.

(RAB.) Because the law and the prophets, etc., up to “and patiently endure all things, bitter and angry at his sins.”

## Verse 25

**“For David said: ‘The Lord God has given rest,’” etc.** (ID.) While the children of Israel were in the desert, etc., up to “but the Gospel is stable and [Col. 0659C] fixed.”

## Verse 28

**“And they shall be under the hand of the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house,” etc.** So that the lesser may learn to obey the greater, and the greater, assisted by the lesser, may perform their office more worthily—as happens in the Church today.

**“In the chambers and in the place of purification.”** In the halls or rooms where the Levites and priests live. The ministers of the true temple likewise ought carefully to guard the entrance, admit those who are worthy, and repel the unworthy.

## Verse 29

**“For the heated fine flour and for the roasted grain,” etc.** Namely, the ears of the firstfruits, which were roasted and whose grains were eaten; these are commonly called *grancae*. In some manuscripts it reads: “For the heated fine flour.” In others, only “for the heated”; but [Col. 0659D] in Hebrew it reads “for roasting.”

# CHAPTER XXIV

## Verse 2

**“And he performed the priesthood.”** (RAB.) This may be understood through Eleazar, Aaron’s elder son, etc., up to “because there are more children of the deserted woman than of her who has a husband.”

## Verse 4

**“By sixteen families.”** The number eight has been doubled. In the law carnal circumcision is celebrated on the eighth day; in the Gospel, however, there is at present the circumcision of hearts, and in the future that of bodies.

## Verse 6

**“And he recorded them.”** (RAB.) The order of preachers, etc., up to “and is rightly reckoned under the name of righteousness.”

[Col. 0660A]

## Verse 7

**“The lot went out.”** If anyone thinks that God must be consulted in necessity by means of lots, following the example of the apostles, let him observe that the apostles did this after gathering the full number of the brothers and first pouring out prayers to God.

**“The first was Joiarib, the second,”** etc. David distributed the Levitical tribe and the priestly order into twenty-four lots, showing that the Church fully possesses the priestly and royal dignity and perfectly preserves both the teaching of the law and that of the Gospel; or, alternatively, the perfection of works, commended by the number six, and the brightness of evangelical preaching, figured by the number four. For four times six makes twenty-four.

# CHAPTER XXV

## Verse 1

**“Therefore David and the officers of the army separated them for service,” etc.** (RAB.) Because our true David, King and Lord, etc., up to “and, rising above every desire for earthly things, renders worthy praise.”

## Verse 7

**“All the teachers.”** These are those who today explain the canons of the divine books in an evangelical sense. For four times seventy-two makes two hundred eighty-eight. There is no doubt that the books of the Old and New Testaments number seventy-two. Therefore whoever performs a divine office should devote himself to evangelical teaching, attending to the four principal virtues, and should intend to shape according to its rule whatever he has learned or taught.

# CHAPTER XXVI

## Verse 2

**“Meshelemiah.”** (RAB.) His name is interpreted as “the Lord repaying,” and he signifies the order of the apostles and the first teachers, to whom the eastern gate—that is, the primitive Church—is entrusted, and to whom the promises made to the ancient Fathers have been restored.

**“Zechariah.”** His name is interpreted as “remembrance of the Lord,” and he signifies the teachers of the Gentiles, because they were appointed by the first preachers to preach. Hence, while the apostles were praying and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: “Set apart for me Paul and Barnabas” (Acts 3).

## Verse 4

**“Obed-edom.”** “Red one”: those who were born in servitude and, drenched in the redness of Christ’s blood, openly bore their guilt; they are rightly restored to their former rank through the condescension of teachers. Hence Paul: “I have made myself the servant of all, that I might win the more” (1 Corinthians 9).

[Col. 0660D]

## Verse 15

**“To the south.”** (RAB.) The southern gate signifies the Jewish people, illumined by the law and the prophets and near to receiving the warmth of faith and the light of wisdom.

## Verse 16

**“To the west, beside the gate,” etc.** The western region signifies the end of the world, in which the persecution of Antichrist will occur: “Iniquity will abound, and the love of many will grow cold” (Matthew 24). The gatekeepers of this gate are the teachers of that time, who strengthen the Church by teaching and exhortation. Hence *Sephim* is interpreted as “humble” or “of the plain,” and *Hosa* as “divining.” For in persecution the Church will be humbled, and in the field of wantonness it will be disordered. But in the action of the perfect it will be raised up, as is foretold by the divine utterances [Col. 0661A]: “The words are closed and sealed until the appointed time” (Daniel 12).

## Verse 17

**“Six Levites, and four toward the north each day,” etc.** The number six signifies the good work of God’s ministries; the number four, evangelical teaching and the fullness of the principal virtues.

**“Two by two.”** He says that the gatekeepers are two by two in the chambers and on the road, because whether they attend to the care of their hearts in the chambers or explain God’s word outwardly on the road, they must keep entirely the two commandments of charity and the rule of both Testaments.

## Verse 24

**“The sons of Moses,” etc.** These, according to Josephus, were especially honored by David and were placed over the treasuries. They signify teachers from the Jews, to whom the ornament of the Church—that is, the beauty of the soul—is entrusted.

[Col. 0661B]

## Verse 25

**“His brothers also, Eliezer.”** He shows that the gifts of rulers are the treasures of the saints; for whatever they offered to their enemies, they donated for the equipment of the temple. Whoever, by laboring well, acquires some virtue or good work should attribute the good to God, not to himself. Hence: “Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory” (Psalm 113).

## Verse 29

**“But over the Izharites was Chenaniah,” etc.** These are those who humbly and obediently receive with devoted minds whatever they hear from their teachers in the Church; and although they cannot teach by speech, they display the doctrine of virtues by their actions.

## Verse 30

**“The Israelites beyond the Jordan toward the west,” etc.** The Israelites who received their possession beyond the Jordan signify those who, content with moderation, do not seek the stronghold of virtues by crossing beyond the turbulence of this age, yet do not neglect to exercise God’s commandments in action. Since no one does these things except by God’s gift, their leader is called *Asabias*, that is, “the Lord doing,” so that they may say with the prophet: “You have wrought all our works in us” (Psalm 26).

## Verse 31

**“Now the chief of the Hebronites was Jeriah, according to their families and kindreds.”** David began to reign in Hebron; he signifies those who begin well to conduct themselves and prepare David’s kingdom during their life. Among the Hebronites, Jeriah—“fearing the Lord”—is chief, because “the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom” (Psalm 110). *Hebron* is interpreted as “marriage”; for whoever fears progresses so that he may love and cast out fear (1 John 4).

# CHAPTER XXVII

## Verse 24

**“He was not entered in the records.”** (RAB.) Because, when anger intervened, the number was thrown into confusion, and they were not distributed into ministries according to it.

## Verse 25

**“Over the treasuries,” etc.** (ID.) The treasure of Christ is knowledge and the wisdom of virtue; from these he honors those who serve him. Azmoth is placed over them; his name is interpreted as “strong in death,” for a man’s teaching is recognized through patience. Hence: “The patient man is better than the strong” (Proverbs 16). Azmoth is also the son of Adiel, whose name means “my father is God.” Whatever virtues the saints possess, they attribute to God.

[Col. 0662A]

**“Over these treasuries.”** He is rightly preferred over the treasuries of the true Solomon in cities, villages, and towers who, through faith and works, prefers the dignity of the name Jonathan and of his father Uzziah. For *Jonathan* means “house of God,” and *Uzziah* means “strength of the Lord.” Whoever receives the light of knowledge by God’s gift and firmly preserves uprightness of faith in action rightly receives care of the churches of God.

## Verse 26

**“Ezri the son of Chelub.”** *Ezri* means “helped by the Lord”; *Shemaiah*, “hearing the Lord”; *Zabdiah*, “vehement” or “abundant fruit.” Whoever hears the Lord’s commandments, assisted by his mercy, gathers an abundant fruit of good work unto eternal life.

## Verse 28

**“The olive groves and fig orchards that were in the plains,” etc.** These contain olive trees and fig trees, and they signify gatherings of saints who possess the oil of mercy in their breast and the sweetness of gentleness amid mortality. These virtues are in the plains—that is, openly and readily available to all—and they seek in their hearers not partiality but uprightness of good will.

**“Baal-hanan the Gederite.”** Baal-hanan, whose name means “having grace,” is placed over the olive groves and fig orchards. For the abundance of good works is given by God’s grace. Joash, whose name means “hoping” or “the Lord’s strength,” guards the storehouses of oil, because no one reaches the reward except one who, through strength of mind, advances toward the heavenly kingdom in the confidence of hope.

## Verse 29

**“Shaphat.”** His name means “I judged.” He is the son of Abdi, that is, “of the father of grace,” and signifies the apostles, appointed by the Lord over the other teachers [Col. 0662C]. To them it is said: “You also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Matthew 19).

## Verse 30

**“Over the camels, Ubil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys, Jadias.”** These animals are misshapen and unclean, and they signify the Gentiles, distorted by sin and unclean through lust. Yet, coming into the kingdom of our David, they have as teachers Ubil and Jadias, who, scorning philosophy and the empty deceit of the world, chose the simplicity of the Gospel as humble and despised men. Hence: “If anyone among you seems to be wise, let him become foolish” (1 Corinthians 3).

## Verse 32

**“Jonathan.”** (RAB.) When Jonathan was, etc., up to: “Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, except upon the humble and quiet one who trembles at my words?” [Col. 0662D]

**“Ahithophel”** (2 Samuel 16). Later, corrupted by desire, he plotted David’s death with Absalom. His name is interpreted as “my brother falling,” or “bursting in,” or “plotting.” He is Judas Iscariot, who was familiar with the Lord among the apostles but afterward, corrupted by greed among the Jews, earned the ruin of perpetual death by plotting his death; according to the Book of Kings, he also hanged himself with a noose. Ahithophel may also signify the Jews, who were once most beloved through the privilege of the Fathers and most illustrious through converse with God, but afterward, plotting death against Christ, were destroyed by the Romans in their own house, just as Ahithophel was—that is, in Jerusalem.

[Col. 0663A]

## Verse 33

**“Hushai.”** That is, “Ethiopian” and “faithful to David”; he signifies the Gentiles in every respect, concerning whom it is said: “The people whom I did not know served me; at the hearing of the ear they obeyed me” (Psalm 17).

## Verse 34

**“After Ahithophel was Jehoiada.”** When Judas transgressed, the twelfth place did not remain vacant; rather, Matthias, “humble and faithful,” succeeded him—one who knows the grace of God and humbly preserved the grace he had received as God’s gift. For *Jehoiada* is interpreted as “knowing” or “recognizing,” and *Benaiah* as “builder of the Lord.” Whoever is chosen by God’s grace as an apostle is established in that dignity by recognition of sound faith. Abiathar, who for a time was among David’s counselors but, in the election, defected with Joab against Solomon, signifies those who, corrupted by desire, do not preserve the rank of their dignity which they received from the Lord [Col. 0663B]. For if they do not remain in the prison of repentance according to the fear represented by Ahithophel, they will be punished forever by the true Solomon.

**“Joab.”** That is, “enemy”; he signifies those whose person is addressed in the words: “I directed myself toward all your commandments; I hated every way of iniquity” (Psalm 118). Elsewhere it is said to them: “Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect” (Matthew 5). For *Joab* is also interpreted as “the same father.”

# CHAPTER XXVIII

## Verse 1

**“With the eunuchs, and the powerful and exceedingly strong men in the army of Jerusalem.”** (RAB.) The law prohibits Israelites from being castrated, and foreigners are not ordinarily admitted to secret counsel. But they explain that in this passage “eunuchs” are called those who, alienated from the activities of the world, devoted themselves to prayer and reading; they had wives not for the sake of lust but for the begetting of offspring. Josephus calls them Essenes.

## Verse 11

**“Now David gave,” etc.** David the Psalmist and the other Fathers of the Old Testament represented through figures and riddles all the things that the true peacemaker would accomplish in the Church: how all nations would gain entry into the Church through faith and the baptismal rite; what the future state of the Church would be; what the perfection of the saints would be; and how each person would receive his reward in the heavenly kingdom according to his merits, through its various chambers and halls, because in the kingdom of God there are many dwellings.

## Verse 17

**“And the little lions.”** (RAB.) Neither in Exodus, in the construction of the tabernacle, etc., up to “we have touched upon.”

[Col. 0663D]

(ID.) The Hebrews relate that the model of the temple and its vessels shown to Moses on the mountain came to Joshua, then to the judges, to Eli, to Samuel, to David, and finally to Solomon. Or the hand of the Lord is the Son, through whose gift David and the other saints received whatever they brought forth concerning the structure of the holy Church.

# CHAPTER XXIX

## Verse 6

**“Therefore they promised,” etc.** (RAB.) Whoever has learned to rule himself and others well, etc., up to “building upon it wood, hay, and straw, will suffer loss.”

## Verse 10

**“And he blessed the Lord,” etc.** The congregation of the faithful, admonished by the writings of the prophets and stirred by the words and examples of the holy Fathers, sings praises and hymns to God, offering the sacrifices of devout confession and the fruitful works of holy conduct [Col. 0664B].

## Verse 22

**“And they ate and drank before him,” etc.** (RAB.) This is the joy and purpose of the saints: to guard themselves from future hunger through works of virtue, and to feast and rejoice in the sight of God.

**“They anointed Solomon the son a second time,” etc.** Because Christ, in both royal and priestly dignity, is celebrated by all the faithful with sound faith and devout confession. *Solomon* is interpreted as “peaceful,” and *Zadok* as “just.” Christ is our peace, who made both one; he is the just Lord and loves righteousness: “the Judge of the living and the dead” (Ephesians 2). Every faithful person first anoints him as king and priest when, in the profession of baptism, he confesses the true king and priest. He anoints him a second time when, by teaching and acting, he proclaims the same to others [Col. 0664C]. Hence: “Your name is oil poured out” (Song of Songs 1).

## Verse 28

**“And he died in a good old age, full of days and riches and glory,” etc.** This signifies ending the present life with an abundance of virtues and works of light, worthy of future rest and the glory of the heavenly kingdom. Abraham likewise died in a good old age, of perfect maturity, and full of days. Isaac was gathered to his people, full of days. Joseph died in a good old age after completing one hundred ten years of his life, and was embalmed with spices. Moses died at the age of one hundred twenty; his eye was not dim, nor were his teeth loosened. “Men of blood and deceit shall not halve their days” [Col. 0664D] (Psalm 54). They seem to themselves to spend their days in prosperity, yet in an instant they descend to the underworld (Job 21).

[Col. 0663]

# THE SECOND BOOK OF CHRONICLES (G)*

# CHAPTER I

[Col. 0663D]

## Verse 1

**“So Solomon was strengthened,” etc.** (RAB.) When, by his death, he triumphed over the one who possessed the power of death and acquired for himself the kingdom of all things. Hence: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (Matthew 28).

## Verse 3

**“Gibeon,” etc.** It was the metropolitan city of the Hivites; it fell to the lot of Benjamin and was assigned to the Levites. It is therefore surprising that Josephus says that Solomon came to Hebron to sacrifice at the bronze altar which Moses had made—unless perhaps he wished that Hebron itself should be understood as the high place of Gibeon, because Solomon first reigned there. For *Gibeon* is interpreted as “height” or “the hill of a kinsman.”

[Col. 0665A]

## Verse 10

**“Give me wisdom,” etc.** He does not ask God for gold, riches, or earthly glory, but that he may know how to rule and judge God’s people. If the ruler of bodies chose this, how much more should rulers of souls choose it, so that they may show God’s people the entrance into faith and the departure toward hope.

## Verse 13

**“From the high place,” etc.** This signifies the ark, in which were the tablets of the covenant. For it was written above: “The tabernacle of the Lord which Moses had made in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time on the high place of Gibeon,” etc. (1 Chronicles 21). After David brought the ark of the Lord into his house, it remained there until the temple was built.

**“And twelve thousand horsemen.”** This number signifies the time of grace, in which apostolic teaching instructs the people of the New Testament. It is fitting that Solomon’s chariots and horsemen are counted by the number forty or twelve, because through both Testaments holy men, instructed in the sacred Scriptures, are fitted for God’s service; the supreme charioteer himself governs them at his command.

## Verse 17

**“For six hundred shekels of silver.”** Through the preaching of teachers, people are brought into the service of the true Solomon so that they may come to know the truth of faith. Six hundred—that is, sixty times ten—signifies the perfection of evangelical teaching, in which the perfection of the law is entirely contained, especially since our Redeemer suffered on the sixth day and completed everything written about him in the law and the prophets. Hence he said: “It is finished.” And, bowing his head, he gave up his spirit (John 19).

**“One hundred.”** These are three times fifty. They clearly signify the Old Testament through Pentecost, the jubilee, and the threefold division of Scripture, since it is said: “Everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms must be fulfilled” (Luke 24).

# CHAPTER II

## Verse 1

**“Solomon determined to build a house,” etc.** (Bede, *Questions on the Book of Kings*, vol. II.) The house which Solomon built, etc., up to those who prepare themselves as God’s building by believing, acting, and teaching others.

**“Solomon.”** Both in name and in his most peaceful kingdom he signifies him, etc., up to “and the illumination of the Holy Spirit.”

## Verse 8

**“And they shall be servants.”** (RAB.) My apostles and first teachers, etc., up to “and therefore they fought more subtly.”

## Verse 14

**“The son of a woman.”** He shows that this man was descended from Salomith, from the tribe of Dan, concerning whom the Book of Numbers speaks. The Hebrews relate that his father was a Hebrew, from the family of Oholiab, of the tribe of Dan, who worked with Bezalel in the wilderness. As for calling him a Tyrian, the Hebrews say that this was done by translation. For *Zochri* in their language means “psalmody.” *Chyros*, which they call *Zor*, sometimes signifies “distress” and sometimes “formation.”

[Col. 0666A]

**“Who knows how to work in gold and silver.”** In all these matters Hiram spiritually knows how to work, so that the adornment of God’s house may shine before human eyes with worthy beauty and become acceptable to God through the fragrance of a good reputation.

## Verse 16

**“But we,” etc.** (RAB.) This signifies that the Gentiles, having heard the fame of the Gospel, send various kinds of people through faith to baptism. Yet it belongs to the true peacemaker alone to unite them to the unity of the Church by absolving sins through the sacrament of baptism. Concerning him it is said: “The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him is the one who baptizes” (Matthew 3).

## Verse 17

**“Therefore he counted,” etc. ‘There were workers for the house of the Lord from the children of Israel,’ etc.** (RAB.) up to “they build the Church of Christ by living rightly and teaching” [Col. 0666B].

**“Three thousand six hundred.”** In Chronicles, in place of the three thousand three hundred overseers counted in the Book of Kings, three thousand six hundred are recorded, signifying the perfection of exalted men. For God completed the adornment of the world in the number six; and because Holy Scripture teaches faith in the Trinity and works of righteousness, it is rightly said that there were three thousand six hundred.

# CHAPTER III

## Verse 1

**“On the threshing floor of Ornan.”** (RAB.) The Church is signified by the threshing floor, etc., up to “but when Christ looked upon it, he found in himself both the place and the name of peace.”

## Verse 2

**“In the second month,” etc.** That is, in May, immediately after Passover, so that the people, consecrated by the mystical solemnity, might worthily undertake the mystical work.

**“In the fourth year of his reign.”** After the dispensation of the divine incarnation, which is written in the four Gospels, had been completed, the Church was built through the Spirit sent from heaven. What we explained in the Books of Kings, we touch upon briefly in Chronicles.

The length of the house signifies the Church’s long-suffering. Its breadth signifies charity, by which it even loves enemies, until it rejoices with its friends alone in God. Its height signifies hope of the future life and reward, because it despises all adversities until it sees the Lord’s goodness in the land of the living.

It should be noted that the thirty cubits of height mentioned in the Book of Kings did not reach the roof of the temple but extended only to the lower upper chamber. [Col. 0666D] For here the height was one hundred twenty cubits. Another thirty will be counted to the middle upper chamber, another thirty to the third, and a further thirty thence to the highest roof of the temple; thus the entire height of the house is completed in one hundred twenty cubits. By this number the primitive Church in Jerusalem received the grace of the Holy Spirit.

For fifteen, composed of seven and eight, signifies the future life, which is now lived in the rest of souls and will be completed in the resurrection of bodies. Fifteen multiplied into a triangle—that is, counted together with all its parts—makes one hundred twenty; by this number the future blessedness of the elect is signified. It is fitting that the third upper chamber of the house is completed by this number [Col. 0667A], for after present labors and after the rest of souls, it will be filled with the glory of complete happiness in the resurrection.

## Verse 4

**“The portico,” etc.** Namely, the temple itself, which was before the doors of the inner sanctuary. The structure was divided into three parts: the portico before the temple; the temple itself, in which were the altar of incense, the table of the bread of the Presence, and the lampstand of light; and the inner sanctuary, that is, the Holy of Holies, where the ark of the covenant and the cherubim were placed behind the veil.

The portico before the temple bears the figure of the ancient faithful. The temple itself represents those who came into the world after the Lord’s incarnation. The inner house represents the joys of the heavenly kingdom, given to both groups.

[Col. 0667B]

It should therefore be noted that the walls of the house were made of precious stones, covered with panels of cypress or cedar, and clothed with sheets of gold. Hence it is said in the Book of Kings: “The whole house was clothed with cedar,” etc. The stones of the wall or pavement, the panels, and the gold signify the life of the saints in the Church.

The living stones are the saints, joined together by the strength of faith into one rule. The cedar or cypress panels are likewise the saints, joined to one another in the same faith through the breadth of various virtues according to the gift of the Holy Spirit. The sheets of gold are the saints who possess surpassing charity of knowledge and rejoice together through its most pleasing radiance.

## Verse 6

**“He also laid the pavement,” etc.** Just as the breadth of the wall, rising upward and reaching the ceilings, signifies the advancement of virtues by which the saints reach heaven, or the choirs of saints succeeding one another through different ages, so the evenness of the pavement signifies their harmonious humility, through which they live in social charity while placed in this life.

The pavement laid with precious marble, and the marble covered with fir panels, signifies that the life of the righteous must first be fortified in the heart by the firmness of faith and then adorned in action by the breadth of virtues. For what benefit is the beauty of marble covered with panels unless it displays something mystical? It signifies that the greatness of good works must be supported by the strength of faith.

The fir, high and durable, reveals the mind of the elect, scorning what is low, clinging to heavenly things, and excelling in the virtue of patience. The sheets of gold [Col. 0667D] laid over the marble beneath the fir panels signify the breadth of charity arising from a pure heart, a good conscience, and an unfeigned faith. As gold shines above other metals, so charity shines above the other virtues in the temple of God.

## Verse 7

**“The doorposts and the walls,” etc.** He covered them when, with the Lord himself opening the way of faith, he showed to all entering the Church with what truth it shines. Christ is the door of the temple, through whom one comes to the Father. He says: “I am the door,” etc. (John 10).

It is written this way in the Book of Kings: “The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high” (1 Kings 6). It is called the inner sanctuary, or Holy of Holies, because there divine and angelic speech reveals hidden things to human beings.

Hence: “The inner sanctuary was made in a hidden place,” that is, in the inner house, because in the heavenly homeland the vision and converse of the angels and the very presence of God will be revealed. When it says that it was twenty cubits high, this signifies the cedar wall that separates the inner sanctuary from the outer building.

**“He carved cherubim.”** This house, as is read in the Book of Kings, has projecting carvings, since the saints do not perform works of virtue secretly but set an example before everyone.

## Verse 8

**“He also made the inner house,” etc.** The inner sanctuary, where the ark was, was twenty cubits in length, breadth, and height—that is, square—because in the heavenly homeland, where the saints see the King in his beauty, only the charity of divine and heavenly grace shines everywhere. Hence, below: “He covered it with sheets of gold” (1 Kings 6), that is, he filled the walls of the heavenly city with the grace of charity.

**“With six hundred talents,” etc.** In the weight of the talents there is perfection, expressing the perfection of charity, just as the perfection of the number six is expressed when it is multiplied by one hundred to make six hundred.

## Verse 9

**“And the nails also.”** (RAB.) The number fifty signifies the forgiveness of sins, etc., up to the one who, reaching greater perfection through the nails, says: “But it is good for me to cling to God” (Psalm 72).

**“The upper chambers also.”** Just as the Holy of Holies, where the ark was, signifies the inner life of the saints in the sight of the Redeemer—hence: “You will hide them in the hiding-place of your face, from the disturbance of men” (Psalm 30)—so the upper chambers, being high, signify that same life as existing in heaven and not in this world. Hence: “Seek the things that are above” (Colossians 3), where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.

## Verse 10

**“He also made.”** (RAB.) This is read more fully in the Book of Kings, etc., up to “to be rewarded with the denarius of the everlasting kingdom.”

## Verse 11

**“So that one wing.”** One wing of a cherub was five cubits, etc., because the angels guard the law of God, written in the five books, with tireless devotion—namely, loving God with all their strength and their neighbors as themselves. “The fullness of the law is charity” (Romans 13).

The neighbors of the angels are likewise the spiritual beings and elect human beings. Hence each wing of the cherub is of the same measure, because with the same devotion by which they love one another in God, they desire also our fellowship as we ascend to them. Thus the wings together make ten cubits when, in the twofold expression of charity, the angels rejoice in the presence of their Creator.

## Verse 12

**“They touched the wall.”** With their wings they touch the two walls equally, because they have the Jews and the Gentiles with them as possessors of the heavenly court—not because there is a local distinction between the two peoples there, but because the inward festivity of blessedness is greater through the fellowship of fraternity united in God.

They therefore extend their wings to both walls, because, rejoicing in the heavenly homeland, they stir the righteous of both peoples to praise the Creator. They extend their wings, covered with gold, toward the walls of the inner sanctuary, just as they have their faces turned toward the outer house [Col. 0669A], because, even as the angels preserve their own innocence, they rejoice in the blessedness of the saints and bring aid to those whom they still see on earth, until they lead them into the heavenly homeland.

For all of them are ministering spirits sent out for service on behalf of those who are to inherit salvation (Hebrews 1). With their outer wings, one touches one wall and another the other, because the Old Testament, written for the ancient people, is rightly compared to the first wall, while we, who came to faith after the Lord’s incarnation, are compared to the second wall—that is, the northern one—because after the cold and darkness of idolatry we came to know the light of truth.

**“His wing.”** They extend their wings toward one another over the ark when they refer every good they have received to the praise of the Savior [Col. 0669B]. They extend their other wings toward the walls of the inner sanctuary when they rejoice to see the saints with them and touch them, as it were, with the tips of their wings, rejoicing that those saints were imitators of their purity in this life.

**“And their faces were turned.”** Because for our sake—for we still stand outside, though we have been saved in hope—the divine books were composed. Their authors, now reigning with the Lord, care for our salvation and intercede for us before God.

## Verse 14

**“He also made.”** (RAB.) This is set forth earlier in the Book of Kings, etc., up to “and the truth of the Gospel and entrance into the kingdom are opened by that very truth.”

And he interwove them. The cherubim are interwoven with these four colors when, in everything we piously do, we are protected from the poisonous arrows [Col. 0669C] of demons through angelic defenses, and continually make use of the abundance of knowledge, always looking toward the divine utterances lest we stray from the path of the virtues.

**VERSE 15.**—Two columns also before the doors of the temple. They stood in the portico before the doors of the temple and adorned the entrance to the temple with their beauty on either side. The door of the temple is the Lord, who says: “No one comes to the Father except through me,” etc. (John XIV). The columns stand beside the door on both sides when ministers of the word show both peoples the entrance to the heavenly kingdom, so that whoever comes to the faith of the Gospel from the light of knowledge of the Law or from the error of paganism may find them ready to show him the way of salvation by word and example. In Kings we read of these columns: [Col. 0669D] “When he had come to King Solomon, he performed all his work, and cast two bronze columns,” etc. (3 Kings VII).

**Thirty-five.** This number signifies the perfection of teachers. For seven multiplied by five, or five by seven, produces thirty-five. Five signifies the Law; seven, on account of the sevenfold Spirit remaining in the flower of Jesse’s root, signifies the Gospel. Hence elsewhere the Lord is related to have fed five thousand people with five loaves, and four thousand people with seven loaves. The columns of thirty-five cubits therefore signify that the teachers of the Gospel possess perfect knowledge of the two Testaments. [Col. 0670A] Hence: “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God” (Mark IV). And elsewhere: “He opened their minds, so that they might understand the Scriptures” (Luke XXIV).

**Like little chains.** (RAB.) The manifold interweaving of chains and of the net, according to the expansion in Kings, indicates the various persons of the elect. When they adhere faithfully to the preachers’ words by listening and obeying, the nets and little chains placed above the capitals of the columns present to those who look upon them a marvel of their interconnection.

**VERSE 16.**—The capitals of the columns. The capitals of the columns, that is, their uppermost part, are the innermost thoughts of the teachers. Just as the limbs are directed by the head, so all their works and words are directed by thoughts devoted to God.

[Col. 0670B] **Pomegranates.** A single outer rind surrounds many seeds within; hence they signify the Church, because it surrounds innumerable hosts of the elect with the protection of one faith. Alternatively, they signify the life and conduct of each righteous person, who fortifies the many marks of his thoughts and virtues, lest they fall away, with the firm protection of faith and humility. Properly, then, the capitals of the columns were surrounded on every side by pomegranates, because the holy teachers recall the lives of the faithful of former times and confirm their own words in every respect by their examples, lest, if they live or teach otherwise than their rule requires, they go astray.

**VERSE 17.**—The same also. The two columns were made and arranged in this way so that they might teach us to keep before our eyes the entrance into the heavenly kingdom both in prosperity and in adversity. [Col. 0670C] It should be noted, moreover, that the portico of the temple is also called the vestibule, and that what we read as “between the vestibule and the altar” should be understood as “between the portico and the altar.” The second column signifies the preachers who were sent to preach to the Gentiles. Alternatively, the column on the right signifies those who prophesied that the Lord would come in the flesh; the second signifies those who testify that he has already come and redeemed the world by his blood. Both columns are designated by similar language, when one is called “strength” and the other “firmness,” so that it may be shown that the strength of faith and of works must be present in all teachers. At the same time, the teachers of our own age are silently indicated: they wish to be seen and called columns of the house of God, although they possess in themselves neither the strength of firm faith to despise the pomp of the world and desire invisible goods, [Col. 0670D] nor the diligence to correct or understand the errors of those entrusted to them.

## CHAPTER IV

**VERSE 1.**—He also made, etc. (RAB.) The altar of holocaust signifies those who consecrate body and soul to God by the fire of love. The length of the altar expresses their perseverance in good works; its breadth, the extent of their love of God and neighbor; its height displays their hope in expectation of visitation.

**Twenty cubits.** The number twenty signifies the great perfection of tireless patience and sincere love, which is granted to us through observance of both Testaments. For four times five makes twenty; [Col. 0671A] there are five books of the Law and four Gospels. When, enlightened by grace, we attain to understanding and observance of the Law, we complete the number twenty. The same number is found in the length and breadth of the altar when the hearts of the elect, taught by both Testaments, preserve this perseverance in their works even amid persecutions, and preserve the gladness of love even toward those who persecute them.

**And ten cubits.** The number ten signifies hope of heavenly rewards. Hence those who labor in the vineyard of the master of the household are rewarded with a denarius. Therefore the altar, which signifies the elect, is raised ten cubits to mark their perpetual life.

**VERSE 2.**—The sea also. (RAB.) The laver of salvation, etc., up to “and ought to hope from the Lord for the common crown of righteousness.” [Col. 0671B]

**It was five cubits.** Whatever we offend through sight, hearing, smell, taste, or touch is wholly forgiven in baptism. But remission of past sins is not enough unless each person thereafter devotes himself to good works. Otherwise the devil who had gone out returns in greater force, and “the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.” Hence he hears:

**A cord of thirty cubits.** This is the discipline of the heavenly commandments, by which we are bound back from our own wills. Hence: “A threefold cord is not quickly broken” (Ecclesiastes IV), because observance of God’s commandments, strengthened in the hearts of the saints by faith, hope, and love of heavenly recompense, cannot be dissolved by any adversity. [Col. 0671C]

**VERSE 3.**—And ten cubits. (RAB.) The sculpture beneath the rim, etc., up to “with what misery the reprobate perished because of their crimes.”

**VERSE 4.**—The back parts. The reward with which preachers are to be endowed forever has been determined by God’s judgment, but remains hidden from us. Yet this cannot be hidden from us: everyone who receives baptism for salvation must possess faith, hope, and love, and cannot work or enter into salvation without these three virtues. Hence it is said in Kings: “The thickness of the laver was three inches” (3 Kings VII). The thickness of the laver is the firmness of virtue; “three inches,” because the reception of baptism is fortified by the strength of faith, hope, and love. [Col. 0671D]

**VERSE 5.**—Moreover, its breadth. The thickness which Josephus said was four fingers, indicating the size of a handbreadth. These things signify the same. Whoever performs works of righteousness in faith, hope, and love according to the teaching of the four Gospels receives also the reward of eternal life.

**Three thousand measures.** The number one thousand signifies perfection, because ten multiplied by itself makes a solid square. Ten times ten makes one hundred, which is like a square figure but flat; but in order for it to rise in height and become solid, multiply one hundred by ten, and it becomes one thousand. By this number the stable and unconquerable, as it were square, conscience of the righteous is signified. However you turn a square, it stands. Thus the mind of the elect is not bent from its upright state by any temptation. The sea holds three thousand measures when the sacrament of baptism, given in faith in the Trinity, grants those washed in it forgiveness of all sins. [Col. 0672A]

**VERSE 6.**—He also made basins. In Kings it reads as follows: “He also made ten bronze lavers. One laver held forty baths and was four cubits. He placed each laver upon each of the ten bases,” etc. The apostles and apostolic men, signified by the oxen carrying the sea, are also represented by the bases prepared for carrying the lavers. The lavers themselves signify baptism, which the sea prefigured. For the priests washed in them everything that they were going to offer in holocausts. The Lord’s holocaust can be understood as the whole multitude of the faithful, which is baptized by him in water and fire. Therefore, just as the priests who are washed in the sea signify those who through baptism become sharers in the supreme priest, so the holocausts represent the same people when, after the washing of baptism, they are filled with spiritual grace. The victim is washed in the laver when the faithful person is drenched with baptismal water; it is offered as a holocaust when, through the laying on of the bishop’s hand, he receives the gift of the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0672B]

**VERSE 8.**—And he placed five. The bases of the lavers were placed on each side of the temple so that it might be indicated that the grace of the sacred font was to be opened to both peoples. There are five on each side so that, as we already said in the exposition of the sea, which was five cubits high, it might be shown typologically that everything a person had sinned through the five bodily senses is forgiven through the washing of baptism. [Col. 0672C] Thus, just as the one sea set upon twelve oxen expresses the unity of baptism that was to be preached throughout the whole world by the apostles, so the two rows of lavers mystically show that the Gentiles together with the Jews were to be brought forth into one fellowship of faith through the water of baptism.

**Golden lampstands.** The divine utterances, which bring forth the light of wisdom. Hence: “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light,” etc. (Psalm CXVIII). Solomon says here: “For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light” (Proverbs VI). There are ten lampstands, twice five, because there are five volumes of the Lawgiver, and in them the whole sequence of the Old Testament embraces the five ages of the world. Five are placed on the right and five on the left when, after the Lord’s incarnation, the same Scripture is entrusted to both peoples. Alternatively, it is shown to be full of evangelical figures, although once it was thought to be understood only according to the letter. [Col. 0672D]

**And also tables.** (RAB.) These tables, etc., up to “whose works are set before us like life-giving breasts as examples of life.”

**VERSE 9.**—He also made the court. (RAB.) The court of the priests in the Church, etc., up to “we have expressed more fully in the book of Kings according to Bede.” [Col. 0673A]

**And the great basilica.** This was outside the court of the priests, and all the people gathered there to pray or to hear the word. In the Church it signifies the life and conduct of carnal people, to whom it is said: “I could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as carnal,” etc.

**And the basilica.** Carnal people are rightly signified by the great basilica, because their number in the Church is much greater than that of the perfect. But by as much as they surpass them in number, by so much do they fall short in merit. Therefore, although this great basilica contains very many, it does not admit them to the service of the altar, nor even into the court of the priests itself, because carnal and weak people, although on account of the merit of a pure faith and piety they belong to the lot of the elect, are nevertheless far removed from those who say: “I do not dare to speak of anything except what Christ accomplishes through me, in obedience of the Gentiles by word and deed.”

**And the doors in the basilica.** These signify that the entrance of faith is prepared by the preaching of the word, so that those who come may learn how they ought to enter the Church of God through faith in Christ and the sacraments of salvation, and, after they have entered, how religiously they ought to conduct themselves. [Col. 0673B]

**VERSE 11.**—Now Hiram made. The cauldrons receive the sacred ashes when the faithful, with devout mind, carefully recall the examples and mysteries of the Lord’s passion for the preservation of their own lives, or attentively contemplate the departure of the righteous, who, after laboring through great and arduous struggles, rejoice without end in the prize they have received. Thus, by considering the virtues of their predecessors, they too may become great. Hence: “Considering the outcome of their way of life, look also to their faith.”

**And the flesh-hooks.** The flesh-hooks signify preachers who refresh the souls of the faithful with the word of God, comparing spiritual things with spiritual and supplying carnal people with the milk of simple doctrine. Those who wish to know the mysteries of Christ in summary and receive them for imitation are, as it were, satisfied with the flesh of the saving victim. Since it belongs to teachers to distribute to each person what is appropriate, flesh-hooks are rightly made for the priests, with which they may arrange the flesh of the victims as required, bringing some things to clean people and leaving others to be consumed by the fires of the altar. For certain things are revealed for the refreshment of our humility; certain things are open only to the knowledge of the Holy Spirit; certain things in Chronicles, which we passed over after expounding them in Kings, are explained; and some things we do not find explained, nor do we wish to exceed the custom of our small ability. For nowhere have we explained anything by ourselves. [Col. 0673C]

**And bowls.** Bowls signify the broader and more open discourse of sacred teaching. It supplies a draught of wisdom to those who thirst piously and grants suitable refreshment through the ministries of preachers to those who labor piously, so that they may reach the fountain of eternal life, from which those who drink will never thirst. [Col. 0673D]

**VERSE 17.**—In the clay ground. The clay earth from which molds were made for casting vessels signifies sacred Scripture, from which we receive the rule of good living. Like clay hardened by fire, it displays the form of the Lord’s vessel, showing how great and of what kind such vessels ought to be. Scripture shows us the rule of righteousness that we should follow and the examples of the saints, who, made invincible by the fire of tribulation, persevered in all things, so that we might [Col. 0674A] desire to be precious vessels in the house of the Lord.

Bronze melted by fire enters the clay molds so that it may become a vessel suitable for heavenly ministries. This happens when, softened by salutary humility and by the flame of divine love or human adversity, we enter the way of the Fathers by doing good works, so that by running well we may reach their rewards. For we need not always be constrained by rules of good conduct; once the good work has been completed, the palm of blessed recompense is to be hoped for. Vessels were not always held enclosed in clay molds: when they had reached perfection, they were brought into the light after the restraints of the molds had been broken, and each was placed in its proper location in the temple for the Lord’s service. This does not mean that the works of the saints will perish, but that, once they have received the crown of righteousness, the duties of laborious activity will cease. [Col. 0674B]

**In the region of the Jordan.** In the Jordan Christ was baptized, and by being immersed in its waters he turned the element into the washing away of sins for us. Since every baptism of the faithful, by which we are consecrated to the Lord, is celebrated as an example of that baptism, the vessels of the house of the Lord were rightly made in the region of the Jordan. We cannot otherwise become vessels of election unless, looking toward his baptism, we strive to be washed in the life-giving river.

It should also be noted that he says the vessels were made not only in the region of the Jordan but in its plain, signifying the multiplication of the faithful, which was to take place not only in Judea but throughout the breadth of the Gentiles. Hence: “The plains will rejoice and everything in them” (Psalm XCV). And elsewhere: “We heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of the wood” (ibid. CXXXI). Therefore the king cast the vessels of the house of the Lord in the plain of the Jordan, because the Lord filled the whole breadth of the world with the baptism of salvation, from which he would make vessels of mercy. [Col. 0674C]

**VERSE 18.**—And Solomon made. He commanded what Hiram completed in the actual work. Allegorically, however, our Redeemer prepares the adornment of the Church in the holy preachers and in all the faithful, and brings about works of virtue. He says: “Without me you can do nothing” (John XV); and elsewhere: “Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above,” etc. (James I).

**VERSE 19.**—The golden altar. The hearts of the perfect, shining with the light of inward love and chastity; the elevated position of the altar also signifies their sublimity. It stood before the door of the Holy of Holies, as we read in the construction of the tabernacle. There not the blood of victims or libations but only incense was burned; its smoke, rising upward, covered the ark and filled the oracle with the fragrance of sweetness. In this the saints are represented: while, neglecting the desires of temporal things, they seek heavenly things with their whole attention, they are as though placed within, beside the oracle. Nor are they far removed from the veil that separates the temple and the Holy of Holies, because in body they dwell on earth but in their whole mind they are in heaven. [Col. 0674D]

The smoke of the incense rises from this altar into the Holy of Holies, where the ark is concealed, so that the prayers of the saints, kindled by the flame of love, may reach heaven, where Christ sits at the right hand of God. For on this altar no blood of victims but only incense is burned, because such men do not possess works of flesh and blood to slaughter for the Lord upon the altar of the heart; rather, they offer vows of tears and prayers out of desire for the heavenly kingdom. [Col. 0675A]

**VERSE 21.**—And tongs, etc. Bronze tongs were made for use at the altar. Those also with which the lamps were cleaned signify, through the offices of teachers, the interpretation of spiritual meaning. They transfer the very words of sacred discourse from history to allegory and from shadow to truth, and, placed as it were upon the mystical lampstand, multiply the light of knowledge in the Church.

**VERSE 22.**—And he engraved the doors. These are the teachers and priests who, by instructing, baptizing, and communicating the mysteries of the Lord’s body and blood, first open to us the thresholds of the Church. [Col. 0675B]

**And thus all the work was completed.** This occurs when the true Peacemaker, on the last day, glorifies all the elect with the immortality of the resurrection. As long as the present state of this age continues, Solomon indeed performs the work of the house of the Lord, but does not complete it, because the Lord inspires and assists the hearts of the elect to do good, yet grants no one freedom from sin; this he reserves for the faithful in the future. He completes the whole work of his temple and makes it fit for dedication when, having transferred the elect from this life, he brings them into the eternal kingdom. Hence it is built over seven years and dedicated in completion in the eighth. For the whole of time revolves in seven days; the eighth is the day of judgment and resurrection, to which what follows is appropriate. [Col. 0675C]

## CHAPTER V

**VERSE 1.**—Therefore Solomon brought in all, etc. (RAB.) This occurs when Christ, etc., up to “but in it are many dwellings for receiving all whom the Lord blesses, the small together with the great, because they fear and love him.”

**VERSE 9.**—But the poles. (ID.) It should be noted that, etc., up to “the less they see the inward joys.”

**VERSE 10.**—And there was nothing else. He shows generally that there was nothing in the ark contrary to the law of the Lord contained on the two tablets. Rather, only those things had been placed there which, according to the commandments of the Law, had been made typologically for the worship of the one God and the commendation of our faith, so that the shadow of future things might in every respect bear witness to the future truth and reach its fulfillment when that truth appeared in the world. [Col. 0675D]

According to Paul, there was in the ark a golden urn containing manna, because in the man Christ “the whole fullness of divinity dwells bodily.” There was also Aaron’s rod, which, though cut off, had flowered again, because all power of judgment belongs to him whose judgment appeared to have been removed in the humility of his passion. There were also the tablets of the covenant, because in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The poles by which it was carried also remained attached, because the teachers who once labored in the word of Christ now rejoice together in the glory of Christ through his present vision. Hence: “I desire to depart and be with Christ” (Philippians I). [Col. 0676A]

**VERSE 12.**—Clothed in linen garments. By the linen robes, the white purity of bodily chastity is signified. All who attend upon the service of God are clothed in this, and they resound with his praises by mouth, conduct, and action. The cymbals signify confession by the mouth; the psalteries, mortality; the lyres, the mortification of the flesh and the vigor of good action, furnished with twenty-four strings, that is, with prophetic and apostolic teachings.

**The priests.** Or the teachers, represented by the number one hundred and twenty, because the Lawgiver completed the sum of his years with this number, and on the day of Pentecost believers received the grace of the Spirit, the Paraclete, in the same number. [Col. 0676B]

**VERSE 13.**—Then, when all. (RAB.) All the priests and Levites, etc., up to “they lost the ministry of the true priesthood.”

**VERSE 14.**—For it had filled [it]. The mysteries that lay hidden beneath a veil were opened to believers through the coming of Christ and to those who received him worthily. But for the others, who were unwilling to approach the faith, their former blindness remained. Hence: “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God,” etc. (Matthew XIII).

## CHAPTER VI

**VERSE 1.**—In darkness. Hence Job: “He makes the clouds his hiding place” (Job XXII). And the Psalmist: “Darkness was beneath his feet, and he made darkness his hiding place” (Psalm XVII). The Lord’s hiding place is sacred Scripture, which bears heavenly mysteries beneath parables and figures. Hence: “I confess to you, Lord, Father of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones” (Matthew XI). [Col. 0676C]

## CHAPTER VII

**VERSE 5.**—He dedicated it. (RAB.) Christ cleansed it with his blood, sanctified it with spiritual grace, and multiplied it with various gifts of the virtues. The sons of Israel dedicate it because each faithful person, according to the gift bestowed on him by God, turns and advances his neighbors toward better and more perfect things by word and example. [Col. 0676D]

**VERSE 7.**—He sanctified. Christ perfects in the Church those things that could not be perfected in the Law because of its weakness. For it is the court of the house of the Lord, through which the entrance into the heavenly Jerusalem lies open. Since, therefore, holocausts and sacrifices could not be offered upon the altar of the Old Testament, because everything there was done figuratively, our king and priest raised up in the Church a new altar of faith, on which rich holocausts and sacrifices acceptable to God are offered daily. Hence: “The sacrifice of praise will honor me, and there is the way,” etc.

**VERSE 8.**—Therefore he made. (RAB.) I do not think this should be understood otherwise, etc., up to “in the future rest of souls, in the actual perception of truth.”

**VERSE 10.**—Therefore on the day, etc. This is after the eighth day of the solemnity of the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is contained in Kings. It signifies that after the end of this life, and after the repose of holy souls beneath the altar, in which they rest before the judgment, in the eighth age—that is, on the day of resurrection—the saints will receive immortal bodies and be placed in heavenly dwellings according to the quality of their merits. There they will rejoice forever, praising God for all the good things that the Father has bestowed upon the Christian people in Christ. [Col. 0677A]

## CHAPTER VIII

**VERSE 1.**—When twenty years had been completed, etc., he had given to Hiram, etc. (RAB. in Chronicles, from Jerome.) That is, he had returned them, because when Solomon had given them, they did not please Hiram. Therefore Solomon assigned them to his own uses.

**VERSE 5.**—Beth-horon. (RAB.) It is a city to which Jesus pursued the hostile kings in the tribe of Ephraim, etc., up to “and the other, lower Beth-horon, was given to the Levites as a possession.” [Col. 0677B]

**VERSE 6.**—And all. Namely, Ezer, Megiddo, Gezer, and Millo: all of these display the beauty of the Church, because the true Solomon prepared them for himself in the joy of his kingdom, for praise and gladness.

Millo is interpreted as “fulfillment”; Ezer as “separated and sanctified”; Megiddo as “his banquet”; Gezer as “cutting off” or “division”; Beth-horon as “house of the mountains”; and Baalath as “ascending.” The holy Church is the city of the living God, where the will of God is fulfilled daily, and which, separated from every error of unbelievers, is sanctified by faith and good works. There is the refreshment of the virtues. It distinguishes between clean and unclean, and between vice and virtue. It is the house of the mountains, that is, the dwelling of the saints, and, flowering through the fruit of righteousness like a palm, it ascends from virtue to virtue, so that it may see the God of gods in Zion (Psalm LXXXIII). Solomon fortified all its villages because Christ so protects the gatherings of his faithful with the protection of his grace that they are able to resist their spiritual enemies. [Col. 0677C]

**In Lebanon.** (HIERON.) Namely, in the temple, which was clothed in the beauty of cedars; hence Zechariah: “Open your doors, O Lebanon” (Zechariah XI). Or in the royal buildings, which had been made from the wood of Lebanon.

**VERSE 10.**—Two hundred. The number one hundred, which in counting on the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, signifies eternal life. The number fifty signifies the remission of sins, eternal rest, and the grace of the Holy Spirit, because in the psalm bearing that number repentance, confession, and remission of sins are described, and future rest is signified by the jubilee. Through Pentecost, the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit at his coming is expressed. [Col. 0677D]

**Who instructed.** From both peoples he chose rulers of the Church, who, enlightened by spiritual grace and fully taught, were to teach by their example the remission of sins, the life of eternal salvation, and the perpetual blessedness that must be desired.

**VERSE 12.**—Holocausts. (RAB.) A holocaust is called something wholly burned. It is burned on the altar when the good work of each elect person, who has wholly vowed himself—that is, flesh and heart—to God, is kindled by the fervent fire of love. [Col. 0678A]

**VERSE 14.**—According to the appropriateness of each season he arranges everything in the Church, so that each order, having fulfilled its office, may minister worthily.

**VERSE 17.**—In Ezion-geber. It is said to be an island not far from Eloth in the Red Sea, where Jehoshaphat’s fleet perished.

(RAB.) The fleet that Solomon made, etc., up to “they find through the grace of the Holy Spirit, and, attributing him to divine wisdom and counsel, offer him as a gift.”

**VERSE 18.**—In Ophir. The name of the province Ophir, named after one of the later descendants of Eber, whose descendants, coming from the river Cophene as far as the region of India called Gerra, Josephus reports to have lived there.

## CHAPTER IX

**VERSE 1.**—The queen also. (RAB. on Chronicles, volume III.) The queen of the South, who was stirred up from the ends of the earth and came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, prefigured the Church from the Gentiles, which was to come to Christ. Clothed in garments embroidered with gold and variegated colors, she had not become barbarian in spirit, although she came from a barbarian people, because she desired to become a fellow citizen of the saints. Hence: “The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation” (Matthew XII). [Col. 0678B]

**VERSE 3.**—When she had seen, etc. These things apply to the Church, which, having heard Christ’s miracles, was provoked to seek him. But after she came to him through baptism and faith, and recognized the presence of his divinity by considering the testimonies of Scripture, what she had previously heard about him seemed little in comparison with the grace she received. Hence, in wonder, she broke forth into his praise, saying: “Blessed are your men,” etc. [Col. 0678C]

**VERSE 12.**—From wood. Christ places precious wood—that is, the holy teachers, whose faith’s greenness never withers and whose leaves of words never fall, but who yield the fruit of good works in their seasons—in the fortress of the house of the Lord and of the royal house, that is, for the strengthening of the Church, so that, surrounded on every side by their teachings and examples, it may not experience ruin. They are said to have been fashioned like lyres and harps for praising the Lord, because whatever they do prospers, and in prosperity and adversity they proclaim the Lord’s praise in heart, mouth, and work. They do everything for the glory of God and do not cease day or night from praising the name of the Lord. [Col. 0678D]

**VERSE 13.**—Six hundred. Six multiplied by six makes sixty [sic]. One hundred multiplied six times makes six hundred. Ten signifies the perfection of the commandments; one hundred, the reward of eternal blessedness. The king desires our perfection so that he may have people to whom he can give perfect recompense. Hence: “Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments” (Matthew V, XIX). And shortly afterward: “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell what you have,” etc.; and “everyone who has left a house,” etc., “will receive a hundredfold and possess eternal life.”

**And all the kings of Arabia.** Various peoples and merchants, all the kings of Arabia and the satraps of the lands, offer gold and silver to Solomon, because every people and every person, vying according to his strength, offers our Peacemaker the gift of right faith, purity of understanding, fullness of sacred confession, and brilliance of eloquence. Hence: “The kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts,” etc. “And all kings will worship him; all nations will serve him” (Psalm LXXI). [Col. 0679A]

**VERSE 15.**—Therefore he made. The fathers of both Testaments, perfected in teaching and action, proved by their works whatever they taught in speech.

**Golden spears.** This is the armor of God by which we resist the snares of the devil. The holy preachers possess it: they guard the house of God and keep watch at its door, lest the ancient enemy enter. Hence: “Sixty mighty men surround Solomon’s bed” (Proverbs III). [Col. 0679B]

**VERSE 16.**—He also made three hundred. This signifies perfect faith in the confession of the holy Trinity. The guards of the house of God rightly carry golden spears and shields, because the preachers who are the Church’s guardians, shining with the brightness of wisdom, pierce their enemies with the arrows of their words and extinguish the flaming darts of the wicked with the shield of faith.

**Also six armrests.** In the number six is the perfection of good works. God made the world in six days, and six is the first perfect number. By good and perfect works one ascends to heaven.

**A golden footstool.** The saints, shining with the splendor of the virtues, in whom God dwells. By the footstool may also be signified those who are weak in the body of Christ, such as penitents, or those who will be converted last, namely, near the end of the world. Yet they are golden, refined and tested by the fire of the tribulations of that time. [Col. 0679C]

**Standing beside the armrests; and also twelve other little lions, etc.** The holy Fathers attributed whatever good they did in the Gospel not to themselves but to God. Hence: “Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory” (Psalm CXIII).

**The armrests, etc.** In Kings it reads: “And two hands on either side held the seat” (3 Kings X). These are the supports of divine grace, which advance the Church toward the heavenly kingdom. Alternatively, this is signified by the number two, because both Testaments especially commend that nothing good can be perfected except through divine assistance. Hence: “Without me you can do nothing” (John V). [Col. 0679D]

**VERSE 19.**—Six steps. They contend through teaching and example so that the labor of the foolish in doing good may not falter, but may firmly preserve uprightness in advancing through the virtues.

**There was no such throne, etc.** For it is written of the Church: “Strength and beauty are her clothing,” etc. (3 Kings X.) And: “Many daughters have gathered riches; you have surpassed them all” (Proverbs XXXI).

**VERSE 20.**—All the vessels also. The souls of the saints, who serve the will of God, shining with the splendor of wisdom and love, contain the water of life, which becomes in them “a fountain of water springing up into eternal life” (John IV). [Col. 0680A]

**Silver.** The word of God is not in speech but in power, as in the preaching of the Gospel—not in persuasive words of human wisdom but in the demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

**VERSE 21.**—For the king’s ships went to Tarshish, etc. (RAB.) Christ sends the apostles, teachers of the Gospel, whom he chose from the Jews, together with preachers chosen from the Gentiles, into the world with a threefold confession but one faith, so that among believers they may bring him gold of wisdom, silver of eloquence, and ivory of chastity. The monkey is an ingenious animal and an imitator of human beings, and may signify philosophers, who sometimes alter the meaning of true wisdom and discuss actions in the disciplines of moral life. The peacock, which displays its praised feathers, signifies those who exhibit the appearance of various virtues for the sake of human praise. But instructed by the doctrine of the preachers, they learn to do good with God alone in view and are prepared for the delights of the eternal king. [Col. 0680B]

**VERSE 25.**—Forty. The number forty signifies the periods of the ancient Law. Moses fasted forty days when he was about to receive the Law, and the people instructed by him wandered through the wilderness for forty years. Six signifies the present age, in which apostolic teaching nourishes the people with the doctrine of the New Testament. Therefore Solomon’s horses placed in the stables are rightly numbered by forty, because by the harshness of the ancient Law the insolence of the former people was restrained. Twelve signifies the present age, in which apostolic authority nourishes the people of the Gentiles with the doctrine of the New Testament. [Col. 0680C]

**In Jerusalem.** “Vision of peace.” The distance between places displays a distinction of dispositions. Those who are in the chariot cities signify those who are instructed in the Church’s various disciplines by spiritual teachers. Others, already instructed and fitted for the service of the heavenly king, are worthy to possess his presence. Hence: “The chariots of God are ten thousand,” etc. (Psalm LXXVI). And elsewhere: “You will mount your horses, and your riding is salvation” (Habakkuk III).
