**Verse 14.—“A golden crown,” etc.** On it was the name of almighty God. It signifies the honor of the divine majesty, since we must place God above all things, so that in all our deeds and words God may be honored through Jesus Christ, who is our head (I Pet. IV).

**Verse 17.—“Sacrifices.”** (RAB.) How Moses appointed Aaron, etc., up to the point where Christ’s priesthood and the rites of sacrifice will remain forever.

**Verse 28.—“Phinehas, son of Eleazar.”** (ID.) Phinehas, as it is written in the Book of Numbers (chapter XXV), etc., up to the point where he happily reached the mountain of strength, that is, Christ.

[Col. 1227B]

**Verse 31.—“And the covenant of David.”** (ID.) It signifies that David, in the distribution of God’s ministries, etc., up to the point where he arranged the turns of the ministers in the tabernacle.

### Chapter XLVI

**Verse 1.—“Jesus the son of Nave, mighty in war.”** (RAB.) Jesus signifies Christ both in deed and in word, etc., up to the point where he triumphs over principalities and powers in himself.

**Verse 4.—“Who was before him,” etc.** (ID.) How the sun was held back at Joshua’s approach, etc., up to the point where they will be shortened at the time of destruction.

**Verse 9.—“From sins.”** Of despair: when they heard the report of the spies, they despaired of entering the land.

[Col. 1227C]

**Verse 13.—“And the judges, each one,” etc.** (RAB.) After Joshua, judges succeeded who defended God’s people from their enemies; and after Christ’s Passion, the apostles became rulers of God’s Church.

**Verse 14.—“So that their memory might remain,” etc.** Because they persevered in the true faith, so that their memory might be established with perpetual blessing. “Bones.” The strength of good works is granted as a reward, so that the memory of their name might be transmitted with glory to posterity.

**Verse 16.—“Beloved by the Lord,” etc.** (RAB.) The history relates that the Lord spoke to the infant Samuel, etc., up to the point where he announces future punishment and everlasting death for wicked rulers.

### Chapter XLVII

[Col. 1227D]

**Verse 1.—“After these things Nathan arose.”** Literally, he recalls David’s deeds, which the Books of Kings and Chronicles narrate most fully.

**Verse 2.—“Like fat.”** He signifies David as filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit and separated in life and conduct from the company of the carnal.

**Verse 3.—“He played with lions.”** (RAB.) David signifies Christ, etc., up to the point where he gave him the name that is above every name.

**Verse 14.—“After him a discerning son arose.”** (ID.) Mystically, Solomon, etc., up to the point where, as in one threshing floor, the good are signified by grain and the evil by chaff.

**Verse 23.—“So that you might establish a kingdom,” etc.** (ID.) Because ten tribes followed Jeroboam and two followed Rehoboam. Jeroboam was from Ephraim, and he was the first to rule cruelly over the ten tribes.

[Col. 1228A]

**Verse 27.—“And he left behind him,” etc.** (ID.) Mystically, Rehoboam, whose name is interpreted as “breadth of the people,” etc., up to the point where he remained within the rule of the Catholic faith.

**Verse 28.—“He turned the nation aside by his counsel.”** That is, by trusting the counsel of young men.

### Chapter XLVIII

**Verse 1.—“And Elijah arose.”** (RAB.) He burned with heavenly fire the two captains of fifty sent by King Ozia (IV Kings I).

**Verse 2.—“Who brought in.”** (ID.) Mystically, the three-year famine represented a famine of the word of God and of faith in the Trinity, etc., up to the point where the one would later come who, neither translated nor carried upward, would penetrate the ethereal heavens by his own power.

### VERSE 13

Elijah indeed in the whirlwind, etc. (ID.) Since a disciple is not above his teacher, etc., up to: for whoever touches Christ’s death with firm faith is a participant in his resurrection.

Fulfilled in Elisha. He prayed, “Let your spirit be doubled in me,” and obtained it. Hence he was unconquerable in patience and virtue; in both life and death he performed many signs.

### VERSE 17

A very small remnant of the people was left. Because the house of David, and the tribe of Judah, and Benjamin did not entirely abandon the worship of God, although some of them were idolaters, such as Joram and Ahaz, while others clung to God, such as Hezekiah and Josiah.

[Col. 1228C] ### VERSE 19

Hezekiah fortified his city, etc. (RAB.) That Hezekiah stopped up the spring, etc., up to: the city liberated after the enemies had been destroyed is fully shown in Chronicles.

## CHAPTER XLIX

### VERSE 1

The memory of Josiah. (RAB.) The memory of King Josiah, etc., up to: he himself, out of zeal for God, cleanses the land of Judah and Jerusalem from all abominations; he says: “Zeal for your house has consumed me.”

### VERSE 5

Apart from David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, etc. These three are not said to have sinned in comparison with the others. Whatever sins they committed, they wiped away through worthy repentance, and they pleased God through devotion and piety.

[Col. 1228D] ### VERSE 8

They burned the chosen city of holiness, etc. (ID.) Some understand this passage as referring to Christ, etc., up to: after these things had been destroyed, he built the Church of God.

### VERSE 10

Ezekiel, who saw, etc. (ID.) Mystically, Ezekiel, etc., up to: and foretold remedies for those who repent.

### VERSE 11

In the rain. He signifies that he preached that a rain of vengeance would come upon sinners, while he promised the consolation of mercy to those walking along the way of God’s commandments.

### VERSE 13

For he too, etc. Because he signifies Christ, who is the image of God, so that whoever believes in God may be marked as though with a seal.

[Col. 1229A] ### VERSE 14

And Jesus son of Josedec. Because through the grace of Jesus Christ, who is our king and priest, the Church is rebuilt after the captivity of diabolical oppression.

### VERSE 15

Nehemiah. (RAB.) “God is the consoler,” or “consoled by the Lord,” etc., up to: he who builds the city of God, that is, the Church, and comforts those who mourn.

### VERSE 16

No one, etc. Enoch means “dedication.” Here he signifies Christ, who built and consecrated the Church with his blood; he came into the world without sin and will receive it into heaven with glory.

### VERSE 17

Like Joseph. Joseph, like his father Jacob, longed for the land of promise and detested Egypt, teaching us to desire the land [Col. 1229B] of the living, so that we may rest in peace.

### VERSE 18

And his bones were visited. (RAB.) He signifies that Joseph, etc., up to: and they buried him at Shechem, which is Neapolis, the city of the Samaritans.

### VERSE 19

Seth and Shem, etc. Seth, the son of Adam, and Shem, the firstborn of Noah, surpassed the people of their own time both in faith and in conduct. Christ is signified in them, for he is both God and man.

## CHAPTER L

### VERSE 1

Simon son of Onias. (RAB.) He came to the people of his own time, etc., up to: since Jesus describes Simon’s life and conduct so explicitly.

### VERSE 3

Wells of water. The depths of Scripture, which lie hidden under figures in the divine books, [Col. 1229C] but overflow from the mouths of preachers like a sea for the satisfaction of many.

### VERSE 5

And he enlarged the entrance of the court-house. Because among the simple, signified by the court, and among the perfect, signified by the house, the merit of teachers increases.

### VERSE 11

In receiving the robe, etc. The order of preachers, in receiving the robe of glory and clothing itself with the completion of virtues, displays the judgment of its dignity, the adornment of faith, and the garment of good works. These things ought to appear in priests, so that they may teach worthily.

### VERSE 13

But in receiving portions from the hand of the priest. He receives portions from the hand of the priest who requires from ministers the performance of good works.

### VERSE 15

And performing the completion upon the altar. The completed offering is given to the exalted King when Christ’s body is offered to God.

### VERSE 17

He poured it out upon the foundation. In commemoration of Christ, who is the foundation of the Church, the fragrance of this offering is most pleasing to almighty God.

### VERSE 18

Then the sons of Aaron cried out. The priests of Christ presented preaching through the passion brought to completion. The trumpets are rightly called “hammered,” because preachers grow all the more as they are struck by the hammers of tribulations.

### VERSE 19

Then all the people, etc. When the ecclesiastical office is performed by the ministers of the altar in memory of Christ, the people, summoned to the praise of God, prostrate themselves on their faces—that is, they display the humility of their heart.

To offer prayers to the Almighty. Because whatever is done out of love of God is prayer and an odor of sweetness before God. The whole Church strives to persevere in prayer until the end of the world, when Christ’s body will be honored in incorruption and the members will be joined to their head.

[Col. 1230A] ### VERSE 21

And the people prayed, etc. (RAB.) Whatever is offered to God in the unity of faith is accepted by him; whatever is offered outside it is counted as impiety. A great sound arises in the Church when the whole people responds “Amen” to the priests praying and blessing. This sound pertains both to the cry of the voice and to the devotion of the heart.

[Col. 1230B] ### VERSE 22

Then, descending, etc. The assembly of the saints rejoicing.

He exalted. When he gives thanks for the completion of labor in the salvation of the whole people, then he multiplies praises and repeats prayer, because he never ceases from praises.

### VERSE 23

To show the power of God. That is, to preach his mercy, who gives us gladness of heart and peace in eternal times, so that all Israelite men and lovers of the eternal King may proclaim the power and goodness of God in the liberation of his people.

### VERSE 27

Two nations, etc. A twofold ruin: namely, the Gentiles, who have been defiled by idolatry, and by a vain way of life.

### VERSE 29

The teaching of wisdom, etc. He commends his work, showing how useful it is to the reader, the one who meditates, and the one who practices it.

## CHAPTER LI

### VERSE 1

The prayer of Jesus son of Sirach. It is better referred to the whole Church than to one person, because it describes in it many kinds of tribulation and diverse consolations.

I will confess to you, Lord the King. (RAB.) Jesus Christ is the helper and protector of his bride. He handed himself over for her so that he might free her from the destruction of original sin.

### VERSE 5

The gates of tribulations. These are the mouths of rulers and tyrants, from which threats and deceptions proceed and which compel the servants of God to deny the faith.

[Col. 1230D] ### VERSE 6

From the pressure of the flame. This happened bodily to the three youths in the furnace of fire; but all the saints are spiritually delivered from the heat of persecution.

### VERSE 9

And my life was drawing near to hell. Because the life of the flesh, failing each day, tends toward death. He calls death “hell,” because the death of the flesh is the punishment for the first sin, just as hell is the everlasting punishment of sinful souls.

### VERSE 10

They surrounded me on every side, etc. Seeing herself surrounded by enemies and lacking human consolation, the Church seeks help from God, from whom all good comes, and to him she attributes her deliverance from her enemies.

[Col. 1231A] ### VERSE 18

When I was still younger. (RAB.) In youth or childhood, etc., up to: how from infancy he sought wisdom.

Before I went astray, etc. He signifies that before the error of childhood or youth he desired wisdom, asked it of the Lord, and persevered in it until the very end.

### VERSE 19

Like an early grape. He compares the beauty of wisdom to an early grape, to show that delight is found in it. An early grape is so called because it ripens quickly.

### VERSE 24

I took counsel, etc. (RAB.) First he says that he made a decision to practice it, etc., up to [Col. 1232A]: for thus strengthened, he will arrive at the fruit of wisdom.

### VERSE 29

My belly. Moved to repentance through knowledge of wisdom.

Therefore. To attain the perfection of wisdom is not a matter of human effort but of a divine gift.

### VERSE 30

The Lord gave me, etc. An instructed tongue is a good reward, for it enabled him to instruct and correct brothers.

### VERSE 37

Let the soul rejoice. Great is the gladness of the heart if it remembers the mercy of the heavenly Judge.

[Col. 1231]

# THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. (G)*

## PROLOGUE OF SAINT JEROME ON THE PROPHET ISAIAH

(See Jerome on Isaiah, volume IV of his works.)

## THE LIFE OF ISAIAH

(From Epiphanius, *On the Lives of the Prophets*)

[Col. 1231B] Isaiah was born in Jerusalem of noble lineage, and prophesied there. Under King Manasseh he was cut into two parts and died. He was buried beneath the oak of Rogel, near the passage of the waters that King Hezekiah had once blocked by throwing in dust.

For God made the spring of Siloam on account of the Prophet, because, before he died, he prayed briefly that God might deign to produce waters there. Immediately God sent him living water from heaven. Hence that place received the name Siloam, which, if interpreted, means “sent down.”

Under King Hezekiah also, before he had built the pool and reservoirs, through Isaiah’s prayers it came about [Col. 1232B] that a small stream burst forth, because the people were being held under siege by enemies and the city might otherwise perish, deprived of water.

In perpetual memory of this event, the people carefully committed the Prophet to the ground there with glory and honor, so that through his intercessions the benefit of water of this kind might be obtained until the consummation of the age; they attributed the use of it, naturally, to him as a benefit received.

There is also a monument of Isaiah adjacent to the burial place of the rulers, beyond the tombs of the priests, toward the south and the southern region. For when Solomon was building Jerusalem, he raised mausoleums for the kings, just as David had described them.

## PREFACE ON ISAIAH

[Col. 1231]

[Col. 1231C] (JEROME on Isaiah.) Isaiah, a man of noble birth and polished eloquence, with nothing rustic in his speech, should be called not so much a prophet as an evangelist. For he sets forth the mysteries of Christ and the Church so clearly that he might be thought to be weaving a history of past events.

He prophesied in Jerusalem and Judah, before the ten tribes had been taken captive. Sometimes together and sometimes separately, he composed oracles concerning both kingdoms. Although at times he looks toward the present history and signifies the people’s return to Judea after the Babylonian captivity, he directs all his concern toward the calling of the Gentiles and the coming of Christ.

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 1231D] ### VERSE 1

The vision of Isaiah, etc. There are three kinds of vision. The first is bodily, by which we see heaven, earth, and things of this sort. The second is spiritual, by which, as in dreams, we see images of human beings and things of this sort. The third is intellectual, which exists in reason and through which we know the Creator and, with the Holy Spirit [Col. 1232C] revealing it, understand anything whatsoever.

“To see” is also often used for “to understand.” Hence we often ask, saying, “Do you see?”—that is, “Do you understand?” Prophets are likewise called “seers” for this reason—that is, “those who understand.”

Isaiah saw this vision through the Holy Spirit: namely, he understood what was going to happen, because the Spirit disclosed it inwardly. Hence at the beginning he does not set forth visions, as Daniel does, nor say what he saw; instead, he immediately says: “Hear, O heavens, and listen with your ears, O earth.”

(JEROME on Isaiah, vol. IV.) Not only Isaiah, etc., up to: therefore, according to Montanus, they did not remain ignorant, since they saw in this way.

(ID., ibid.) Isaiah is interpreted, etc., up to [Col. 1232D]: and when he has done everything, he says: “I am an unworthy servant; I have done what I ought to do.”

Sons of Amos. (ID., ibid.) Amos, the father of Isaiah, is not the third of the Twelve Prophets, etc., up to: they contend that they were prophets.

Concerning Judah and Jerusalem. (ID., ibid.) Isaiah speaks principally [Col. 1233A] about the two tribes, etc., up to: these things were foretold for the correction of the two tribes.

The vision of Isaiah, etc. (JEROME, ibid.) In place of Judah, in which the two tribes are signified, etc., up to: concerning her it is said, “Arise, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come.”

In the days of Uzziah. (ID., ibid.) Uzziah is the same person as Azariah, etc., up to: so that they may appear older than the Gentiles in our history.

### VERSE 2

Hear, O heavens, etc. (ID., ibid.) Above he identified who the Prophet was, etc., up to: since this belongs to God’s power, not to earthly understanding.

The Lord has spoken. (ID., ibid.) “Not to you, but to me,” so that I may report to you what I heard in the spirit, since you are not worthy to hear him himself.

I have nourished sons. (ID., ibid.) When he says, “I adopted them as sons,” etc., up to [Col. 1233B]: hence, “He gave them power to become sons of God.”

### VERSE 3

The ox knows, etc. (ID., ibid.) Hence: “You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together” (Deut. 22). Like Ebion, etc., up to: to whom it is said, “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened.”

The ass. The Gentile, or the converted libertine—formerly unclean and burdened with sins—who believed in Christ’s incarnation. As soon as he was born, Christ was laid in a manger, so that by the bridle of his flesh he might refresh everyone.

Israel. (JEROME, as above.) The scribes and Pharisees, who possess the key of knowledge and of the Law. Hence they were called Israel, “those who see God.”

He did not know me. Namely, the one whose day Abraham saw and rejoiced (John 8), whose coming [Col. 1233C] the chorus of prophets foretold while awaiting it.

### VERSE 4

Woe to the nation, etc. (JEROME, ibid.) In this heading he recalls the person, the cause, and the time. Secondly, he makes his hearers attentive. Thirdly, he relates what the Lord said. Fourthly, as though in an outburst, he rebukes the sinful nation.

Woe to the nation, etc. He threatens eternal destruction because they reject the Son, who brought salvation.

Iniquity. (ID., ibid.) Hence: “Iniquity sits upon a talent of lead” (Zech. 5). Elsewhere also: “They are burdened with a heavy load against me” (Ps. 37).

Wicked. Others read “of the most wicked,” so that the fault belongs not to the seed but to the wickedness of those who abandoned God by their own will. For one must not think that good and evil have different natures.

[Col. 1233D] They blasphemed. Saying: “You have a demon, and you are a Samaritan” (John 8); and, “We have no king but Caesar”; and, “Is this not the son of the carpenter?”

They have become estranged. (JEROME, ibid.) Those who were called the portion and sons of God (John 19; Matt. 13). It is said of them: “The sons of strangers have lied to me” (Ps. 17). Hence: “No one who puts his hand to the plow,” etc. (Luke 9); hence the Apostle: “Reaching forward to what lies ahead and forgetting what is behind” (Phil. 3).

### VERSE 5

Upon what part shall I strike you, etc. (ID., ibid.) As though he said, etc., up to [Col. 1234A]: but he shows that there is now no place suitable for medicine in this way: “Every head is sick,” etc.

Every head is sick. (ID., ibid.) Just as the joy of the mind sometimes alleviates bodily pains, etc., up to: hence, “From the sole of the foot,” etc.

### VERSE 6

Wound and bruise. (ID., ibid.) As though he said, etc., up to: and they killed the merciful physician sent to them.

Not treated with medicine. (ID., ibid.) Hence: “We treated Babylon, and it was not healed”—namely, the city of confusion and vices, etc., up to: and he expressed the irremediable captivity of the Jews.

### VERSE 7

Your land is desolate, etc. (ID., ibid.) These things were partly fulfilled under the Babylonians, etc., up to: hence, “Unless the Lord guards the city, the watchman keeps watch in vain,” etc.

### VERSE 8

The daughter of Zion, etc. (ID., ibid.) This is the affection of a most loving father. And: “By nature we are all sons of God” [Col. 1234B] (John 14), but by our fault we become strangers. Hence Babylon is often called a daughter.

### VERSE 9

Unless the Lord. (ID.) This is spoken in the person of the Prophet, etc., up to: thus the Almighty is the Son of the Almighty.

### VERSE 10

Hear the word. (ID.) After the remnant has been saved, etc., up to: and now it is perceived by the mind, when he is believed to be invisible.

### VERSE 11

I am full. (ID.) As though he said: “Do you think that I need these things or delight in them? I am full”—that is, I lack nothing. “The earth and its fullness are mine.” Or, “I am full”—that is, I am wearied, because you do not offer properly.

Burnt offerings of rams, etc., up to: “Judge for the orphan,” etc. He rejects the sacrifices of the Jews and commends obedience [Col. 1234C] to the Gospel: “Burnt offerings of rams,” etc. He indicates the final destruction of the temple, which continues forever. For after the Babylonian captivity, the temple was built by Zerubbabel, and sacrifices were offered in it for a long time.

(ID.) Burnt offerings of rams. This can also be understood of those who, while despising God’s commandments, wish to appease him by a multitude of sacrifices and purchase permission to sin; or of those who offer robbery and greed upon the altar and give them to the poor.

I did not desire. By using the past tense, he shows that he never loved the sacrifices of the Jews, but tolerated them for a time because of what they signified; and, once the true sacrifice had been fulfilled, he regarded them as nothing.

### VERSE 12

When you came. (ID.) God did not [Col. 1234D] seek these sacrifices as though he needed them, but so that they would not sacrifice to demons and so that through bodily and typological things they might more easily reach the spiritual and true sacrifice.

Who asked for this? Let the Ebionites hear this, who think that after Christ’s passion the Law must still be observed. Let their associates hear this as well, who decree that it is to be kept only by the Israelite race.

### VERSE 13

The new moon, etc. The festival of the new moon, which they celebrated at the beginning of the months: *neos*, “new”; *mene*, “moon.” Hence: “Blow the trumpet to the Lord at the new moon” (Ps. 80).

Your assemblies are wicked, etc. (ID.) Because they do not offer spiritual sacrifices. Hence: “A sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit” (Ps. 50).

[Col. 1235A] ### VERSE 14

My soul has hated. (ID.) Ἀνθρωποπαθῶς (*anthropopathically*). Not because he has a soul, but he speaks according to our manner—as though he said, “I have utterly hated them.”

I have labored, etc. (JEROME.) Symmachus: “I have failed through pity,” etc., up to: but you will be saved by my help alone.

### VERSE 15

For your hands are full of blood, etc. (ID.) The blood of the prophets and finally of their Lord, etc., up to: they keep watch in prayer day and night.

### VERSE 16

Wash yourselves, etc. As though he said: “This is what I hated; the truth of the Gospel is pleasing.” Wash yourselves with the blood of Christ and the water of baptism. Be clean, remaining innocent in life. For baptism alone can bring remission of sin. Hence: “Unless one is reborn” (John 3), etc. And elsewhere: [Col. 1235B] “Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father,” etc.

(JEROME, as above.) The chief order, etc., up to: but also in the sight of God, from whom nothing can be hidden.

Cease to act perversely. (ID.) This echoes the Gospel, etc., up to: whom those who shine with the brightness of virginity follow in the Apocalypse.

### VERSE 17

Learn to do good. (ID.) Not trusting in nature, etc., up to: the thresholds of teachers must be worn smooth.

Seek justice, etc. (ID.) The commands of the Gospel succeed the sacrifices of the Jews. Care is provided for orphans and widows, so that martyrs, secure concerning wives and children, may go forth to battle.

[Col. 1235C] ### VERSE 18

Though they be scarlet, etc. Scarlet and crimson are the same, and “worm-colored” likewise: namely, great sin, murder, adultery, etc. What is signified by snow is signified by wool: the cleansing and washing away of sins.

Like snow. Because they will be cold toward the incitements of vices; and like wool, because they will be clothed against the cold of unbelief.

White wool, etc. From which Christ’s garment is made.

### VERSE 19

If you are willing and listen, etc. (ID.) Free will is preserved, etc., up to: religious observance would pass into the praise of God.

(ID.) Morally: while the faithful soul, full of judgment, obeys God, God dwells in it, and he is the justice that justifies. But if it departs from God—not in place but in merit—it is inhabited by malignant spirits, who are murderers [Col. 1235D] of souls.

### VERSE 21

Justice. (ID.) “Justice” in Hebrew is *ṣedeq*, which more properly signifies “just,” so that we may understand the Lord to have dwelt in her, concerning whom it is said: “But the Just One—what did he do?” This is signified in Ezekiel by Oholibah, which is interpreted as “tent,” or “my tent in her.”

### VERSE 22

Silver, etc. Those who were clear and bright have returned to vices.

Into dross. (ID.) Dross, in Hebrew *siggim*, is the rust of metals, or the refuse and filth that are purified by fire.

Your wine, etc. Others: “Your wine merchants mix wine with water.” Symmachus: “Your wine has been mixed [Col. 1236A] with water.” Morally: “Your wine has been mixed with water,” because he softens the precepts of Holy Scripture, by which they ought to correct their hearers, according to their hearers’ wishes; by mixing in his own interpretation, he corrupts the wine.

Your wine, etc. Heretics also corrupt the Gospel. They are the worst wine merchants, making water out of wine, when the Lord turned water into wine—a deed that the steward marveled at—and when the queen of Sheba praised the cupbearers and wine servers at Solomon’s banquet.

### VERSE 23

Companions of thieves. (ID.) They accepted gifts from the scribes and Pharisees, gifts that those men had taken from the poor. At the Lord’s passion also they were unbelievers, unwilling to believe in Christ, and companions of thieves—namely, the scribes, Pharisees, and Judas the traitor.

Companions of thieves, etc. We too must beware lest we accept gifts from those who gather wealth from the tears of the poor, lest we become companions [Col. 1236B] of thieves and it be said of us: “If you saw a thief, you ran with him,” etc.

Retributions follow. (ID.) Because they do not regard them as friends, etc., up to: that is, endure patiently.

### VERSE 24

The Mighty One of Israel. (ID.) The Septuagint: “Woe to the mighty ones of Israel,” etc., up to: or in conduct.

Alas, I. In the affection of a loving father, he laments and strikes them, although they are enemies, because they are perishing and do not wish to repent.

I will be consoled, etc. (ID.) He is consoled by vengeance, etc., up to: in which he signifies that they will suffer torments.

### VERSE 25

Your tin. (ID.) The false teaching of the scribes and Pharisees, which resembles [Col. 1236C] the true, as tin resembles silver. And I will give a pure and perfect knowledge of the Law and the Gospel.

### VERSE 26

And I will restore your judges, etc. (ID.) Not only after the captivity, such as Zerubbabel, Ezra, and others who governed the people down to Hyrcanus, but also after the Lord’s coming: the Apostles and other teachers of the Church.

The city of the Just One, the faithful city Zion, will be redeemed in judgment. The Church is the place in which people are recalled to live justly. A city is, in fact, a gathering of people for the purpose of living justly.

[Col. 1236C] ### VERSE 30

Like an oak with falling leaves. (ID.) As an oak shaken by dryness, etc., up to: it does not even produce vegetables for a sick person to eat.

## CHAPTER II

[Col. 1236D] ### VERSE 2

In the last days. (JEROME.) Of which Jacob said, etc., up to: “It grew into a great mountain.”

The mountain. The mountains are angels, prophets, patriarchs, apostles, martyrs, and others who shone with miracles. The hills are lesser figures, receiving light from their greater ones.

And it will be exalted. (ID.) Above all the saints, because all receive from his fullness (concerning whom it is said: “The mountains surround him”), and because of the mountain—Christ—they are called mountains.

### VERSE 3

The house. (ID.) This is said so that we may accept the Old Testament and not, like Mani, seek another house of God than the house of Jacob.

[Col. 1237A] His ways, which others have worn smooth. The Lord also, ascending the mountain, taught his disciples. First, therefore, the ways must be learned; afterward one must walk in the paths.

From Zion. (JEROME.) Not from the rock of Sinai, but from Mount Zion, on which Jerusalem stands, where the temple and the worship of God are found. The Lord also taught in the temple, because the Prophet ought not to die outside Jerusalem.

The Law and the word. As above, he placed “word” and “law” together, so that rulers might hear the word and the people receive the law with their ears. Whoever fulfills the Law will reach the word of God; the Law will go forth from the word as from a spring, to water others.

### VERSE 4

And they will turn their swords, etc. (ID.) Every concern with waging war will be turned into peace, etc., up to: “Let us eat in the time of harvest,” namely, [Col. 1237B] of death.

### VERSE 5

House of Jacob, etc. (ID.) After the calling of the Gentiles and the manifestation of God’s mountain, he invites his people, who are from Jacob, to leave the darkness of unbelief and receive the light of Christ.

In the light. (ID.) “While you have the light, believe in the light.” Draw near to him and be enlightened, etc. As though he said: “Whoever does evil hates the light; but come with me, let us walk in the light of the Lord,” who says: “I am the light of the world,” etc.

### VERSE 6

For you have rejected. After exhorting them, he saw their hardness in the spirit and suddenly turned the eyes of his mind toward the Lord, saying: “For you have rejected,” etc. It is as though he said: “They must therefore be exhorted, because you have rejected,” etc.

[Col. 1237C] Because they have been filled, as formerly, etc. (ID.) When the Romans drove them out, foreigners lived in Judea—people brought from everywhere by Titus and Vespasian or by the other rulers. Or, before they were devastated by the Babylonians, they committed these things under impious kings.

Like the Philistines. (ID.) The Philistines, who are today called Palestinians, because the Hebrew language does not have the letter *p* but uses the Greek phi, φ, in its place.

With boys, etc. He signifies the lust of the conquerors toward the Jewish nation. For Greeks and Latins long suffered from this vice; but under the emperor Constantine, when the Gospel shone forth, this shameful practice, along with other evils, was suppressed.

[Col. 1237D] ### VERSE 7

The land is filled. (ID.) The greed of both Romans and Jews is censured; for Greek and Latin histories testify that neither people was more avaricious. Among the idols, avarice is condemned.

### VERSE 8

With horses and innumerable, etc. (ID.) This too is against the Lord, who prohibited the multiplication of chariots and horses. For these animals were given to help, not to encourage pride; hence they are also called beasts of burden.

### VERSE 9

He bowed down. Where once there was the temple and the worship of God, there now stands a statue of Hadrian and an idol of Jupiter.

Therefore not. Isaiah does not curse, but blesses, etc., up to: and they were filled with idols, etc.

From the face of the fear of the Lord. From the anger of judgment.

And from the glory of his majesty. Because he will come with great power and majesty.

[Col. 1238A] ### VERSE 11

The eyes of the lofty, etc. (JEROME.) Neither riches, nor power, nor nobility of lineage will save anyone; one captivity will come upon all. These words can also be understood of the day of judgment, when every creature will be humbled in the sight of God and will recognize itself as nothing in comparison with him.

But the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.

### VERSE 12

The Lord of hosts. Whenever he speaks of the Lord’s victory or vengeance, he mentions him as the Lord of hosts, so that we may not doubt the victory of the one whose power is so great.

### VERSE 14

High mountains. (JEROME.) Because of the variety of virtues, some are called mountains of the good and others hills. Because of the diversity of vices, some are mountains of the wicked and others hills, to whom it is said: “I will bring the sword [Col. 1238B] upon you,” etc.

And upon every tower. (ID.) Literally: when the Romans came, the towers and walls were utterly overthrown, etc., up to: so that a perverse doctrine might not prevail over the truth.

### VERSE 16

Ships. (ID.) Jehoshaphat had ships that he sent to Tarshish, etc., up to: there are also good ships, of which it is said: “Those who go down to the sea in ships,” etc.

Tarshish. (ID.) Of any sea, etc., up to: if it is said otherwise, it is Syriac.

### VERSE 17

Every one will be bowed down. (ID.) Allegorically: human speech appears rational, etc., up to: they too will be utterly crushed by the one by whom they were fashioned.

[Col. 1238C] ### VERSE 18

And the idols completely. This occurred in the captivity of the Chaldeans, etc., up to: this must especially be referred to the earlier meaning.

(BED.) Solomon built the idol Astarte of the Sidonians in Jerusalem, etc. Here, unless I am mistaken, it is shown that Solomon never fully repented, because he did not destroy the idols he had built.

### VERSE 20

To worship moles. (JEROME.) Not literally, but “like moles,” etc., up to: by which the truth is reached.

### VERSE 22

Cease, therefore. These things will happen unless you cease. Cease, therefore, from raging against Christ, who appears to be merely a pure man, because he breathes through his nostrils and lives like other human beings.

Exalted. “The Lord is exalted above all nations.” [Col. 1238D] “And the Most High himself founded it” (Ps. 112; 89). Nevertheless, the Hebrew signifies “exalted,” not “the Exalted One.” For he himself is the height itself, not merely one who is high.

## CHAPTER III

### VERSE 1

For behold. Up to this point they think he is speaking about judgment, etc., up to: after all the gifts of grace had been taken away from the Jews.

### VERSE 2

The warrior. (JEROME.) Among the Jews there is no one who fights for the Law or judges according to it; for all are vain and foolish.

And the diviner. Because sometimes they divine truly, like Balaam, and the diviners of the five cities of Palestine, on whose advice the ark of the Lord was sent back. It is as though he said: [Col. 1239A] both true and false prophets will be taken away from the Jews.

The elder. The Septuagint translated this as “presbyter,” etc., up to: because he refused to listen to the presbyters.

### VERSE 3

The prudent man. A teacher or hearer, etc., up to: those who could discern by what spirit the prophets were speaking.

Of the architects. Christ himself is called the Son of the carpenter, and in Chronicles we read of the Valley of Craftsmen. There were craftsmen there whom knowledge did not puff up, but who followed the humble Christ.

### VERSE 4

And I will give, children. (JEROME.) Although the other words are spoken in the person of, etc., up to: the Apostle prohibits a neophyte from being chosen as bishop, lest he become proud like the devil.

Effeminate. The Septuagint: “mockers,” etc., up to: the holy condition of the Church is brought into confusion.

[Col. 1239B] ### VERSE 6

He will seize. Literally, etc., up to: and may our ruin be sustained by your help.

### VERSE 7

He will answer. (JEROME.) This is not found in the Hebrew, but is added from the Septuagint. According to the Hebrew, it is joined in this way: “On that day he will say:

I am not a physician.” We must not immediately submit to the judgment of the multitude, etc., up to: “Do not seek to become a judge, lest you be unable to offer the iniquities” (Eccl. 7).

### VERSE 8

For Jerusalem has fallen. In the person of the Prophet. As though he said: “For this reason they will find no one willing to help them, because they blasphemed the Lord, saying: ‘You have a demon’” (John 8), and similar things.

Because the tongue. Although the Romans came to besiege them, so far as their own interests were concerned, because the tribute had been refused, nevertheless the Lord’s death was chiefly the cause.

[Col. 1239C] ### VERSE 9

Recognition. They will recognize that this happened because of their sins, or they will always have their sins before the eyes of their mind.

Woe to their soul. (ID.) The Septuagint: “Woe to their soul, because they devised an evil plan against themselves, saying: ‘Let us bind the righteous one, for he is of no use to us’” (Wis. 1).

(ID.) Let us therefore beware lest we become exactors among the people; lest, in the manner of the impious Porphyry, matrons and women become our senate, ruling in the Churches, and lest the favor of women determine judgment concerning the priestly rank.

### VERSE 12

And the way of their steps, etc. (ID.) Therefore that man is the ecclesiastical teacher, etc., up to: concerning which he says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14).

### VERSE 13

He stands to judge. (ID.) Now, as though [Col. 1239D] angered, etc., up to: he comes against the rulers and presbyters to judge, giving them an opportunity for defense.

### VERSE 14

For you have devoured. (ID.) I think that what existed among the elders and rulers of the ancient people is what exists among the presbyters and bishops of our own time.

My vineyard. (ID.) “You brought a vine out of Egypt.” “The vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel” (Ps. 79).

### VERSE 15

Why do you crush my people? Our rulers also, etc., up to: they make the wealth of themselves or of their own people their own.

### VERSE 16

Because they are exalted. This can refer especially to the wives of the scribes and Pharisees, and also to others. On account of their luxuries and extravagance, their husbands stripped the poor. Therefore, so that they would not consider themselves free [Col. 1240A] from sin, the Lord says: “Because,” etc.

### VERSE 17

He will make bald. What is hidden will be exposed, and shameful baldness will appear. For nothing is covered that will not be revealed.

### VERSE 18

On that day—that is, on the day of the Babylonian captivity, or, more truly, when they were captured by the Romans and lost all their ornaments.

Of the shoes. They were not worn out in the wilderness, etc., up to: so that instead of the cleanliness of a married woman, the filth of the earth may appear.

### VERSE 21

Rings. By these we are sealed in the image of Christ, whom the Father sealed. The prodigal son also received a ring together with the robe and sandals.

[Col. 1240B] Gems on the forehead. By these our faces and head are adorned.

### VERSE 22

Linen garments. (JEROME.) So that we may enjoy broad delights in the Lord.

### VERSE 23

Ribbons. They bind the mind as it flows this way and that.

*Theristra*. A very delicate, transparent woman’s garment, suitable for summer; it is so named because *theria* means “summer.”

### VERSE 24

A haircloth breast-band. By this the breasts are chastised, lest they swell excessively.

### VERSE 26

And they will mourn, and… Whoever gives place to the devil and does not guard his heart with all vigilance—his gates will mourn; and, with the bridegroom absent, he will always remain in mourning, and, falling into the dust, will [Col. 1240C] sit there.

His gates will mourn, and she will sit desolate upon the ground. By metonymy: judges, kings, and rulers who were accustomed to sit at the gate.

## CHAPTER IV

### VERSE 1

And seven will seize. (JEROME.) When Nebuchadnezzar took King Zedekiah, etc., up to: in this passage we can understand several things.

Seven women. (ID.) The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and he will fill him with the spirit of the fear of the Lord.

They are called women because no one is born for God except through the Spirit; and they are spoken of in the plural because there are several gifts, although the Spirit is one.

[Col. 1240D] **Our bread.** Our bread is Christ, the rod from the root of Jesse, and the flower; the bread of the women is the Father, as also of Christ, who says: “My food is to do the will of my Father” (John 4). “We shall eat our bread”: the body of Christ.

**We shall cover ourselves with our garments.** With the ornaments of virtues.

**Let your name be invoked.** Let us be called Christians from Christ.

**Take away the reproach.** The reproach that we suffer from the Jews as though we were without God, etc., up to the point at which we are often compelled to change our lodging.

**Take away.** Because they will rise up against the wisdom of false doctrine and against the other women, that is, the virtues: each thing’s opposite rises up against it when false virtues steal their name.

[Col. 1241A] **VERSE 5.—A cloud,** that is, the overshadowing of the Spirit, so that they may not be lifted up in prosperity, just as the cloud was over the children of Israel by day and the fire by night.

**And smoke, etc.** (HIER.) Hence: “The house was filled with smoke” (Exodus 13); and elsewhere: “He touches the mountains, and they smoke” (Psalm 103).

**For over all.** Most of the Jews, etc., up to our own time, however, at the first coming of Christ.

## CHAPTER V

**VERSE 1.—I shall sing for my beloved, etc.** (HIER.) A song is sometimes sung in joy and sometimes in sorrow, as in this case: namely, the song composed by the one who, seeing the city, wept and said: “For if you also had known,” etc. (Luke 19).

**VERSE 2.—A chosen vineyard.** (ID.) Another edition has *a vineyard of Sorec*, which is a kind of excellent vine, exceedingly fruitful with perpetual produce. Everything said concerning the vineyard refers to the condition of the soul, which, planted by God, produced not grapes but wild grapes; and it was handed over to beasts to be trampled, nor did it receive the rain of teaching, because it despised the gifts formerly given.

**VERSE 3.—Now therefore, inhabitants, etc.** Similarly, Nathan questions David so that he might pronounce judgment concerning himself as though concerning another.

**VERSE 4.—Or what was there that I expected, etc.?** According to some, he said the preceding words to himself, but here he questions others about what he had considered.

**VERSE 5.—And now I shall show you.** As though he said: “Because you do not wish to answer, I shall answer for you.”

[Col. 1241C] **I shall take away, etc.** So that those who did not recognize God through benefits may recognize him through punishments; and therefore he threatens punishment so that they may turn to repentance.

**VERSE 6.—And to the clouds.** (ID.) Those which existed under Elijah, etc., up to the time when they had neither prophets nor accepted apostles.

**VERSE 7.—The house of Israel, etc.** (ID.) From the time when the kingdom was divided, etc., up to the point that Christ was born from them.

**Behold, a cry.** With which he cried out against the Lord and shouted, saying: “Take away, take away, crucify him”; or they raised a cry for justice because they killed Christ, whose blood cries out to the Lord: “The voice of your brother Abel’s blood cries to me from the ground” (Genesis 4).

[Col. 1241D] **VERSE 8.—Woe to you who join house to house.** This is directed especially against the Jews, who are exceedingly greedy, etc., until the earth fails—that is, human understanding and speech fail.

**VERSE 9.—In the ears.** (ID.) As though the prophet said: “I heard these words with my inner ears; they are the words of the Lord of hosts.”

**Unless the houses, etc.** Namely, the pomp and construction of heretics, etc., up to the one who is constrained by unity in comparison with the multitude of the number.

**VERSE 10.—For ten acres.** (ID.) The barrenness of the land that will follow the captivity is indicated.

**VERSE 11.—Woe to those who rise early.** As though he said: “Captivity is imminent,” etc., up to the point that they do not understand the works of the Lord within themselves.

[Col. 1242A] **VERSE 17.—And lambs shall feed.** (ID.) According to the historical sense, this means the same as above: foreigners devour your region before your eyes.

**Foreigners.** “The kingdom of God will be taken away from you,” etc. For, gathered from the whole world, etc., up to the point that the lambs might occupy the places of the bulls.

**VERSE 18.—Woe to those who drag.** This is directed against the rulers of the Jews, etc., up to the point that they anathematize the name of Christians.

**With cords of vanity.** (ID.) In which they were, etc., up to the point that we are held as though by the strongest bonds.

**VERSE 19.—Woe to those who say.** (ID.) This is directed especially against the Jews, who chose Barabbas and condemned Christ; generally, against all who justify the unjust and condemn the just. “Evil,” “darkness,” and “bitter” are set down with a similar meaning and figure. In Barabbas we understand the devil, concerning whom it is said: “Deliver us from evil.”

[Col. 1242B] **VERSE 21.—Woe to those who are wise.** They despise the wisdom of God, etc., up to the point that they neither enter to Christ nor permit others to enter.

**VERSE 22.—Drunkenness.** Wine contains every vice. Drunkenness—which in Hebrew is *shekhar*—signifies everything that overturns the condition of the mind. Through an abundance of bread and wine, the sin of the Sodomites increased.

**VERSE 23.—Who justify the wicked for gifts.** It was said above that, instead of grapes, they produced thorns, hay, wood, straw, and burning briars, because they not only did these things but also rejected the Law [Col. 1242C] and blasphemed the word of God. Concerning them it is said: “From Zion the law shall go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

**VERSE 24.—Their root.** (ID.) A wicked thought, from which the deed proceeds like a shoot.

**VERSE 25.—Therefore he was angry.** (ID.) It should be noted that he does not reproach them for idolatry and the other sins, but because they rejected the law of the Gospel and blasphemed the Lord’s holy word. He had been angry against the rulers and the powerful, who were wise in their own eyes and pursued gifts; the tongue of fire devoured them, so that the powerful might suffer powerful torments.

**He was angry.** (ID.) Not because he is subject to human passions, but because, when we sin, unless we hear that the Lord is angry, we do not fear.

[Col. 1242D] **And he struck, etc.** He speaks of future things as though they were past, in prophetic certainty.

**VERSE 26.—And he will hiss for him from the ends of the earth, etc.** (ID.) The Hebrews understand this passage of the Babylonians, etc., up to the point at which he joins himself to the people in affection and says:

**VERSE 30.—We shall look.** They did not dare to look back toward heaven, whose inhabitant, God, they had offended; and our light, which we always had in God, has been darkened by the gloom of tribulations.

## CHAPTER VI

**VERSE 1.—In the year, etc.** (HIER.) Uzziah himself is Azariah, etc., up to the point at which, falling on his face, he cries to the Lord with a loud voice.

[Col. 1243A] **King Uzziah.** Namely, the leprous king who usurped the priesthood.

**I saw the Lord.** Namely, Christ. The Son was seen in the appearance of one reigning; the Holy Spirit spoke because of the sharing of majesty and the unity of substance.

**Upon a high and exalted throne, etc.** (HIER.) Whoever sees the Lord reigning among the heavenly powers sees him upon a high and exalted throne, which signifies the Thrones and Dominions, etc.

Some say that the seraphim are powers in heaven standing before and praising God, who are sent in service especially to those who need purification and, because of certain sins, punishment to some degree.

(ID.) The cherubim signify a multitude of knowledge, upon whom the Lord is shown to sit in the manner of a charioteer; hence: “You who sit upon the cherubim,” etc. I do not remember having read of seraphim in the canonical Scriptures anywhere except in this passage. Therefore those who customarily write in their prayers, “You who sit upon the cherubim and seraphim,” are mistaken.

**VERSE 2.—They stood.** (ID.) That is, they stand in attendance upon God; they fly, demonstrating God; they uncover, as it were, half; they do not reveal what is veiled, nor veil what is known.

**Six wings for one.** (ID.) Victorinus understands the twelve apostles. We, however, understand the twelve stones of the altar untouched by iron, and the twelve gems in the priest’s diadem.

(ID.) Angels are said to have wings because they dwell in higher places [Col. 1243C], or because of their swift movement everywhere, just as winds are also called winged.

**With two they covered his face.** I do not know what existed before these things, etc., up to the point that angels and preachers likewise teach nothing about it; similarly:

**They covered their feet.** (HIER.) We do not know what will happen after this world. Yet we know the intermediate things that were made or are made during the six days or ages. “With two they covered,” because we have knowledge only of the present.

(ID.) My Hebrew commentator entered by a very different path, etc., up to the point at which, then truly purified in lips, I said to the Lord: “Behold, here I am; send me.”

**VERSE 3.—And they cried out.** (ID.) They do not speak softly, but proclaim by shouting a confession that brings salvation to all: [Col. 1243D] “Holy, holy, holy,” because they themselves, namely the seraphim, are holy; for nothing is holier than these. They marvel, however, that the Son humbled himself so greatly, underwent the cross, and became known among earthly beings.

**Holy, holy, etc.** The mystery of the Trinity. The Trinity is proclaimed in both Testaments: the Lord Christ, namely, who here is represented by four letters, which are properly used of God: *Yod, He, Yod, He*—that is, two *Yah*s, which, doubled, form the ineffable name of God.

**The whole earth is full.** (ID.) “And it shall be filled,” etc., up to the point of two and forty years after the Lord’s Passion.

**VERSE 4.—The doorposts.** In the Old Testament the Lord spoke, etc., up to the point at which, receiving them, we say: “We know in part, and we prophesy in part” (1 Corinthians 13).

**VERSE 5.—Unclean.** (ID.) He says this because of his association with the people, with whom he was compelled to speak. It is harmful to live among sinners.

**I dwell.** Note that one must not remain among sinners.

**And I saw the King, the Lord of hosts, with my eyes; and one flew to me.** Thus Abraham, after he saw the Lord and heard his voice, confessed that he was ashes and dust, because however great human dignity may be, it becomes insignificant in comparison with him.

**VERSE 6.—From the seraphim.** (ID.) We say *seraphim* with *m* in the masculine gender and with *n* in the neuter plural. Yet *seraphim* can also be said in the singular, as can [Col. 1244B] *cherubim* and *cherub*.

**And in his hand.** That is, by his operation, namely Christ’s. The coal signifies charity, which he had taken from the altar with tongs—that is, the teaching of the two Testaments—and placed before Isaiah as an example.

**Coal.** (ID.) The Septuagint has *carbuncle*, a burning stone, which is called fiery because of its flame-colored appearance.

**With tongs.** (ID.) This is Jacob’s ladder, the two-edged sword, etc., up to the word of God grasping by the double edge of its commandments.

**From the altar.** The altar that John saw in the Apocalypse, full of burning coals by which sins can be cleansed.

**VERSE 7.—Behold, I have touched your lips.** Hence: “What shall be given to you, or what shall be added to you, for a deceitful tongue? The sharp arrows of the mighty one, with desolating coals” (Psalm 119). This is the word of God, concerning which it is said: “You have coals of fire; you shall sit upon them, and they will be your aid.”

**And iniquity shall be taken away.** (ID.) Jeremiah, who was a child and therefore almost free from sin, is cleansed by the touch of a hand alone. But to Isaiah, who says, “I am a man unclean in lips,” an angel is sent with a coal.

**VERSE 8.—Whom shall I send?** He does not compel but seeks the will; for only the will merits a reward. Isaiah, however, as one purified, offers himself willingly.

**Send me.** (ID.) He thinks he is about to announce something good, etc., up to the point that his offering of himself was not rashness but obedience.

[Col. 1244D] **VERSE 9.—Hear by hearing.** (ID.) Luke, according to the Septuagint, in the Acts of the Apostles, has: “With the ear you shall hear and shall not understand,” etc., up to the point that he uses testimonies from the Greeks more than from the Hebrews.

**VERSE 10.—Blind, etc.** (ID.) To which something similar applies, etc., up to the point that this is not God’s cruelty but mercy: while the faithless are blinded, the humble are enlightened.

**And be converted.** Although it is a grave sin, if someone converts, he can be saved. But these, because of the greatness of their crime, are unworthy of repentance.

**VERSE 13.—And still.** “And” means “still”: still a tithe from that nation, as though a tenth part of that nation would still remain.

**And it shall be.** Under Hadrian, Judea was again devastated, [Col. 1245A] in the fiftieth year after the captivity of the Romans. For the Jews were forbidden by public laws to enter Judea.

## CHAPTER VII

**VERSE 1.—And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz, etc.** (HIER.) What is written up to this point was seen under Uzziah and Jotham his son; what follows occurs under Ahaz, the most impious king, who, abandoned by God, was attacked by enemies.

**Ahaz.** He closed the doors of the temple and worshiped the Baals; he consecrated his son to an idol; he removed the bronze altar and placed an idolatrous altar in the temple. Therefore he was rightly abandoned by the Lord: “And enemies rose up against him” (2 Chronicles 28).

**He went up, the second time.** First, the Assyrians from the tribe of [Col. 1245B] Judah, etc., up to the point at which Herod and Pilate became friends during Christ’s Passion.

**VERSE 3.—He was abandoned.** By his brother Rabshakeh, who had gone over to the Assyrians, as the Hebrews relate.

**Jashub your son.** (ID.) He is interpreted as “the remaining companion” and “the one who converts”; the people of Judah was to be delivered from the hands of the two kings.

**On the road.** Rabshakeh was there; later, at Sennacherib’s command, he blasphemed God’s people.

**VERSE 4.—Two tails.** The two tails, etc., up to the point that he was led away with the ten tribes into the mountains of the Medes and Persians.

**VERSE 6.—Tabeel.** (ID.) *Tabeel* means “good God,” as though he were saying: “There let us set up the idol of our god”; or, literally, he calls him “son of man.”

[Col. 1245C] **VERSE 8.—Still sixty, etc.** As though he were saying: “In the meantime they will be content with their own boundaries; Rasin will rule Damascus as the metropolis of Syria, and Samaria will be the capital of the cities of Ephraim; in it the son of Romelia will reign for the time being.”

**Sixty-five years.** From the twenty-sixth year of Uzziah’s reign, when he was struck with leprosy, his son Jotham reigned for twenty-seven years while his father was still alive. After his death Jotham reigned for sixteen years, after whom Ahaz reigned for another sixteen; then Hezekiah reigned for six years. Ephraim—that is, the ten tribes—were led into captivity and ceased to be a people.

**VERSE 11.—Ask for a sign.** (ID.) So that the one who did not believe the prophet might be terrified by the Lord’s authority. As though he said: “It seems difficult to you that the most powerful kingdoms should soon come to an end, while you and your people are delivered; but ask for a sign.”

**Ask for a sign.** Moses received a sign from the earth, etc., up to the point that it concerns both the Lord’s death and his ascension.

**I shall not ask.** Not humbly, but arrogantly. For many are read to have asked the Lord for signs and received them; but Ahaz answered as though he possessed authority: “You shall not tempt the Lord your God.” Or he feared that God would be glorified in the sign and the idols made worthless.

**VERSE 14.—Behold, a virgin shall conceive.** (ID.) In Hebrew, *‘almāh*; in Latin also *alma* means “holy,” etc., up to the point that even fools can see that it arose violently.

**Emmanuel.** (ID.) Some say that Isaiah had two sons, etc., up to the point that the Word became flesh for her sake.

**VERSE 15.—To reject evil.** (ID.) As though he said: “Placed in the swaddling clothes of infancy, he will possess discernment between good and evil.” From these words we understand that the divine infancy of the Savior did not diminish the wisdom in him, although it is said: “The child grew in age and wisdom,” so that the reality of his human body might be demonstrated; infancy does not prejudice divine wisdom.

**VERSE 16.—It shall be forsaken, etc.** (ID.) As though he said: “The land of Syria and Samaria shall be devastated because of the invocation of his name, and the house of Judah shall be freed from the two kings.”

[Col. 1246B] **VERSE 18.—Flies.** (ID.) That is, the Egyptians, an unwarlike people polluted by idolatry. We read that Josiah was killed by the Egyptians and that the people of Israel was subjected to them; not long afterward, Nebuchadnezzar, with an innumerable army, captured Jerusalem, burned the temple, and settled Assyrians in Judea.

**VERSE 20.—A razor.** (ID.) The king of the Assyrians—who in Jeremiah is called “the dove of God”—will, as with an exceedingly sharp razor, shave in Judea the head and the hair of the feet, that is, all the strength of the kings, rulers, and subjects; and this will be done by those who are beyond the River, namely the Assyrians.

**VERSE 22.—He shall eat butter.** He will delight in Christ’s Passion or in his own. For butter is made from many ingredients.

**VERSE 25.—And all the mountains that shall be hoed with the hoe.** (ID.) Abandoning the plains out of fear of the enemy, they will flee to the mountains; cultivating the rugged mountain land with their own hands, they will sustain a wretched life. The rest will be for pasture.

## CHAPTER VIII

**VERSE 1.—And the Lord said to me: Take for yourself.** (HIER.) First the prophet foretells what is to happen to Ahaz, etc., up to the point at which the virgin birth is again described.

**Swiftly seize the spoil.** (ID.) This is the child’s name, as though he were saying: “Do not allow the devil to reign any longer; send neither angels nor prophets, but descend yourself.”

[Col. 1246D] **VERSE 2.—Uriah, etc.** (ID.) Uriah means “light of the Lord”; Zechariah, “memory of the Lord”; Berekiah, “blessing of the Lord.” The Lord’s birth is confirmed by these witnesses. Hence, beginning with Moses and the prophets, he explained to the two witnesses going to Emmaus what had been said concerning him.

**VERSE 3.—To the prophetess.** (ID.) To the Holy Spirit, from whom all prophecy comes. In Greek *pneuma* is neuter, in Hebrew *ruach* is feminine, and in Latin it is masculine; therefore it takes different grammatical forms, for it belongs to none of these genders. Or it refers to Mary, whom no one doubts to have been a prophetess.

**VERSE 4.—The child.** (ID.) Isaiah is therefore commanded, etc., up to the point that the house of David would be saved by the mere invocation of the name.

[Col. 1247A] **Because the people rejected the waters of Shiloah.** (HIER.) In which the blind man washed, etc., up to the point that he attempted to possess the land of Judah itself.

**VERSE 7.—The waters of the river.** (ID.) The army of Sennacherib, whose power, occupying the land of Samaria, is compared with the inundation of a river.

**VERSE 9.—Gather yourselves, peoples.** (ID.) As though he said: “You can do nothing against Emmanuel,” etc., up to the point that perversity cannot overcome what is straight.

**VERSE 12.—Do not say.** (ID.) As though he said: “Do not fear the conspiracy of the two kings against Judah; a conspiracy is the agreement of many for evil.”

**Do not fear or be terrified.** You and the people who are with you should not fear, although they appear formidable; for “the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.”

[Col. 1247B] **VERSE 14.—Into a stone.** (ID.) “Whom the builders rejected,” etc., up to the point that they join sins to sins and are bound by the snares of transgressions.

**To the two houses.** Or, to the two families, etc., up to the point that through their traditions they destroyed and defiled the precepts of the Law.

**VERSE 16.—Seal the law.** As though he said: “Open it, Lord, to my disciples,” etc., up to the point that we can also understand this as doctrines.

**VERSE 18.—My children, born of God.** The other prophets and their disciples. Some understand this of Isaiah’s two sons, etc., up to the point that they were a portent of the worldly wisdom and pride of the Jews.

**VERSE 20.—You shall not have it from them.** (ID.) That is, if this people does not wish to seek the truth from the Lord, it will not have Christ, namely the light of truth, which it neglects.

[Col. 1247C] **VERSE 21.—To his king.** To the devil and to the traditions of their fathers, that is, to ancient errors.

## CHAPTER IX

**VERSE 1.—At the first time.** (HIER.) These two tribes were led into captivity by the Assyrians, etc., up to the point that he first saw the light of Christ’s preaching.

**The land of Zebulun.** (ID.) In it Christ first preached and performed miracles: there he changed water into wine and chose the apostles.

**The way of the sea.** In this passage “sea” means Lake Gennesaret, formed by the inflow of the Jordan. On its shore are Capernaum, [Col. 1247D] Tiberias, Bethsaida, and Chorazin, where the Lord stayed most often; thus: “The people who walked in darkness saw a great light.”

**Galilee of the nations.** There are two Galilees: one of the nations, near Tyre, in the tribe of Naphtali; the other around Tiberias and the Lake of Gennesaret, in the tribe of Zebulun.

**VERSE 2.—In the region of the shadow of death.** (ID.) Those who still live in sins are in the shadow of death; those who have already descended to the underworld through dead works are in the region of the shadow of death.

**VERSE 3.—You have not increased the joy.** Our joy concerning the salvation of the Jews. For although they rejoice in the conversion of the nations, they grieve over the rejection of the Jews.

[Col. 1248A] **They shall rejoice before you, etc.** The prophet speaks to Christ concerning the disciples.

**VERSE 4.—For the yoke.** (ID.) Christ has a yoke, but it is easy; the devil also has one, but it is an unbearable burden. Christ has dominion upon his shoulder, on which he carried the cross; the devil has a rod upon his shoulder, with which he boasts.

**Of the exactor.** Of the one who exacts. Every day he demands from the descendants, with interest, the coin of sin that he entrusted to the first man.

**VERSE 5.—For every violent plundering.** (ID.) As though he said: “The human race, which the devil plundered, the Lord will violently—that is, powerfully—take away from him, and with tumult he will thrust him into hell.” Hence it is said both of him and of his members: “Their memory has perished with a sound” (Psalm 9).

**The garment mixed.** (ID.) The devil, who is filled with everyone’s blood and is a murderer from the beginning; or human beings, with whom the devil is clothed as with a garment, whose hands are full of blood.

**VERSE 6.—A child is born for us.** Not for the Jews, but for us, etc., up to the point that he is not seen by those who do not see the rising of the light.

**The dominion upon his shoulder.** (ID.) When he was led to the place of execution, he carried the cross, through which he merited dominion.

(ID.) The Septuagint has: “The angel of great counsel.” This is not found in the Hebrew; rather, terrified by the majesty of the names, they did not dare to say openly of the child that he should be called God. Therefore, in place of these six names, [Col. 1248C] they put this one: “the angel of great counsel.”

**VERSE 7.—The zeal of the Lord.** (ID.) The prophecy began with Emmanuel, where it says: “Ask a sign for yourself from God.” It ends here.

**VERSE 8.—The Lord sent a word.** (ID.) The Hebrew word is *dabar*, etc., up to the point that they despise the Church and regard her simplicity as ignorance.

**VERSE 10.—The bricks have fallen.** (ID.) They were saying above, etc., up to the point that “from strong and warlike rulers we shall fortify the people.”

**Cedars.** That is, “We shall appoint over them rulers from among us who cannot be conquered.”

## CHAPTER X

[Col. 1248D] **VERSE 1.—Woe to those who make.** (HIER.) Most still consider this to be spoken against the ten tribes, etc., up to the time when the day of captivity or judgment arrives.

**VERSE 5.—Woe to Assyria.** (ID.) Up to this point he has spoken against the ten and the two tribes, etc., up to the point that he not only led them into captivity but partly destroyed them.

**VERSE 7.—But he himself.** (ID.) So philosophers, so heretics, and so persecutors of the Christian name: when God permits some people to be scourged by them, they rage against all; they desire not to scourge but to kill, and after overcoming a few they take courage against all.

**VERSE 9.—Are not my princes together?** The order is: “Kings are my princes,” that is, serving me; for he brought many kings with him whom he had subjected.

[Col. 1249A] **Damascus.** Damascus is the metropolis of Syria. Eliezer, Abraham’s servant, founded it; Rasin reigned there.

**VERSE 10.—How has my hand found?** The voice of Sennacherib marveling at his own power. He completely fulfilled what he said. For he plundered all the cities of the ten tribes, and Judah and Benjamin except Jerusalem, as well as the lower part of Jerusalem itself, which Shebna the scribe handed over to him.

**VERSE 12.—When the Lord has completed.** The overthrow of the city, including the siege when Rabshakeh came and did the things recalled in what follows.

[Col. 1249B] **VERSE 14.—Ganniret.** *Gannire* is the cry of foxes, or, according to others, of birds.

**VERSE 16.—And beneath the glory.** Jerome says, according to the Hebrews, that the bodies of the slain Assyrians were burned by heavenly fire and reduced to dust, while their garments remained unharmed; the Jews came, grasped the edges of the garments, and shook out the dust.

(HIER.) Some wish this king to signify the opposing power, etc., up to the point that the Hebrews relate that only ten of his army survived.

**VERSE 17.—And the light shall be.** The Hebrews say that this was the archangel Michael, to whom the guardianship of that nation was entrusted, as Daniel says.

[Col. 1249C] **VERSE 18.—And the glory of the forest.** Mount Carmel is great and fruitful in trees. As though he were speaking of an innumerable army, like the trees of the forests: it will perish in body and soul.

**To the flesh.** (ID.) Heretics also, when ecclesiastical teaching has shone forth and their deception has been exposed, will come to such desolation that, from the forest and its fruitless trees and its innumerable multitude, scarcely a few will remain who follow their error.

**VERSE 20.—And it shall be in that day.** (HIER.) When Pekah and Rasin wished to come, etc., up to the point that they would place their hope in God.

**VERSE 21.—The remnant shall be converted.** According to Josephus, after an innumerable multitude of Jews had been killed, we understand that a few were saved among the apostles and apostolic men.

[Col. 1249D] **VERSE 22.—A shortened consummation.** The completion of what had been foretold concerning Christ for so long a time, completed in three and a half years.

**Justice.** Because, though he was unjustly killed, he justly conquered death and the devil, and redeemed the world by his death.

**VERSE 23.—For he shall make a consummation.** (ID.) Literally: he did this, because within the brief span of a single night he killed such a multitude, except for ten.

**VERSE 24.—Against you on the way of Egypt.** Of the captivity of the ten tribes, etc., up to the point that he captured and overthrew it.

**VERSE 25.—A little while, a very little while.** This was completed after a long period; yet all ages, compared with eternity—in which everything is present—are momentary.

[Col. 1250A] **VERSE 26.—His rod upon the sea.** (ID.) As though he said: “Before he comes against you, he will attack Tharaca, king of Ethiopia; he will cross the Red Sea, raise his rod over Egypt, and thus return with a large army against Jerusalem.”

**VERSE 29.—They passed swiftly.** Geba is a dwelling, etc. The past is used for the future according to prophetic usage.

**VERSES 31–32.—Strengthen yourselves; there is still a day.** (ID.) After Sennacherib had pitched his tents at Nob, intending to attack Jerusalem in the morning, he did not cease until midnight to threaten Jerusalem with desolation, saying: “Behold, will this single city be able to be rescued from my hand?”

[Col. 1250B] **VERSE 33.—Behold, the Lord, the ruler of hosts, etc.** He spoke of the child’s name, who was to be born of the virgin, etc., up to the point that Lebanon with its cedars would also be cut down.

## CHAPTER XI

**VERSE 1.—And a rod shall go forth.** (HIER.) Up to the beginning of the vision of Babylon, the prophecy concerns Christ; we explain it in parts so as not to confuse the reader’s memory.

**It shall go forth.** The Jews interpret the rod and the flower as Christ himself, etc., up to the point: “And you are my firstborn Son, who reign forever.”

**VERSE 2.—And the Spirit shall rest.** (ID.) Because the whole fullness of divinity dwells in him.

**Spirit.** Just as the word of the Lord is called light, life, and resurrection, etc., up to the point that these are the seven eyes in one stone according to Zechariah.

[Col. 1250C] **VERSE 3.—And the spirit shall fill him.** (ID.) Spiritually, because of the little ones who need fear, which perfect love casts out. For whoever fears has punishment and is not perfect in love.

**Not according to.** He will not accept a person’s status, because God is not a respecter of persons; rather, in every nation, whoever fears God is acceptable to him.

**He shall rebuke.** (ID.) The Pharisees and those who reproved the apostles when, walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, they plucked ears, rubbed them in their hands, and ate.

**VERSE 4.—With the rod of his mouth.** (ID.) The rod may be understood as the sentence of judgment. At the beginning of his preaching he said: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near”; and he added: “Every tree that does not produce good fruit shall be uprooted and cast into the fire.”

**VERSE 5.—He shall kill the wicked.** Even if Michael will kill him, as some say, God himself will nevertheless do this through Michael.

**Faith.** (HIER.) The faithful, by doing good, will cling to him who was made wisdom, righteousness, and sanctification, who says: “I am the light and the life.”

**VERSE 6.—The wolf with the lamb.** (ID.) Paul with Peter, hence: “Benjamin is a ravenous wolf,” and: “Feed my sheep.” The wolf will dwell with the lamb. It was not the lamb and kid that dwelt with the wolf and leopard, but the wolf and leopard; the lambs and kids imitate innocence, namely Christ.

**The wolf will dwell.** (HIER.) Our Judaizing Jews, etc., up to the point that they regard nothing as evil except shamefulness.

(ID.) The calf and the sheep are humble and innocent, etc., up to the point that the Church may provide this in the world.

**VERSE 7.—The lion like an ox, etc.** (ID.) The rulers of this age and other simple people are content with the surface of the historical account; for they do not understand the wheat and marrow, that is, the inner meaning.

**VERSE 8.—The infant.** Christ, or the apostles—little ones in malice, perfect in understanding—who cast demons out of possessed bodies.

**Little king-snakes.** The *regulus* is king of all serpents, etc., up to the point concerning possessed bodies.

[Col. 1251B] **The hand.** That is, he will hand over captive to the divine power the asp or little king-snake that has been grasped, namely the devil.

**VERSE 9.—For the earth is full.** In his customary manner, prophetic words are unfolded at the end so that they may not be taken literally.

**VERSE 10.—Who stands as a sign.** Hence: “Behold, this one is appointed for the fall and resurrection of many in Israel, and as a sign that will be opposed” (Luke 2). The Septuagint has: “Who will rise to be a prince,” etc., up to the point that it signifies the same thing as “tomb.” We translate *sepulchrum* as “tomb,” using a different word but the same meaning for “sleep” and “rest.”

**VERSE 11.—The remnant.** (ID.) The apostle says: “The remnant shall be saved.” For histories relate that the apostles, scattered throughout the whole world, preached the Gospel; indeed, they penetrated even to the Persians and Indians, so that Ethiopia might stretch out its hand to God.

**VERSE 12.—A sign.** Of the cross, in which there is victory, so that all may know where the devil was conquered.

**From the four quarters.** (ID.) This appears to have been fulfilled at Pentecost, etc., up to the point that the calling of the whole world might be demonstrated.

**VERSE 13.—And it shall be taken away, etc.** (ID.) When Isaiah foretold this, there was irreconcilable discord between the two tribes and the ten tribes; but those who believed were reconciled in the faith of Christ and the unity of charity.

**VERSE 14.—The command of the hand, etc.** What they command, they perform; they teach by word and by example.

**VERSE 15.—The tongue of the sea.** (ID.) The tongue that praised idols. [Col. 1251D] “Sea,” that is, the people of Egypt, who worship idols more than all others, so that they may praise and fear God and condemn and reject the idols.

**And he shall raise.** Just as Idumea, Moab, and the children of Ammon will surrender their hands to the apostles, so also will the Egyptians.

**And he shall strike.** That is, he will diminish it by appointing seven rulers in place of one, etc., up to the point that they might cross on dry feet.

**So that they may pass through it, etc.** Under the metaphor, the Nile is said to have been divided and cut into parts, etc., up to the point that the Lord prepares a way for the Gospel.

## CHAPTER XII

**VERSE 1.—I shall confess to you.** (HIER.) Just as, after crossing the Red Sea, they said: “Let us sing to the Lord,” etc., so, after the kingdom of the world has been destroyed, the Church says: “I shall confess to you.”

**VERSE 3.—From the springs of the Savior.** Hence: “Bless the Lord from the springs of Israel,” etc., up to the point that the prophecy may agree with the Gospel.

## CHAPTER XIII

**VERSE 1.—The burden of Babylon.** (HIER.) Babylon, the metropolis of the Chaldeans, etc., up to the one who says: “I shall give you all these things, if you fall down and worship me.”

**VERSE 7.—They shall be dissolved, etc.** Because no work worthy of God’s justice will be found.

**VERSE 8.—They shall be burned.** As though they were coals from excessive anguish, or literally. For many were burned. “Burned with fire”: with the fire that they kindled for themselves, because they cannot say: “The light of your countenance has been marked upon us, O Lord” (Psalm 4), and: “But we, contemplating the glory of the Lord with unveiled face” (2 Corinthians 3).

**VERSE 10.—The sun has been darkened.** These things may be referred to the day of judgment, when all the heavenly lights will appear darkened in comparison with the splendor of Christ.

**VERSE 11.—And I shall visit the evils of the world.** I shall punish in order to correct, etc., up to the words: “But my mercy shall not be taken away from them.”

**And to make rest.** As though he said: “I shall do this so that the proud may be humbled.”

**VERSE 12.—A man shall be more precious than gold, etc.** (ID.) Everything rare is precious: that is, a man of Babylon will be found more rarely than gold. Similarly, the word of the Lord is called precious because it was rarely found. On the day of judgment also, the Lord will visit the evils of the world, bring the arrogance of the demons to rest, and few will be found among the elect because of the persecution of Antichrist.

**VERSE 13.—I shall disturb heaven, etc.** Not because these things are animate, but because of the Lord’s indignation: he looks upon the earth and makes it tremble. Perhaps, when the captivity was imminent, heaven was moved with thunder and the earth by shaking. This may be read of the day of judgment.

**VERSE 14.—A fleeing doe.** The doe is the devil or wicked doctrine; its teachers are signified by the doe, which in Greek is called *dorkas* (δορκάς).

**VERSE 17.—Behold, I shall raise up, etc.** We read in Genesis 10 that Madai, the son of Noah, was the ancestor of the Medes; his name is interpreted as “measure,” or “from the powerful” or “strong one.” Therefore, against the Babylonians, who are confused in mind, powers are raised up by the powerful and strong God for punishment, to repay each according to his works.

**VERSE 19.—And that Babylon shall be, that city, etc.** (ID.) It was not rebuilt afterward, etc., up to the point that they are to be devoured by wolves and dogs.

**VERSE 21.—Beasts, etc.** Through all these beasts that shun the light, we understand the powers of demons or angels, to whom they are handed over for punishment.

**Ostriches.** These have been sufficiently discussed in Job; they do not rise high above the earth, although they appear to have wings.

**Hairy creatures.** Wild, shaggy men, who are also called incubi, satyrs, or kinds of demons.

[Col. 1253A] **VERSE 22.—Owls in the houses.** The size of crows, but sprinkled with spots; with their beaks placed in the marsh, they screech horribly.

**Sirens.** They are crested and winged serpents, or, like certain other sea creatures, have the appearance of women; or they are portents of the devil, who deceive human beings with sweet song—those who pass through the shipwreck of this age without stopping their ears.

## CHAPTER XIV
